title: Stock Picks: AMMB And Orkim
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified AMMB Holdings Bhd and Orkim Bhd as stocks displaying bullish technical momentum, following recent breakouts on strong trading volumes. AMMB Holdings may see its upward trajectory extended after breaching the RM6.60 resistance level with high volume, validating a bullish continuation pattern. RHB Research said sustaining prices above this breakout point could pave the way towards the next resistance at RM6.90, followed by RM7.15. However, a decline below the RM6.35 support level would invalidate the bullish setup and signal a potential pullback. Meanwhile, Orkim has extended its rally with a decisive breakout above its resistance level, supported by elevated trading activity. The stock’s close above RM1.06 confirms that bullish momentum remains intact, positioning it to test the next resistance at RM1.12 and subsequently RM1.17, according to the research house. On the downside, a move below the RM1.01 support level would negate the positive outlook and could trigger a correction. RHB Research’s technical view suggests both counters are trading within favourable momentum trends, although key support levels will need to hold to sustain the bullish bias. Related

title: Tech Rally Lifts Wall Street To Two-Week High
body:
Wall Street closed higher on Wednesday, with technology shares leading a rebound that pushed major indices to two-week highs as investors refocused on the long-term promise of artificial intelligence rather than its disruption risks. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 288.40 points, or 1.26%, to 23,152.08, marking the strongest percentage gain among the three major indices. The S&P 500 advanced 56.06 points, or 0.81%, to 6,946.13, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 307.65 points, or 0.63%, to 49,482.15. Chipmakers and software counters spearheaded gains. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index climbed 1.6% ahead of Nvidia’s earnings, while the S&P Software & Services index rebounded 2.9%, trimming part of its 23% year-to-date decline. Nvidia, at the forefront of the AI revolution, reported fourth-quarter revenue of $68.13 billion, beating analyst estimates. Its shares were up about 3% in extended trading. “We’re in the middle of a push-pull here between some negative sentiment and some extreme price action in parts of the market,” said Zach Hill, head of portfolio management at Horizon Investments in Charlotte, North Carolina. “I think the (AI) disruption concerns are more acute right now than worries over return on investment,” Hill added. “Investors are trying to grapple with what could potentially be existential risk, and that’s a bigger deal than not receiving as much payout as you would like.” Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said it is not clear that the AI rollout will displace workers, adding that the technology could enable workers and improve labour market efficiency. Gains were broad, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by 1.78-to-1 on the NYSE and 2.02-to-1 on the Nasdaq. However, pockets of weakness remained. Axon Enterprise surged 17.6% after beating quarterly profit estimates. In contrast, First Solar slid 13.6% and Lowe’s Companies fell 5.6% after issuing weaker-than-expected annual sales guidance, dragging housing and homebuilder stocks lower despite mortgage rates hitting a three-and-a-half-year low last week. Consumer staples also lagged. Brown-Forman dropped 7.6% and Molson Coors declined 4.8% after Diageo projected a 2% to 3% organic sales decline in 2026 and halved its interim dividend. GoDaddy tumbled 14.3% after forecasting annual revenue below expectations. Total trading volume reached 17.50 billion shares, below the 20-day average of 20.27 billion. Reuters Related

title: Stock Picks: MPI And Malaysia Smelting Corp
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd (MPI) and Malaysia Smelting Corp Bhd as technical breakout candidates, citing strong volume and bullish chart patterns. MPI’s bullish trajectory may be extended after the counter pushed past its resistance on strong trading volume. The research house noted that the stock formed a bullish candlestick and closed above the RM31.50 resistance, confirming that a positive setup is in play. Following the breakout, the stock is expected to climb towards the next resistance at RM33.50, followed by RM35.50. However, RHB Research cautioned that a drop below the RM29.50 support level would negate the bullish view. Meanwhile, Malaysia Smelting Corp continued its rally with a strong breakout above its resistance level, supported by elevated trading volume. The close above the RM1.85 resistance signals sustained bullish momentum, positioning the stock to test the next resistance at RM2 and subsequently RM2.10. On the downside, a fall below the RM1.75 support level could invalidate the bullish setup and open the door to a potential correction, according to the research house. Related

title: Singapore Stocks Kick Off On A High Note, STI Rises 0.3%
body:
The Straits Times Index (STI) opened higher on Thursday, climbing 14.95 points, or 0.3%, to 5,022.68 in early trading. Market breadth was positive, with 113 advancing stocks against 73 decliners. Total trading volume on the Singapore Exchange (SGX) reached 144.83 million shares worth S$228.09 million as of 9.05 am. Notable gainers included UMS, up 2.19% to S$1.40, while key banking counters were steady with DBS at S$57.73, UOB at S$37.14, and OCBC Bank at S$21.56. Seatrium Ltd rose to S$2.30, and YZJ Shipbuilding advanced to S$3.90. Singtel was trading at S$5.12. Among broader indices, the iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index stood at 1,526.59, the iEdge S-REIT Index at 1,112.48, and the iEdge-OCBC Singapore Low Carbon Select 40 Capped Index at 3,731.72. Regional and thematic indices, including the iEdge APAC Financials Dividend Plus Index and iEdge Southeast Asia+ TECH Index, also showed early gains. SGX derivatives saw a total volume of 16,380 contracts, with futures such as the MSCI Singapore Index Futures at 461.00 and FTSE China A50 Index Futures at 14,817.00 reflecting moderate early activity. Early market activity suggests a positive start for Singapore equities, supported by steady buying across major sectors and continued interest in banking and industrial stocks. Related

title: Ringgit Opens Firmer On Positive Outlook, Gains On Softer US Dollar
body:
The ringgit opened firmer against the US dollar on Thursday, underpinned by Malaysia’s positive economic outlook and a softer greenback. At 8 am, the local currency strengthened to 3.8850/8960 against the dollar from Wednesday’s close of 3.8900/8955. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the government is reviewing this year’s gross domestic product growth forecast, currently projected at 4.0 to 4.5 per cent. “Given last year’s performance, the revision is likely to be upward. That in itself signals a positive outlook,” he told Bernama . He added that monetary policy should remain supportive, with the central bank widely expected to keep interest rates unchanged. Meanwhile, the US dollar index slipped 0.17 per cent to 97.675, reflecting continued softness in the greenback. Mohd Afzanizam noted that the dollar-ringgit pair had hovered near its immediate support level of RM3.8722 on Wednesday before trading around RM3.8855 in the afternoon session. “The ringgit is likely to remain well supported in the near term, given the softer US dollar outlook and Malaysia’s positive economic prospects,” he said. At the open, however, the ringgit traded lower against a basket of major currencies. It eased against the Japanese yen to 2.4878/4950 from 2.4848/4885 at Wednesday’s close, slipped versus the British pound to 5.2669/2818 from 5.2585/2659 and fell against the euro to 4.5901/6031 from 4.5855/5920. The ringgit was mixed against its ASEAN peers. It rose against the Thai baht to 12.4988/5418 from 12.5121/5374, strengthened against the Indonesian rupiah to 231.2/232.0 from 231.5/231.9 and edged up versus the Philippine peso to 6.75/6.78 from 6.76/6.78. However, it slipped against the Singapore dollar to 3.0760/0850 from 3.0736/0782. Bernama Related

title: HSIF Rebounds Off 50-Day SMA, RHB Keeps Bullish Bias
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintained its positive trading bias on Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the contract rebounded strongly from its 50-day simple moving average (SMA), signalling renewed upward momentum. The HSIF advanced 199 pts to settle at 26,758 pts, after opening at 26,566 pts and sliding to an intraday low of 25,525 pts. Strong buying interest subsequently emerged, pushing the index to a high of 26,843 pts before it closed at 26,758 pts, forming a bullish candlestick. During the evening session, it gained a further 189 pts, closing at 26,947 pts. RHB Research said the latest price action confirms that firm support has developed near the 50-day SMA line. A decisive close above the 20-day SMA would signal a resumption of the upward trajectory, while continued trading above the 50-day SMA raises the likelihood of a bullish crossover at the 20-day SMA. The relative strength index is trending higher, indicating that bullish momentum is picking up pace. With buyers now holding the technical advantage, the research house advised traders to hold long positions initiated at 21,416 pts, or at the close on Apr 14 2025. To manage trading risks, the stop-loss level has been raised to 26,400 pts. Immediate support is pegged at 26,400 pts, followed by 25,500 pts, while resistance levels are seen at 27,500 pts and 28,600 pts. Related

title: Hang Seng Opens Higher After Economic Forecast Report
body:
The Hang Seng Index gained 254.02 points, or 0.95 percent, to open at 27,019.74 points on Thursday.B Yesterday, Paul Chan financial secretary, gave an economic forecast of 2.5 percent to 3.5 percent in 2026 in a special address post CNY holiday. In his note, the Chief said the Chinese mainland will be a key driver of regional and global economic momentum, providing firm support for Hong Kong while delivering the 2026-27 budget. He expects Hong Kong’s exports of goods to sustain decent growth and domestic demand to grow steadily this year. Improvements in business sentiment, coupled with expectations of interest rate cuts, will boost asset markets and investments, Chan added. Related

title: Decliners Dominate Bursa As Dutch Lady, Maybank And TM Lead Losses
body:
The stock market closed with broad-based weakness on Feb 26 as decliners outnumbered gainers 746 to 367, signalling cautious sentiment in the market. Meanwhile, some 520 counters were unchanged, while 1,136 counters were untraded and 165 suspended. Leading the losses, Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd slid 88 sen to RM32.20, followed by Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), down 36 sen to RM12. Telecom giant Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) eased 29 sen to RM7.46, while Amway (M) Holdings Bhd and Hong Leong Bank Bhd fell 26 sen and 20 sen to RM5.11 and RM23.84 respectively. On the upside, Sunway Construction Group Bhd led gainers, adding 35 sen to RM7.25, followed by Petronas Dagangan Bhd up 32 sen to RM22.28 and Nestlé (M) Berhad rising 30 sen to RM110.80. The market reflected cautious trading as investors weighed corporate results and broader economic signals, keeping overall activity selective and focused on blue-chip movers. Related

title: Bursa Retreats Slightly At Midday, FBM KLCI Dips 0.27%
body:
Bursa Malaysia slipped in early trading, with the FBM KLCI down 4.66 points or 0.27% to 1,743.15 as of 12.30 pm. The broader market followed suit, with the FBM70 easing 41.85 points (-0.24%) to 17,727.23, the F4GBM down 2.77 points (-0.27%) to 1,030.84, and the FBMEMAS retreating 36.73 points (-0.29%) to 12,786.87. The FBMSHA index recorded the largest fall among major benchmarks, slipping 49.10 points or 0.40% to 12,295.67. Trading was led by AQUAWALK, which fell six sen to 30 sen on heavy volume of 38.2 million shares. Other actively traded stocks included TANCO, which gained one sen to RM1.54 with 34.3 million shares, NATGATE declining 7.5 sen to 93.5 sen (32.9 million shares), ASTRO rising half a sen to 8 sen (32.5 million shares), and CAPITALA down 1.5 sen to 59 sen on 31.9 million shares. Among the top gainers, SUNCON surged 35 sen to RM7.25 with 4.97 million shares, PETDAG added 32 sen to RM22.28, KGB rose 23 sen to RM5.35, MPI increased 22 sen to RM32.22, and SUNWAY climbed 15 sen to RM5.99. Conversely, major decliners included NESTLE down RM1.50 to RM109.00, DLADY off 68 sen to RM32.40, TM lower by 37 sen to RM7.38, AMWAY shedding 26 sen to RM5.11, and HL BANK retreating 18 sen to RM23.86. Market sentiment remained cautious as investors digested mixed corporate earnings and moderate regional cues, with active trading concentrated in mid-cap and small-cap counters. Related

title: Bursa Mirrors Cautious Mood, Heavyweights Drag And Mid-Caps Inch Up
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened on a cautious note, with key indices slipping in early trading as investors weighed local developments alongside Wall Street’s tech-led rebound. The benchmark FBM KLCI fell 5.08 points, or 0.29%, to 1,742.73, while the broader FBM70 edged down 2.67 points, or 0.02%, to 17,766.41. Other key indices also posted losses, with F4GBM retreating 2.76 points, or 0.27%, to 1,030.85, FBMEMAS down 29.35 points, or 0.23%, at 12,794.25, and FBMSHA easing 21.81 points, or 0.18%, to 12,322.96. Early market activity was dominated by CapitalA, which led trading with 18.87 million shares, followed by G3 at 15.02 million and Natgate at 14.98 million. Among gainers, Nestle rose 0.40 points to RM110.90, KGB added 0.33 points to RM5.45, and SunCon climbed 0.29 points to RM7.19. On the downside, DLADY led the losers, falling 0.98 points to RM32.10, followed by PETGAS down 0.32 points to RM18.16 and TM retreating 0.20 points to RM7.55. The mixed start in Kuala Lumpur came as investors monitored global cues, with Wall Street rebounding on Wednesday. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 288.40 points, or 1.26%, to 23,152.08, while the S&P 500 gained 56.06 points, or 0.81%, to 6,946.13 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 307.65 points, or 0.63%, as technology shares led a broad rally. Gains in chipmakers and software counters, including Nvidia’s better-than-expected fourth-quarter results, bolstered sentiment overseas, though selective weakness remained in consumer staples and homebuilder stocks. Market watchers said early trading in Malaysia reflected a cautious approach, with selective mid-cap gains tempered by declines in large-cap and sectoral indices, while trading volumes remained moderate in the morning session. title: Bursa Ends Lower As Profit-Taking Weighs On Banks, KLCI Slips 0.39%
body:
Bursa Malaysia closed in the red on Feb 26, though the benchmark rebounded from its intraday low as profit-taking, particularly in financial heavyweights, capped gains. The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI fell 6.87 points, or 0.39%, to 1,740.94 at 5pm, compared to the closing of 1,747.81 on Feb 25. Banking stocks led the decline, with Malayan Banking Bhd sliding 36 sen to RM12, while CIMB Group Holdings Bhd edged down one sen to RM8.46. Public Bank Bhd bucked the trend, rising five sen to RM5. Tenaga Nasional Bhd was flat at RM14.18 and IHH Healthcare Bhd gained two sen to RM9.02. Among active counters, Aquawalk Group Bhd dropped 7.5 sen to 28.5 sen, Zetrix AI Bhd eased half-a-sen to 80 sen, Nationgate Holdings Bhd slid 11.5 sen to 89.5 sen and Capital A Bhd slipped 1.5 sen to 59 sen, while Tanco Holdings Bhd held steady at RM1.53. Broader market sentiment was negative, with the FBM Emas Index losing 55 points to 12,768.60, the FBMT 100 Index down 49.86 points to 12,594.31, and the FBM ACE Index retreating 37.40 points to 4,764.55. title: Bullish On TSH After Positive Financial Move
body:
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has upgraded TSH Resources Bhd to BUY from Hold, with a higher target price of RM1.40, citing a 14.8% capital upside and a 4.1% dividend yield. The research house noted that FY25 core earnings of RM195.2 million (+27.5% YoY) came in line with expectations, accounting for 100–103% of consensus estimates. The upgrade reflects the company’s strengthened financial position, consistent earnings and a 7.2% reduction in share base following the cancellation of 100 million treasury shares. TSH declared a final dividend of 5.0 sen per share (ex-date: 14 Apr 2026) and revised its dividend payout ratio to a minimum of 30% of net earnings, up from the previous 20–30% range. Core earnings for 4Q25 fell 30.4% quarter-on-quarter and 46.1% year-on-year to RM36.5 million, weighed by lower sales volume, softer crude palm oil (CPO) prices and higher production costs. Weaker refining margins from joint ventures also contributed to the quarterly decline. Despite the softer fourth-quarter performance, FY25 results were buoyed by higher realised palm product prices, increased CPO sales volume, lower production costs and controlled corporate expenses. Exceptional items for the year included fair value losses on derivatives (RM0.3 million), impairments (RM1.9 million), write-offs and write-downs (RM5.3 million), adjustments on biological assets (RM1.4 million), forest planting (RM1.7 million) and unrealised foreign exchange losses (RM2.7 million). TSH Resources’ financial moves, including the treasury share cancellation and revised dividend policy, underpin HLIB’s bullish stance. The target price of RM1.40 is based on 10.5 times the revised FY26 core EPS of 13.3 sen, offering investors both yield and capital growth potential amid a stable outlook for the plantation sector. As of 3.06 pm, the stock price was noted at RM1.22. Related

title: Analyst Project 14% CAGR For Inta Bina
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained a BUY rating on Inta Bina Bhd with a target price of RM0.72, offering a 67% upside and a projected FY26F yield of 5%. RHB Research highlighted that FY25 core profit of RM38.6 million (+19% YoY) came broadly in line with expectations at 102% of RHB’s projection, though it fell slightly short of the Street consensus at 97%. The analyst remains optimistic on the company’s outlook, projecting a three-year earnings compound annual growth rate of 14%, underpinned by a sustainable annual orderbook replenishment of at least RM800 million and ongoing property development projects. INTA’s construction division posted a revenue decline of 11% YoY in 4Q25, yet its PAT rose 3% YoY, resulting in a 4Q25 margin of 5.8% versus 5% a year ago. Its property arm, driven by the Senuri Residence project with a gross development value of RM205 million, saw PAT triple to RM2.5 million from RM0.7 million in 4Q24, lifting its margin to 13.7% from 4.6%. The group held an outstanding orderbook of RM1.7 billion as of end-September 2025, representing 2.6 times FY25 construction revenue, alongside a tenderbook exceeding RM4.9 billion as of 25 February. New job wins for FY25 stood at approximately RM865 million, with a projected replenishment of RM1 billion for FY26. RHB Research’s target price reflects a sum-of-parts valuation pegged to FY26F earnings per share with an 11 times P/E multiple, including a 2% ESG premium based on a 3.1 ESG score. The stock currently trades at 5.9 times FY26F P/E, below the five-year mean of the Bursa Malaysia Construction Index at 14 times, a gap the analyst views as unjustified given INTA’s consistent project wins and upcoming property developments valued at around RM500 million. Potential upside catalysts include further job wins in Johor from long-term clients such as Ecoworld and UEM Sunrise, while sluggish job replenishment remains a key downside risk. As of 3.10 pm, the stock price was noted at RM0.425. Related

body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Pavilion REIT Bhd and Frontken Corp Bhd as technical stock picks, citing improving bullish momentum for both counters. RHB Research said Pavilion REIT is poised to extend its upward movement after staging a strong breakout above the RM1.95 resistance level. title: Ringgit Opens Higher On Strong Q4 GDP
body:
Ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Monday, supported by better-than-expected gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 5.7% in the fourth quarter of 2025, signalling continued resilience in the national economy. At 8 am, the local currency traded at 4.0540/0640 against the greenback, up from Friday’s close of 4.0555/0605, as reported by Bernama . Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit showed a mixed performance. It gained against the British pound to 5.4328/4462 from 5.4332/4399, but eased versus the Japanese yen to 2.5728/5793 from 2.5637/5670 and declined against the euro to 4.7120/7236 from 4.7076/7134. Regional currencies saw varied movements. The ringgit rose against the Indonesian rupiah to 240.0/240.7 from 240.1/240.5, and remained largely steady against the Philippine peso at 6.83/6.85 compared with last week’s 6.83/6.84. Meanwhile, it weakened against the Thai baht to 12.9525/9932 from 12.9115/9332 and edged lower versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1502/1585 from 3.1479/1521. Related

title: Markets Jolt As Trump Threatens Tariffs On Europe Over Greenland
body:
Global markets faced renewed volatility on Monday after US President Donald Trump threatened new tariffs on eight European nations, prompting a flight to safe-haven currencies and pushing the euro to a seven-week low in early trading. Trump said he would impose a 10% import tariff from February 1 on goods from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Britain, rising to 25% on June 1 if a deal on Greenland is not reached. Major European Union states condemned the move as economic blackmail, with France signalling potential countermeasures. In early Asia trade, the euro fell 0.2% to around US$1.1572, while sterling also dipped. The yen strengthened against the dollar as investors sought stability amid heightened geopolitical risk. “Hopes that the tariff situation has calmed down for this year have been dashed for now – and we find ourselves in the same situation as last spring,” said Holger Schmieding, chief economist at Berenberg. Trump’s earlier “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025 had similarly rattled markets, though investors largely viewed those threats as temporary, with global economic growth remaining resilient in the second half of the year. The greenback showed mixed performance, retaining its safe-haven appeal but under pressure from rising concerns about US policy credibility. Bitcoin, often seen as a risk proxy, was steady at US$95,330. Countries most exposed to the tariffs, including the UK and Germany, could see GDP reductions of 0.1% under a 10% tariff and 0.2–0.3% if tariffs rise to 25%, according to Capital Economics. European stocks remain strong, with Germany’s DAX and London’s FTSE both up over 3% so far this month, outpacing the S&P 500’s 1.3% gain. Defence stocks have surged nearly 15% as geopolitical tensions escalate, while Denmark’s crown remains under scrutiny amid the uncertainty. “The US-EU trade war is back on,” said Tina Fordham, geopolitical strategist and founder of Fordham Global Foresight. The move coincides with other global flashpoints, including unrest in Iran and renewed questions over Federal Reserve independence. Gold remained near record highs as investors sought security amid rising geopolitical risks. Economists warn that escalating US-Europe tensions could weigh on the dollar and US tech valuations if capital flows shift abroad. Reuters Related

title: HSIF Weakens Below 27,000, RHB Remains Positive
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), despite the contract extending its corrective phase at the end of last week as upside momentum cooled. The research house noted that HSIF retreated by 104 points last Friday to settle at 26,829 points. The index opened at 26,956 points, hit an intraday high of 26,262 points and later eased to a low of 26,762 points before closing slightly higher. During the evening session, HSIF declined a further 189 points to last trade at 26,640 points. RHB Research said the session formed a long upper shadow, indicating continued selling pressure near the 27,400-point resistance level. Price action is now gravitating towards the 20-day simple moving average, which serves as the immediate trend gauge. “A sustained close below the short-term moving average could attract additional downside pressure, opening the path towards the 25,600-point support level,” the research house said. However, it added that the earlier bullish crossover remains intact, anchoring the broader bullish structure. As long as HSIF holds above the 25,000-point support level, RHB Research views the current pullback as a consolidation phase within an ongoing uptrend. Against this backdrop, traders are advised to continue holding the long position initiated at 21,416 points, recorded at the close on April 14, 2025. For risk management, the stop-loss level is fixed at 25,000 points. RHB Research identified immediate support at 25,600 points, followed by 25,000 points, while resistance levels are seen at 27,400 points and 28,000 points. Related

title: Gold, Silver Hit Records, And Stocks Fall As Trade Fear Returns
body:
Gold and silver hit record highs on Monday (Jan 19) while most equity markets fell after United States President Donald Trump revived trade war fears by threatening several European nations with tariffs over their opposition to the US buying Greenland. Trump has fanned already-rising geopolitical tensions this month by insisting that Washington would take control of the North Atlantic island, citing national security needs.And on Saturday, after talks failed to resolve “fundamental disagreement” over the Danish autonomous territory, he announced he would hit eight countries with fresh levies over their refusal to submit to his demands. He said he would impose 10 per cent tariffs on Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Finland from Feb 1 – rising to 25 per cent from Jun 1 – if they did not agree to the takeover. The announcement drew an immediate response, with a joint statement from the countries saying: “Tariff threats undermine transatlantic relations and risk a dangerous downward spiral.”The move also threatened a trade deal signed between the US and European Union last year, with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul telling ARD television: “I don’t believe that this agreement is possible in the current situation.”Meanwhile, aides to French President Emmanuel Macron said he would ask the EU to activate a never-before-used “anti-coercion instrument” against Washington if Trump makes good on his threat. This measure allows for curbing imports of goods and services into the EU, a market of 27 countries with a combined population of 450 million. Related

title: Financials And Energy Lead Gains While Construction And Tech Drag

title: Dollar Slips As Trump Tariff Threats Spur Flight To Safe Havens
body:
The dollar weakened on Monday as renewed tariff threats by US President Donald Trump unsettled markets, prompting investors to seek refuge in traditional safe-haven currencies such as the yen and the Swiss franc. The move followed Trump’s weekend comments that he would impose an additional 10% import tariff from Feb 1 on goods from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Britain, unless the United States is allowed to buy Greenland. The announcement revived concerns over escalating trade tensions and their potential impact on global growth. Safe-haven demand lifted the yen and Swiss franc, with the dollar falling 0.33% to 157.59 yen and sliding 0.45% against the franc to 0.7983. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of major currencies, slipped 0.19% to 99.18. In early Asian trade, the immediate reaction saw the euro and sterling sold down to a seven-week low of US$1.1572 and a one-month trough of US$1.3321 respectively. Both currencies later recovered as attention shifted towards the broader implications of the tariff threats for the dollar itself. The euro rose 0.19% to US$1.1619, while the pound gained 0.17% to US$1.3398. Major European Union states criticised the tariff threat on Sunday, with France proposing a range of potential countermeasures in response to what officials described as economic blackmail linked to Greenland. Market participants drew parallels with last April’s “Liberation Day” announcement, when Trump unveiled sweeping global tariffs that triggered a sharp loss of confidence in US assets and led to heavy selling of the dollar. “My working assumption is that an ‘off ramp’ from these threats will soon be found, and that this turns into yet another ‘TACO moment’, or an example of the ‘art of the deal’, depending on how one views these things,” said Michael Brown, senior research strategist at Pepperstone. Elsewhere, the risk-sensitive Australian dollar edged down 0.02% to US$0.6690, with losses cushioned by the softer greenback, while the New Zealand dollar rose 0.16% to US$0.5761. Reuters Related

title: Bursa Malaysia Ends Lower As Broader Market Weakens Despite Flat FBM KLCI
body:
Bursa Malaysia closed lower as selling pressure across mid cap and small cap stocks weighed on overall market sentiment, despite the benchmark FBM KLCI finishing largely unchanged. The FBM KLCI edged down 0.41 points, or 0.02%, to close at 1,712.33 after moving between an intraday high of 1,712.33 and a low of 1,704.64. Blue chip stocks were mixed, helping to limit losses at the headline index level. However, broader market indices saw steeper declines. The FBM 70 slid 162.85 points, or 0.92%, to 17,522.76, while the FBM EMAS Index fell 33.49 points to 12,611.54. The FBM Small Cap Index dropped 62.13 points, or 0.51%, reflecting continued risk off sentiment among retail and short term traders. The FBM 4G Benchmark Index also ended lower, down 2.50 points to 1,015.73. Trading activity was dominated by heavily traded penny and recovery stocks. Smart Asia Chemical Bhd emerged as the most active counter, falling 26 sen to 18.5 sen after swinging between 33 sen and 15.5 sen, with more than 2.39 billion shares changing hands. Capital A Bhd declined four sen to 50.5 sen, while IJM Corp Bhd fell 15 sen to RM2.65 amid persistent selling in construction related counters. Zetrix AI Bhd eased one sen to 80.5 sen, while AirAsia X Bhd slipped two sen to RM1.65. Overall, market sentiment remained cautious as investors rotated away from smaller capitalisation stocks, with defensive buying in select heavyweights helping to cushion losses at the benchmark level. title: Bursa Dips As Profit-Taking Weighs On Key Indexes
body:
Bursa Malaysia’s key indices were slightly lower at midday, reflecting cautious investor sentiment amid profit-taking. The benchmark FBM KLCI slipped 2.36 points, or 0.14%, to 1,710.38 by 12:35 PM. Broader market indexes followed suit, with the FBM70 down 108.30 points, or 0.61%, to 17,577.31, while the FBM Emas Index eased 32.66 points, or 0.26%, to 12,612.37. On the losers’ board, SMRT Holdings was among the heaviest decliners, falling 0.25 to RM0.195, with a trading volume of over 2 billion shares, following an earlier downgrade by HLIB Research. Other notable decliners included United Plantations, which fell 0.68 to RM31.02, and Malaysian Pacific Industries, down 0.38 to RM34.10. Among gainers, Allianz rose 1.06 to RM21.50 on active buying interest, while Hong Leong Financial Group gained 0.60 to RM21.56. HL Bank, HL Insurance and LPI also contributed to the positive momentum, recording moderate gains by midday. The top traded stocks by volume were dominated by SMRT Holdings, CapitalA and AAX, reflecting continued investor focus on high-liquidity counters despite the overall market dip. Market participants cited selective profit-taking and sector rotation as key drivers behind the cautious session, with investors closely watching upcoming corporate earnings and broader economic indicators for further direction. title: Bitcoin Slips 3% Amid Trump’s Tariff Threats
body:
Bitcoin slid about 3% to around US$92,000 in early Asian trading on Monday as investors cut risk following renewed tariff threats from US President Donald Trump, which rattled global markets and spilled into digital assets. The world’s largest cryptocurrency fell to about US$92,506, down 2.6%, as Trump said the US would impose an additional 10% import tariff from Feb 1 on goods from Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Finland and Britain, with the rate set to rise to 25% on June 1 if no agreement is reached. The move was linked to his push for US ownership of Greenland and drew condemnation from European officials, who described the threat as coercive. The risk-off reaction first emerged in derivatives markets as US cash markets were shut for a holiday, thinning liquidity. US stock futures fell sharply in early Asian hours, with S&P 500 futures down 0.7% and Nasdaq futures losing 1.0%. Asian equities followed suit, led by a roughly 1% decline in Japan’s Nikkei, while Europe’s futures also pointed lower amid fresh trade uncertainty. Other major cryptocurrencies moved in tandem, with ether down 3% to around US$3,203 and XRP sliding 4.7% to US$1.96, pulling total crypto market capitalisation down 2.7% to about US$3.21 trillion. The decline accelerated as leveraged positions were unwound, with traders pointing to heavy long liquidations during the sell-off. In broader markets, investors sought safety, pushing gold up 1.5% to a record high, while silver also hit fresh peaks. Oil prices eased as concerns grew over the impact of a potential US-Europe trade conflict on global growth and demand. Strategists warned that beyond tariffs, capital flows could pose a larger risk. Deutsche Bank noted that European investors hold about US$8 trillion in US bonds and equities, cautioning that any shift in those holdings could prove more disruptive than trade measures themselves. title: Weekly Wrap: Seoul Stocks Rally To Record Highs On Tech, Semicon Momentum
body:
South Korea’s Kospi continued its blistering start to 2026 in the week ending Jan 16, hitting fresh record highs as technology and semiconductor heavyweights drove the market higher. The benchmark Kospi closed Jan 16 at a new peak of around 4,840-4,841, extending a winning streak that pushed the index above 4,800 points for the first time and marking the 11th straight session of gains into the week’s end. Investor optimism was anchored by strong demand for chips and tech stocks, with major exporters like Samsung Electronics and SK hynix leading buying interest as global artificial intelligence and memory demand stays robust. Foreign and institutional investors were net buyers throughout the week, underscoring confidence in Korea’s export‑led equity rally. Other sectors also contributed positively, with autos and defence stocks adding breadth on Jan 15’s session, reflecting broadening participation beyond core tech themes. Still, a softer Korean won and ongoing macro uncertainties, including currency volatility and global rate expectations, remain watch points for traders. Nevertheless, the market’s strong uptrend and record close reaffirm Seoul’s status among Asia’s standout bourses early in 2026. Key takeaway: A record‑setting week for the Kospi, powered by semiconductor strength and foreign inflows, sets an upbeat tone for Korean equities, with broader participation hinting at durable momentum. title: Market Snapshot: Bursa Hits Fresh Highs Before Profit-Taking Cools The Rally
body:
Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) kicked off the week strong, riding continued risk appetite and positive sentiment that saw the index climb steadily from 1,695.44 on Jan 12 as investors warmed to heavy-weight buying and external cues. Mid-week trading saw the index breach the 1,700 level, supported by foreign participation and broader market confidence, reflecting sustained demand for Malaysian equities in early 2026. However, by the close on Jan 16, the rally paused as profit-taking emerged, trimming gains and sending the FBM KLCI down 0.14% to 1,712.74 after an intraday fluctuation between 1,708 and 1,721. Analysts described the pullback as a breather after recent strength, not a breakdown in the uptrend, with mid- and small caps showing resilience even as heavyweights cooled. Market breadth was mixed, with the broader FBM EMAS and Shariah indices ending softer, underscoring selective rotation rather than broad-based selling. Looking ahead, brokers remain upbeat: Revised forecasts suggest the FBM KLCI could scale higher this year on stronger earnings growth and foreign fund inflows, with targets nudged toward the 1,800 area. Key takeaway: Fresh highs and healthy participation marked the week, but profit-taking in late trade capped the rally, a sign of consolidation rather than a reversal, as the market recalibrates after early-year gains. title: Wall Street Ends Flat As Earnings Kick Off; Weekly Losses Logged
body:
US stocks slipped in a choppy session on Jan 16 as investors headed into a long weekend, leaving the major indexes with weekly losses despite a solid start to fourth-quarter earnings season. Reuters reported that the Dow dipped 83.11 points, or 0.17%, to 49,359.33, while the S&P 500 edged down 0.06% to 6,940.01 and the Nasdaq also eased 0.06% to 23,515.39. For the week, the S&P 500 shed 0.38%, the Nasdaq fell 0.66% and the Dow lost 0.29%. Healthcare led sector laggards on Jan 16, dropping 0.8%, while semiconductor stocks extended a two-day rally with the Philly Chip Index up 1.2%. Bank shares were mixed: solid earnings from major lenders were overshadowed by pressure from President Donald Trump’s proposal to cap credit card interest rates at 10%. The financial sector eked out a 0.1% gain but still suffered its steepest weekly drop since October. Markets also digested political signals, after Trump indicated economic advisor Kevin Hassett may remain in his current role — cooling speculation he would replace Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. With investors cautious ahead of Jan 19’s Martin Luther King Jr holiday closure, traders cited monthly options expiration as a factor behind choppiness on Jan 16. Flows also rotated out of megacap tech and into undervalued pockets of the market: the Russell 2000 powered to another record close, up 2.04% on the week. Real estate, consumer staples and industrials topped the week’s sector winners. Breadth was weak on both major exchanges, with decliners outpacing gainers on the NYSE and Nasdaq. Turnover was heavy, with 18.77 billion shares traded versus the 20-day average of 16.85 billion. Related

title: Hong Kong Stocks Close Lower As Tech Headwinds Weigh In
body:
The Hong Kong market ended Jan 16’s session under pressure, with the Hang Seng Index slipping 0.29% to finish at 26,844.96, rolling back earlier gains amid mixed sector performance. After an initial upside attempt, profit-taking and weakness in broader tech and heavyweight names pulled the market down. The Hang Seng Tech Index also lagged, dropping about 0.11% as semiconductor and artificial intelligence optimism failed to lift the broader market. Blue-chip stocks told a mixed story. Tencent eased about 0.7%, while Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing held near flat. Mainland-linked financials saw moderate moves, with some banks inching lower and select insurers seeing modest gains. On the upside, select consumer and property plays outperformed, but gains were not enough to counter selling pressure elsewhere. Trading volume remained robust with turnover in the billions of HK dollar, signalling active repositioning ahead of next week’s China macro data. Market sentiment was cautious, with investors digesting recent global tech sector moves and awaiting fresh catalysts from China’s economic releases. Despite the dip, the broader market managed to clinch a weekly rise, extending resilience after recent volatility. Looking ahead, traders will watch for China’s upcoming GDP and policy signals to gauge whether the market can regain traction next week. Related

title: Wall Street Rebounds As Banks And Chips Spark Buying
body:
US stocks rebounded on Thursday after two consecutive sessions of losses, supported by strong earnings from major banks and upbeat signals from the semiconductor sector. Shares of Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley surged after both lenders posted higher quarterly profits, driven by a pickup in dealmaking activity. Goldman climbed 4.6%, providing the biggest lift to the Dow, while Morgan Stanley advanced 5.8%. The rally came despite lingering concerns over the banking sector earlier in the week, when mixed earnings and worries over US President Donald Trump’s proposed one-year cap on credit-card interest rates at 10% weighed on sentiment. Investors appeared to rotate into value and cyclical names. “It’s been growth, tech or bust in this market,” in recent years, said Jake Dollarhide, chief executive officer of Longbow Asset Management in Tulsa, Oklahoma. Today, “it’s the banks and old-school industrials” that are standouts. The S&P 500 industrials index closed at another record high. Technology stocks also moved higher, led by chipmakers, after TSMC, the world’s largest producer of advanced artificial intelligence chips, forecast robust annual growth and flagged plans to expand US manufacturing capacity. title: Singapore Shares Open Firmer As STI Edges Higher
body:
Singapore stocks opened modestly higher on Friday, supported by early gains among index heavyweights as market breadth stayed positive. As at 9.04 am, the Straits Times Index rose 4.16 points or 0.09% to 4,837.50. Advancers outnumbered decliners 105 to 63, with trading volume at 74.31 million shares valued at S$129.27 million. Banking stocks were mixed in early trade. DBS Group climbed 0.23 points or 0.39% to S$59.12, while OCBC Bank traded at S$20.43 and UOB stood at S$36.42. Singtel was seen at S$4.49, ST Engineering at S$9.52 and Seatrium at S$2.24. Across broader indices, the iEdge Singapore Next 50 Index stood at 1,493.02, while the iEdge S-REIT Index was at 1,132.54. The iEdge-OCBC Singapore Low Carbon Select 40 Capped Index was at 3,683.01 and the iEdge APAC Financials Dividend Plus Index was at 3,631.73. In the derivatives market, trading volume totalled 11.71 thousand contracts. SGX FTSE Taiwan Index Futures were quoted at 2,519.25, while Nikkei 225 Index Futures stood at 53,820. MSCI Singapore Index Futures were at 456.60. Currency futures showed USD/SGD Futures at 1.2872, while USD/CNH Futures were quoted at 6.9432, reflecting steady conditions in early Asian trade. Related

title: Ringgit Edges Higher Ahead Of Advance 4Q GDP Data
body:
The ringgit rebounded to open slightly firmer against the US dollar on Friday, ahead of the release of Malaysia’s advance fourth quarter 2025 gross domestic product estimates later today. At 8 am, the local currency traded at 4.0515/0600 versus the US dollar, marginally stronger than Thursday’s close of 4.0535/0595. According to Bernama , the ringgit had closed 0.17% lower against the greenback on Thursday as the US dollar strengthened following better-than-expected Initial Jobless Claims data, which tempered near-term expectations for interest rate cuts. The US Dollar Index rose 0.32% to 99.371 points after jobless claims fell to 198,000 last week, compared with consensus estimates of 215,000. Meanwhile, the two-year and 10-year US Treasury yields rose by 3.7 and 5.6 basis points to 3.57% and 4.17% respectively. At the opening, the ringgit strengthened against major currencies. It appreciated versus the Japanese yen to 2.5547/5604 from 2.5594/5633, gained against the euro to 4.7034/7133 from 4.7167/7236 and rose versus the British pound to 5.4213/4327 from 5.4467/4548. Against regional peers, the ringgit was mixed. It edged higher against the Singapore dollar to 3.1456/1524 from 3.1491/1540 and strengthened versus the Thai baht to 12.8967/9341 from 12.9096/9349. It was flat against the Philippine peso at 6.81/6.83 and little changed against the Indonesian rupiah at 239.7/240.4 from 239.9/240.3 previously. Related

title: Plantation Slump Leads Bursa Decliners
body:
Plantation heavyweights dragged Bursa Malaysia lower on Jan 16 as profit-taking hit commodity-linked names, overshadowing gains in select industrial and technology stocks. United Plantations Bhd led the losers, tumbling RM1.28 to RM31.70, followed by Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, which slipped 54 sen to RM20, while Ayer Holdings Bhd fell 39 sen to RM7. Malayan Cement Bhd and Westports Holdings Bhd also weakened, shedding 23 sen each to RM7.60 and RM5.89 respectively. On the flip side, tech and industrial counters supported sentiment. Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd topped the gainers, rising 78 sen to RM34.48, while Batu Kawan Bhd added 26 sen to RM20.28. Southern Cable Group Bhd extended its upward momentum with a 20 sen climb to RM2.44, outperforming on strong volume, while LPI Capital Bhd and Hong Leong Capital Bhd gained 18 sen to RM15.14 and 14 sen to RM3.53 respectively. Market breadth reflected the selling bias, with 564 decliners outpacing 482 advancers, while 589 counters were unchanged, 1,021 untraded and 22 suspended, signalling a cautious end to the week. title: Malaysia Gold Prices Dip Amid Stronger US Data
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia fell slightly on Friday as stronger-than-expected economic data from the United States boosted the dollar and reduced expectations for near-term Federal Reserve rate cuts. Spot gold in Malaysian Ringgit dropped 0.19% to RM601.02 per gram, or RM18,693.81 per ounce, according to goldprice.org . Despite the daily decline, gold remains on track for a weekly gain of around 2% after reaching a record high of RM18,925 per ounce earlier this week. Silver also slipped, down 1.22% to RM370.11 per ounce. Analysts attributed the retreat to a combination of factors, including easing geopolitical tensions and a stronger US dollar. “The downward move in gold began predominantly when there was some lowering of the odds of US intervention in Iran,” said Kyle Rodda, analyst at Capital.com. He added, “US economic data shows there is not an urgency to cut interest rates.” The US Labor Department reported that weekly initial jobless claims fell to 198,000, below economists’ expectations of 215,000, according to Reuters . A firmer dollar typically makes gold and other non-yielding assets more expensive for international buyers. Despite the pullback, demand for gold remains resilient in the region. The SPDR Gold Trust, the world’s largest gold-backed exchange-traded fund, saw its holdings rise slightly to 1,074.80 tonnes, the highest in over three years. Meanwhile, gold buying in India remained muted as prices hit record highs, while Chinese demand stayed steady ahead of the Lunar New Year. Over the past year, gold in Malaysia has surged by 53.76%, highlighting its continued appeal as a store of value amid global economic uncertainty. Related

title: Kerjaya Prospek Kicks Off FY26 On Solid Footing, Prompting A TP Revision
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) have maintained a BUY call on Kerjaya Prospek Bhd with a revised target price of RM3.35, indicating a 21% upside, citing a strong start to 2026. The research house reported that the company’s first contract win of the year, a RM201 million project from Greencove, a subsidiary of Kerjaya Prospek Property, reinforces its steady project pipeline and growth prospects. The project involves the main building works of two 39-storey blocks in Damansara Damai, Sungai Buloh, scheduled to commence on April 1 and expected to be completed within 40 months. The contract accounts for around 10% of RHB Research’s internal job replenishment estimate of RM2 billion for Kerjaya Prospek. The company’s outstanding orderbook now stands at RM4.4 billion, translating to an orderbook-to-revenue cover ratio of 2.5 times, with an estimated net profit margin of about 10% for this project. Kerjaya Prospek’s active tenderbook is currently valued at approximately RM2 billion, with over half stemming from related-party transactions, including KPPROP and Eastern & Oriental (Buy, TP: RM1.17), alongside other residential and industrial projects. RHB Research noted potential opportunities in ongoing land reclamation projects, including Andaman Island, which could yield contracts worth RM300–500 million. The group also owns about 89 acres of land, mainly in Penang, with an estimated gross development value of RM3 billion. Ongoing property projects such as The Vue@Monterez and Papyrus@North Kiara have take-up rates of 99% and 82% respectively as of November 2025 and new launches in Jalan Puchong, Selangor and Tanjung Bungah, Penang, are expected in FY26. RHB Research highlighted that industrial property development could further bolster revenue streams. Downside risks include potential property market slowdowns and prolonged cost pressures. As of 11.20 am, the stock price is up 1.81% to RM2.82. Related

title: Dollar Poised For Third Weekly Gain As US Jobs Data Ease Rate-Cut Bets
body:
The US dollar was set for a third consecutive weekly gain on Friday after better-than-expected employment data reduced expectations for an imminent rate cut by the Federal Reserve. The greenback rose overnight following a surprise drop in weekly jobless claims and remained steady in Asian morning trade, while the Japanese yen hovered near levels that could prompt intervention by Tokyo to defend its currency. Kyle Rodda, an analyst at Capital.com, said, “The US dollar is looking firmer to start the year. Weekly US jobless claims data, along with some manufacturing surveys, were better than expected, lowering the implied probabilities of imminent Fed rate cuts.” Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell by 9,000 to a seasonally adjusted 198,000 for the week ended January 10, the Labor Department reported on Thursday, compared with economists’ expectations of 215,000. Fed funds futures have pushed back expectations for the next rate cut to June as central bank policymakers weigh strong employment figures and remain concerned about inflation. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Thursday that amid ample evidence of stability in the job market, the central bank should focus on getting inflation down. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid described inflation as “too hot”, while San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said that incoming economic data looks promising. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies, was little changed at 99.36 and is on course for a 0.2 per cent gain this week. The euro held steady at US$1.1607. The yen strengthened slightly by 0.05 per cent to 158.58 per dollar but is poised to fall roughly 0.5 per cent for the week. Expectations that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi may pursue more fiscally expansionist policies ahead of a snap election next month have weighed on the yen. Policymakers have warned they stand ready to act against one-way movements in the foreign exchange market, giving the currency occasional support. Economists also expect the Bank of Japan to delay any rate hikes until July. Elsewhere in the region, the Australian dollar was little changed at US$0.6699, while New Zealand’s kiwi gained 0.05 per cent to US$0.5745. Philip Lane, chief economist at the European Central Bank, said the ECB would not consider any rate changes in the near term if the economy remains on track, though new shocks, such as deviations from the Fed’s mandate, could alter the outlook. The ECB has held rates steady since ending a rapid cut cycle in June and signalled last month that it is in no hurry to adjust policy again. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin rose 0.2 per cent to US$95,760.92 and ether gained 0.8 per cent to US$3,323.82. Reuters Related

title: Crypto Markets Hold Firm As Bitcoin Eyes US$100K, Ethereum Steadies
body:
Bitcoin and Ethereum extended a steady start to the year as institutional flows, easing macro concerns and balanced sentiment kept crypto markets on solid footing. Bitcoin traded in the US$95,000-US$97,000 range, supported by short-covering and renewed ETF inflows. The outlook remains bullish as traders watch for a potential break toward the US$100,000 psychological barrier, though derivatives markets suggest a moderate probability of achieving that milestone in the near term. Ethereum, meanwhile, consolidated above US$3,300, reflecting range-bound sentiment as investors weighed short-term profit-taking against strong fundamentals. Staking on the Ethereum network has hit new highs, underscoring long-term confidence, while strategic withdrawals from major exchanges suggest supply tightness could build over time. Broader sentiment across digital assets stayed neutral to cautiously optimistic, with institutional allocators remaining active even as regulatory debates in the US inject some uncertainty into near-term adoption timelines. Bottom line: Bitcoin’s momentum remains intact, supported by institutional capital and macro-optimism, while Ethereum’s consolidation signals stability with network fundamentals offering longer-term upside and regulatory clarity along with macro data remain key variables heading into the rest of the first quarter. Related

title: China’s STAR Composite Index Closed Higher On H200 AI Chips Prospect
body:
The STAR Composite Index, which reflects the performance of stocks on China’s sci-tech innovation board, closed 1.63 percent higher at 1,855.03 points on Friday. The STAR 50 Index, which tracks the 50 largest stocks listed on the board that also meet certain liquidity requirements, closed 1.35 percent higher at 1,514.07 points. This comes after US administration approved the export of Nvidia’s H200 AI chips to China, reversing years of tight US restrictions on advanced AI hardware. The Nvidia H200 chips represent the company’s second-most-powerful chip series and were previously barred from sale due to national security concerns. The sci-tech innovation board, commonly known as the STAR Market, was inaugurated in June 2019 at Shanghai Stock Exchange. It is designed to support companies in the high-tech and strategic emerging sectors. Related

title: Hong Kong Shares End Higher As Tech, China Plays Lift Mood

The Hang Seng Tech Index rose nearly 1.9%, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index also climbed, as optimism over supportive economic signals from Beijing lifted sentiment. Blue-chip insurers and infrastructure names outperformed, while broader market turnover topped HK$2.4 billion, reflecting renewed inflows following recent weakness. Despite the strong finish, the market posted a weekly decline, snapping a short rally amid mixed macro cues, including caution ahead of China’s key economic data. Related

title: Wall Street Splits, Dow Climbs To New Peak As Nasdaq Slips
body:
Wall Street ended mostly higher on Thursday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the Russell 2000 notching fresh record highs even as the Nasdaq closed lower, weighed by losses in major technology counters. The market’s performance unfolded against the backdrop of a sharp jump in US jobless claims, a reading that revived concerns over labour market weakness and sent both the US dollar and Treasury yields lower. Technology shares dragged the Nasdaq, with the information communications sector down 1% and tech falling 0.6%. Oracle plunged as much as 16% at one point, marking its worst session since 2001, though it later trimmed losses. Materials and financials, meanwhile, rose around 2%, supporting broader sentiment. The Dow and Russell 2000 outperformed as investors rotated into industrials and small-caps, while Mexico’s benchmark index also set a new record. The dollar index slid to a two-month low, with the greenback hitting a 14-month low against the Chinese yuan at 7.0550. The Brazilian real strengthened 1%. Bitcoin briefly dipped below US$90,000 before recovering. On the bond front, US Treasury yields fell by about 5 basis points at the shorter end, leading to a bull steepening of the yield curve. In commodities, oil fell 1.5%, while silver extended its rally to a new high above US$64 an ounce. The market moves came a day after Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell said the central bank sees stronger productivity as a potential path toward balancing firm economic growth with easing inflation pressures. Investors are now digesting what weaker labour indicators could mean for the Fed’s policy direction in early 2026. Reuters Related

title: Ringgit Opens Firmer On Softer US Data And Fed Rate Cut
body:
The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar for a second consecutive day, supported by softer US economic data and the Federal Reserve’s 25-basis-point rate cut. At 8 am, the local currency rose to 4.1000/1100 against the greenback from Thursday’s close of 4.1040/1105. The ringgit last traded at this level against the US dollar on April 28, 2021, at 4.1000/1050. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index fell 0.44% to 98.348 amid signs of a softening labour market. “The ringgit had traded firmer after the Fed delivered the widely expected 25-basis-point cut to the Fed Funds Rate,” he noted to Bernama. He added, “Today, we expect the ringgit to stay in a tight range and possibly attempt to break the psychological RM4.10 level by the end of the day.” At the open, the ringgit showed mixed performance against other major currencies. It slipped versus the British pound to 5.4911/5045 from Thursday’s 5.4879/4966, weakened against the euro to 4.8138/8256 from 4.8025/8101, and eased against the Japanese yen to 2.6368/6434 from 2.6333/6375. Against regional peers, the ringgit strengthened versus the Indonesian rupiah to 245.8/246.5 from 246.1/246.6, fell against the Singapore dollar to 3.1739/1819 from 3.1711/1763, and eased against the Thai baht to 12.9542/9940 from 12.9219/9505. It remained unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.95/6.97. Bernama Related

title: Markets Remain Bullish Despite Gold Easing To RM564 Per Gram
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia eased slightly on Friday, with the price per kilogram falling RM1,634 to RM564,162, while per gram, the metal was down RM1.64 to RM564.16. The price per ounce also dipped RM50.81 to RM17,547.4. Despite the minor pullback locally, global markets remain on a bullish trajectory. COMEX gold continued its upward movement on Thursday, gaining US$88.30 to close at US$4,313 per ounce, after testing a low of US$4,231.20 earlier in the session. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) noted that the commodity has cleared its consolidation range and is maintaining a constructive technical setup, with resistance levels projected at US$4,400 and US$4,500. Support levels are pegged at US$4,000 and US$3,800. Year-to-date, gold has posted strong gains across major currencies, reflecting a global appetite for safe-haven assets amid ongoing economic uncertainty. Prices have risen 63.1% in US$, 51.3% in Australian dollars, 56.1% in Canadian dollars, and 52.2% in British pounds. In Malaysia, the metal has surged 49.3% over the past year, continuing a long-term upward trend. RHB Research advised traders to maintain long positions in COMEX gold, citing positive momentum and the potential for prices to move into fresh territory if current trends persist. The technical structure suggests that bullish sentiment remains dominant globally, despite minor local fluctuations in the RM-denominated market. Related

title: Lululemon CEO Exit Sends Shares Higher
body:
Lululemon Athletica said CEO Calvin McDonald will step down in January after about seven years leading the company, with no immediate replacement named, while raising its annual profit forecast. The announcement sent shares up roughly 10% in extended trading on Thursday. The company appointed finance chief Meghan Frank and chief commercial officer André Maestrini as co-interim CEOs during the search for a permanent leader. Despite the upbeat forecast, US sales have struggled, with the stock down 61% over the past two years. Lululemon, known for premium leggings and athleisure, has lost ground to rivals such as Alo Yoga and private-label alternatives, with executives acknowledging product execution issues. The Wall Street Journal reported that founder Chip Wilson expressed frustration with marketing and had considered a proxy fight. Lululemon also approved a US$1 billion increase to its stock buyback programme. While the Thanksgiving period showed strong demand, McDonald said holiday shopping has slowed, with consumers trading down in apparel. The company expects higher discounts to clear aged inventory and plans for inventory units to fall below sales in 2026. Interim co-CEO Frank added that marketing investments will continue in the fourth quarter to boost traffic and brand awareness. The company now anticipates annual profit between US$12.92 and US$13.02 per share, up from previous guidance of US$12.77 to US$12.97, while raising its annual sales target. Lululemon expects a US$210 million impact from tariffs on 2025 operating income and an operating margin contraction of about 390 basis points. Analysts note challenges ahead, “Lululemon lost share in a competitive athleisure market and has struggled with its core women’s pants,” said Matt Jacob of M Science, adding that the issue will fall to the next permanent CEO. For the quarter ended Nov 2, Lululemon reported net revenue of US$2.57 billion, exceeding estimates of US$2.48 billion, according to LSEG data. Morningstar analyst David Swartz commented that investors are likely reassured by the board’s decisive action, despite recognising McDonald’s effectiveness as CEO. Reuters Related

title: Hang Seng Index Futures Seen Extending Gains As Momentum Strengthens
body:
The Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) is expected to extend its upward bias as improving sentiment pushes the contract closer to its 20-day simple moving average, according to RHB Investment Bank Bhd. RHB Research said the HSIF added 34 points on Thursday to finish at 25,570, after moving between an intraday low of 25,483 and a high of 25,830. The evening session saw further strength, with the futures contract surging 218 points to last trade at 25,788. The research house noted that the price action, alongside an RSI that is turning higher towards the 50% line, indicates strengthening bullish momentum. It said a break above the short-term moving average could open the path for the HSIF to retest the 26,500 resistance, followed by 27,400. RHB Research said, “If the index crosses above the short-term moving average, it may attempt to retest the 26,500-pt resistance. A breakout above this level would attract further momentum and pave the way for an extension towards 27,400 pts.” On the downside, the immediate support remains at 25,000, with the next support at 24,300. As long as the index holds above the 25,000 mark, the research house said it will keep its positive trading bias. RHB maintains its long position, which was initiated at 21,416 on 14 April, and keeps the stop-loss at 25,000 points. Related

title: Bursa Opens Lower, FBM KLCI Dips On Early Trading
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened slightly lower, with all major indices recording early losses amid cautious investor sentiment. At 9:02 am, the benchmark FBM KLCI (FBMKLCI) fell 2.64 points, or 0.16%, to 1,622.75. Other key indices also opened in the red, with the FBM70 down 21.55 points (-0.13%) to 16,608.95, F4GBM sliding 1.41 points (-0.15%) to 963.12, FBMEMAS easing 17.68 points (-0.15%) to 11,965.98 and FBMSHA retreating 12.20 points (-0.10%) to 11,810.56. In early stock action, small-cap counters led trading activity. TWL was the most active, unchanged at 0.025, with a volume of 154.78 million shares. BMS followed at 0.210 with 64.30 million shares traded, while BORNOIL remained at 0.005 with 33.37 million shares changing hands. VANTNRG rose 0.055 to 0.415 on 24.58 million shares and PSP gained 0.005 to 0.155 with 15.43 million shares traded. Among early gainers, DUFU led the charge, climbing 0.060 to 1.620, followed by VANTNRG (+0.055 to 0.415), ASIAFLE (+0.040 to 1.400), Tenaga (+0.040 to 12.780) and GASMSIA (+0.030 to 4.220). Top losers included Nestle (-1.100 to 113.100), F&N (-0.580 to 34.420), KLK (-0.100 to 19.420), Axiata (-0.050 to 2.600) and RHB Bank (-0.050 to 7.440). The cautious start suggests that investors are weighing global and local cues, including ongoing market volatility and sector-specific developments, before committing to larger positions. Related

title: Bursa Malaysia Extends Morning Rally On Strong Wall Street Lead
body:
Bursa Malaysia pushed higher at midday of Dec 12, buoyed by upbeat regional sentiment and a firm overnight rally on Wall Street. At 12:30pm, the FBM KLCI jumped 10.84 points, or 0.67%, to 1,636.23, rebounding strongly from an early dip after opening 2.83 points lower at 1,622.56. The benchmark moved between 1,622.03 and 1,636.50 through the session. Market breadth was also positive as gainers (558) comfortably outpacing losers (360), while 485 counters were unchanged. Turnover reached 1.69 billion shares worth RM1.06 billion. Heavyweights led the advance with TNB rising 20 sen to RM12.94, IHH Healthcare added 11 sen to RM8.51, Maybank gained eight sen to RM10.34, while Public Bank and CIMB each climbed four sen. Among the actives, Perak Transit gained 3.5 sen, Tanco added three sen and VS Industry who increased by two sen saw steady demand, while Velesto Energy edged up half-a-sen. Top gainers included Petronas Gas, which surged 34 sen to RM17.62, followed by Hong Leong Bank jumping 20 sen and Bintulu Port gaining 14 sen. On the downside, Nestle slipped 60 sen to RM113.60, Dutch Lady lost 50 sen and Batu Kawan eased 14 sen. Broader indices also traded firmer, with the FBM Emas up 75 points to 12,058.66 and the FBM Emas Shariah adding 63.69 points to 11,886.45. The FBM T100 gained 72.63 points, the FBM 70 rose 76.38 points and the FBM ACE advanced 29.51 points. Overall, the market held its upward momentum into midday as investors tracked global optimism and rotational buying across key sectors. Related

title: Bitcoin Slips, Ethereum Sees Rotation
body:
After a volatile 24 hours driven by macro shocks and derivatives expiry pressures, Bitcoin and Ethereum are carving key levels as traders brace for year-end narrative shifts. Bitcoin’s price action has been uncomfortably tight yet tepid near the US$90,000-US$94,000 zone in recent sessions, failing to sustain rallies that briefly flirted with upside breakout territory. This comes amid a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate-cut response that markets interpreted as less dovish than hoped, cooling risk appetite across crypto and equities alike. Bitcoin’s pullback below major psychological support at ~US$90K was confirmed in overnight trade, with the largest crypto sliding about 2% on risk-off flows. Analysts noted that liquidity clusters and technical bids around US$87,000 as the next critical support band, a break there could trigger deeper deleveraging, while defended bids may fuel another short squeeze into year-end positioning. Ethereum’s trajectory, meanwhile, also mirrors Bitcoin’s macro sensitivity but with its own unique narrative: Large holders appear to be rotating capital from Bitcoin into Ethereum, with reported flows totalling over US$140 million into Ethereum in recent weeks. Technically, Ethereum has consolidated around US$3,200-US$3,300, struggling to sustain momentum above the 200-day average amid mixed sentiment. While both coins weather macro drag but Ethereum’s relative performance is noteworthy: Its steeper volatility range suggests short-term traders are pricing rotation and the potential for a breakout once market structure stabilises. Bottomline: The crypto markets are caught between macro risk-off pressures and positioning ahead of the year-end. Bitcoin is testing support floors while Ethereum edges with rotational interest, both setups could flip dramatically once macro catalysts align or break key technical zones. Related

title: Wall Street Rallies As Fed Delivers Expected Rate Cut
body:
US stocks closed higher on Dec 10 after the Federal Reserve (Fed) cut interest rates by a quarter point, a widely anticipated move that reassured investors even as policymakers signalled a pause in further easing for now. Reuters reported that markets took comfort from the Fed’s updated projections, which still pencilled in another quarter-point cut in 2026, while lifting its 2026 growth forecast to 2.3% from 1.8% and holding its unemployment outlook at 4.4%. Chair Jerome Powell avoided offering near-term guidance but underscored downside risks to the labour market, reinforcing hopes the Fed will act again if jobs weaken. The S&P 500 rose 0.67% to 6,886.68, closing just shy of its late-October record. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1.05% to 48,057.75, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.33% to 23,654.16. Rate-sensitive stocks led the advance, with the Russell 2000 surging 1.3% to a record closing high, outperforming large caps as investors leaned into easing expectations. Sector gains were broad-based, with industrials leading the S&P 500, up 1.8%. GE Vernova soared 15.6% after forecasting stronger 2026 revenue, pointing to robust demand for artificial intelligence-linked energy infrastructure. Defensive corners lagged, with utilities down 0.1% and consumer staples barely changed. Market breadth was firmly positive. Advancers topped decliners nearly 3-to-1 on the NYSE, where new highs swamped new lows, while Nasdaq gainers also comfortably outnumbered losers. Trading volume was slightly below average, with 16.9 billion shares changing hands. For investors, the message was clear: The Fed may be pausing, but the door to further cuts and higher stocks remains open. Related

title: Ringgit Hits 4.10 Best In Four Years As Fed Cut Drags USD
body:
The ringgit surged to its strongest level in more than four years at its open on Dec 11 after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) cut interest rates by 25 basis points, weakening the greenback and lifting emerging-market currencies. At 8am, the ringgit strengthened to 4.1010/1075 against the US dollar, its best level since Oct 5, 2021, from the closing of 4.1155/1195 on Dec 10. Gains against the dollar, however, were not mirrored across major currencies as the local currency slipped versus the Japanese yen to 2.6342/6388, weakened against the British pound at 5.4896/4983 and edged lower against the euro to 4.7982/8058. By contrast, the ringgit firmed against most ASEAN peers, strengthening versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1737/1789, the Indonesian rupiah to 245.7/246.2, and the Thai baht to 12.9112/9382. It also opened higher against the Philippine peso at 6.92/6.94. The Fed’s move has reignited demand for regional currencies, with the ringgit emerging as an early beneficiary as markets reassess the US rate outlook. Related

title: Market Closes Lower As Losers Outnumber Gainers
body:
The stock market ended the day on a weaker note, with decliners outpacing gainers as investors trimmed positions across several key counters. At the closing bell, there were 594 losers against 489 gainers, while 543 stocks unchanged. Total market turnover stood at 3.111 billion shares valued at RM2.379 billion. Top decliners included BLD Plantation Bhd, which fell RM1.46 to RM15.04, followed by Nestle (M) Bhd down 80 sen to RM114.20 and Gamuda Bhd slipping 24 sen to RM4.89. Other notable losers were Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd at RM30.10 and Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd at RM32 after both counters eased 18 sen. On the upside, Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd led the gainers, rising 32 sen to RM19.52, followed by Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd up 30 sen to RM18.16 and Westports Holdings Bhd climbing 22 sen to RM5.67. Hong Leong Bank Bhd and Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd also saw modest gains, closing at RM21.60 and RM16.74, respectively, after gaining 18 sen and 16 sen. The session reflected cautious sentiment as investors assessed market movements amid mixed corporate earnings and broader economic signals. Related

title: Hong Kong Shares Open Firm On Fed‑Fuelled Risk Rally
body:
Hong Kong markets opened higher on Dec 11, riding a wave of upbeat sentiment after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) trimmed interest rates, a move that lifted global risk appetite and drew investors back to Asian equities. title: Gold Climbs After Fed Rate Cut; Silver Hits Record High
body:
Gold prices reversed course on Dec 10, rising after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) cut interest rates, though uncertainty over next year’s monetary policy tempered gains. Spot gold gained 0.7% to US$4,236.57 per oz, while US gold futures for February delivery fell slightly to US$4,224.70. The Fed’s latest quarter-point rate cut came in a divided vote, with officials signalling a likely pause on further easing as they monitor the labour market and inflation. Lower rates boosted the appeal of non-yielding assets like gold, even as policymakers remain split over the scale of potential cuts next year. Spot silver surged to a record US$61.85 per oz, up 113% this year, driven by strong industrial demand, falling inventories, and its growing status as a critical mineral. Meanwhile, platinum fell 2.4% to US$1,654.55, and palladium dropped 2% to US$1,475.94, reflecting softer industrial metal sentiment. Related

Bursa Malaysia closed higher on Dec 11, buoyed by bargain hunting following the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) 25-basis-point rate cut, despite a weaker regional market backdrop. title: Wall Street Pauses Ahead Of Fed Decision As JPMorgan Warning Weighs On S&P 500
body:
The S&P 500 closed slightly lower on Tuesday as investors braced for a potentially hawkish tone from the Federal Reserve even if policymakers deliver an expected rate cut this week. Sentiment was also hit by a slide in JPMorgan after the bank warned of higher expenses in 2026. The Fed began its two day meeting on Tuesday, with traders widely expecting a 25 basis point reduction despite inflation remaining above the central bank’s 2% target. Mixed signals from policymakers have added uncertainty, with some stressing risks of renewed price pressures while others have highlighted concerns about labour market softness. Fresh jobs data did little to settle the debate. Job openings rose marginally in October but hiring stayed subdued, while a survey by the National Federation of Independent Business indicated more companies intend to add workers soon. Jeff Schulze, head of economic and market strategy at ClearBridge, said the market now expects a “modestly less dovish Fed” following the job openings data. CME’s FedWatch Tool shows traders pricing in an 87% chance of a quarter point cut on Wednesday, although Schulze said investors are increasingly anticipating a potential pause after that move. US Treasury yields climbed ahead of the Fed’s update, adding further pressure on equities. Justin Bergner, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, said the rally in yields is making investors more cautious. The US 10 year yield rose to 4.18%, marking its fourth straight day of gains. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 179.03 points, or 0.38%, to 47,560.29. The S&P 500 slipped 6 points, or 0.09%, to 6,840.51, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 30.58 points, or 0.13%, to 23,576.49. The small cap Russell 2000 reached an intraday record before closing up 0.2%. Bank shares were volatile. The S&P 500 bank index reversed a near 1% rise to end down 2% after JPMorgan’s consumer and community banking chief Marianne Lake said expenses are expected to reach about US$105 billion in 2026 due to growth and volume related costs. JPMorgan closed 4.7% lower, its sharpest one day drop since April. Five of the 11 S&P 500 sectors finished in negative territory. Energy led gainers with a 0.7% rise while healthcare was the biggest laggard with a near 1% decline. Technology trading was choppy. US President Donald Trump said the administration would allow Nvidia to export its H200 AI chips to China subject to a 25% fee. However the Financial Times reported Beijing may limit access to the chips. Nvidia dipped 0.3% while the Philadelphia semiconductor index inched down 0.04%. Investors are also watching upcoming results from Oracle and Broadcom which may offer fresh clues on corporate spending for AI infrastructure. Media stocks were in focus as traders monitored the bidding battle between Paramount Skydance and Netflix for Warner Bros. Warner gained 3.8%, Paramount added 0.5% and Netflix slipped 0.08%. Among individual movers Campbell Soup dropped 5.2% after raising prices to offset rising costs. AutoZone fell 7.2% after missing quarterly expectations. Along with JPMorgan they were the S&P 500’s worst performers of the day. Market breadth was positive on both major exchanges. On the NYSE advancing stocks led decliners by a 1.14 to 1 ratio with 209 new highs recorded. The Nasdaq saw 2,642 gainers versus 2,137 losers and posted 100 new highs. Total trading volume across US exchanges reached 14.50 billion shares, below the 20 session average of 17.34 billion. Reuters Related

title: Stock Picks: Insight Analytics And Cheeding
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd has highlighted Insights Analytics Bhd and Cheeding Holdings Bhd as technical trading ideas, with both counters showing improving momentum based on recent price patterns. RHB Research said Insights Analytics is positioning for a further extension of its bullish trajectory after staging a breakout. The counter recently formed a bullish candlestick and closed above the RM0.90 resistance, confirming a positive technical setup supported by strong upward momentum. The research house expects follow-through buying to lift the stock towards RM0.97, with the next hurdle at RM1.04. It added that a drop below the RM0.83 support would invalidate the bullish structure and signal the start of a correction phase. Cheeding Holdings is attempting a countertrend rebound after testing its immediate resistance level with a bullish candlestick. The stock has been consolidating sideways below the RM0.825 mark. RHB Research noted that a close above this level would revive a bullish bias. If the breakout occurs, the counter may advance towards RM0.85 and later RM0.875. However, a fall below the RM0.80 support would point to a resumption of downward momentum. Related
