title: Ringgit Opens Lower Vs US Dollar, Gains Against Other Major Currencies On Fed Cut Expectations
body:
The ringgit opened lower against the US dollar on Wednesday as investors focused on incoming US economic data and the Federal Reserve’s anticipated 25-basis-point rate cut after its two-day meeting concludes later tonight. At 8 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.1140/1250 against the greenback, compared with 4.1105/1165 at Tuesday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US Dollar Index rose 0.13% to 99.220 amid mixed labour market signals. “The local note should remain well supported, although it may trade in a narrow range of RM4.11 to RM4.12,” he told Bernama. Mohd Afzanizam added that the market has largely priced in the 25-basis-point cut by the US Federal Open Market Committee on Wednesday. He noted that the key question now is whether the FOMC will maintain a cautious stance next year or pursue more aggressive rate cuts, especially with inflation potentially remaining elevated due to reciprocal US tariffs. The ringgit strengthened against other major currencies. It rose against the British pound to 5.4729/4875 from 5.4863/4943, improved versus the euro to 4.7838/7966 from 4.7900/7970, and edged higher against the Japanese yen to 2.6236/6307 from 2.6332/6373. However, the local currency slipped against regional peers. It declined versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1719/1807 from 3.1705/1753, fell against the Indonesian rupiah to 246.6/247.4 from 246.4/246.9, and weakened versus the Thai baht to 12.9225/9680 from 12.9172/9413. The ringgit also eased against the Philippine peso to 6.95/6.97 from 6.94/6.96. Bernama Related

title: Hang Seng Index Futures Stays Bullish Beneath The Dip
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) even as the contract extended its pullback for a second straight session on Tuesday. The index fell 337 pts to close at 25,440 pts as profit-taking returned. It opened at 25,771 pts, briefly touched a high of 25,853 pts, then slipped to an intraday low of 25,405 pts before closing lower. RHB Research said the bearish candlestick reflects renewed selling pressure following the recent rebound. During the evening session the index eased another 41 pts to 25,399 pts, reinforcing the market’s corrective tone. The research house noted that the ongoing pullback signals a consolidation phase, with the RSI turning lower and showing a moderation in bullish momentum. The HSIF has also dipped below its 20 day and 50 day simple moving average lines. Both indicators are beginning to turn downward, which RHB Research said is weighing on the near-term outlook. Even so the research house stressed that the broader bullish setup remains intact as long as the 25,000 pt support holds. RHB Research continues to advise traders to maintain the long position initiated at 21,416 pts on 14 April. The stop-loss is kept at 25,000 pts. Immediate support is at 25,000 pts followed by 24,300 pts. Resistance levels are now seen at 26,500 pts and subsequently 27,400 pts. Related

title: Crypto Market Firms As Ethereum Rallies, Bitcoin Consolidates
body:
The cryptocurrency market strengthened on Dec 12, with Ethereum leading gains while Bitcoin held steady at elevated levels, signalling improving sentiment among investors toward year-end. Bitcoin consolidated above the US$91,000-mark, trading around US$92,258, up about 2.1% from the previous close. Prices swung between an intraday low of US$89,697 and a high of US$94,522, reflecting active but orderly trading. Market participants said Bitcoin’s ability to hold key support levels suggested that selling pressure had eased, even as investors remained sensitive to global macroeconomic signals. On the other hand, Ethereum outperformed as it surged 6.2% to roughly US$3,310.59. The world’s second-largest cryptocurrency moved within a range of US$3,093.37 to US$3,392.39, driven by renewed interest in its ecosystem. Optimism around staking demand, Layer-2 network growth and longer-term protocol upgrades helped lift sentiment, allowing Ethereum to extend gains ahead of the broader market. Despite the firmer tone, investors stayed cautious, closely watching US economic data and central bank policy expectations for direction. Institutional participation remained selective, with traders wary of sudden shifts in liquidity conditions that could trigger renewed volatility. Overall, Bitcoin’s consolidation and Ethereum’s stronger performance point to a market in recalibration rather than retreat, as investors position for potential opportunities in the final stretch of the year. title: Bursa Opens Lower As Investors Turn Cautious Ahead Of Fed Decision
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened on a weaker note on Dec 10 as investors locked in profits and stayed on the sidelines ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest rate decision, compounded by mostly lower overnight performance on Wall Street. As of 9:05am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slipped 5.04 points, or 0.31%, to 1,609.13 from its close of 1,614.17 on Dec 9, after opening 3.13 points lower at 1,611.04. Market breadth was slightly negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 151 to 130. A total of 281 counters were unchanged, while 2,187 counters were untraded and 12 suspended. Turnover stood at 156.26 million shares worth RM84.9 million, reflecting subdued early trading interest. On the index board, most of the other key benchmarks were lower. The FBM EMAS slipped 0.19% and the FBM Shariah index declined 0.14%. In contrast, the FBM 70 index edged up 0.03%, providing limited support to the broader market. Among early laggards, Press Metal fell 16 sen to RM6.68, LPI slid eight sen to RM14.52 and Gamuda retreated seven sen to RM5.07, weighing on the benchmark. On the active counters list, TWL traded unchanged at 2.5 sen, while newly listed Main Market stock LAC Med rose two sen to 77 sen, extending its debut gains. Zetrix AI also drew buying interest, climbing 2.5 sen to 83 sen. Overall, the cautious opening reflected investor reluctance to take fresh positions as markets await clarity from the Fed later today. title: Asian Shares Ease As Fed Cut Priced, Guidance Uncertain
body:
Asian shares and Wall Street futures gave ground on Wednesday as crunch time neared for a divided Federal Reserve policy board, and earnings results threatened to test sky-high valuations in the AI space. With most assets frozen in the Fed headlights, attention was grabbed by a sudden slide in the Japanese yen and the continued dizzy ascent of silver prices, which both hit record peaks. The futures market, at least, is confident the Fed will cut rates by a quarter point to 3.50-3.75 per cent later in the day, pricing it at a 89 per cent probability. Yet it also assumes the guidance will be hawkish, implying just a 21 per cent chance of a January move. Much will depend on how many “dot plot” forecasts from Fed members see one, two or no more cuts next year. Debt markets could be pleasantly surprised should analysts at BofA prove right and the Fed announces plans to start buying Treasury bills from January to head off a liquidity squeeze. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.1 per cent, as Chinese blue chips fell 0.8 per cent in the wake of mixed inflation data. Consumer price inflation picked up to an annual 0.7 per cent in November, but still slipped for the month alone, while producer prices remained mired in deflation. title: Wall Street Ends Lower Ahead Of Key Fed Decision As Treasury Yields Rise
body:
Wall Street’s main indexes closed lower on Monday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy update due on Wednesday, while US Treasury yields rose, adding pressure on equities. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 215.67 points, or 0.45%, to 47,739.32, the S&P 500 lost 23.89 points, or 0.35%, to 6,846.51, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 32.22 points, or 0.14%, to 23,545.90. Most S&P 500 industry sectors finished in the red, with the exception of technology, which gained 0.9% boosted by Microsoft, Nvidia and Broadcom. Investor attention was partly on consumer spending data from last week, which showed moderate growth toward the end of the third quarter, bolstering expectations for a December rate cut. Traders are now pricing in an approximately 89% chance of a 25-basis-point reduction, according to CME’s FedWatch Tool. “It’ll be hard for the market to find a direction that it wants to follow until after the Fed meeting,” said Carol Schleif, chief market strategist at BMO Private Wealth. Market dynamics were further affected by US Treasury yields, with higher yields weighing on stocks. The 10-year Treasury yield rose soon after a powerful earthquake struck off Japan’s northeastern coast before US markets opened. In individual stock movements, Paramount Skydance’s $108.4 billion hostile bid for Warner Bros Discovery attracted significant attention. Shares of Warner Bros Discovery rose 4.4%, Paramount’s stock jumped 9%, while Netflix fell 3.4%, dragging down the S&P 500 Communication Services Index, which closed down 1.8%. Alphabet and Meta Platforms were also notable drags on the sector, with Alphabet falling more than 2%. Elsewhere, Marvell Technology fell 7% after missing out on a spot in the S&P 500 to Carvana, whose shares rose 12%. Confluent surged 29% after IBM announced an $11 billion acquisition, while Tesla declined 3% following a bearish note from Morgan Stanley. Looking ahead, the market will shift focus to upcoming tech earnings from Broadcom and Oracle, amid investor scrutiny over debt-driven AI spending. In a development expected to support AI companies, US President Donald Trump said he would sign an executive order establishing a single national rule for artificial intelligence. Trading volumes on the NYSE saw 16.12 billion shares change hands, with declining issues outnumbering advancers 2.04-to-1. On the Nasdaq, 2,092 stocks rose against 2,672 declines, while the S&P 500 posted 20 new 52-week highs and 10 new lows. Oppenheimer maintained a bullish outlook despite Monday’s declines, forecasting a year-end 2026 target of 8,100 points for the S&P 500, citing strong earnings and macroeconomic resilience. title: Stock Today: Tanco Dips 3.39% As Port Project HOA Announced
body:
Tanco Holdings Bhd’s shares fell 3.39% to RM1.14 as of 12.18 pm, with a traded volume of 34.2 million shares. The stock opened at RM1.18, hit a high of RM1.20 and a low of RM1.10, while the last average closing price stood at RM1.18. The property developer signed a Heads of Agreement (HOA) with CCCC Dredging Southeast Asia Sdn Bhd yesterday, a subsidiary of China Communications Construction Company (CCCC), appointing the firm as contractor for the Sea Port Component of its Smart AI Container Port in Port Dickson. The engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) works carry a maximum contract value of RM3.53 billion, subject to final design, costing and commercial terms, with construction expected to be completed within three and a half years. The agreement marks a significant step for Tanco in expanding its infrastructure footprint, though the share price decline reflects market caution amid the large-scale project announcement. Related

title: Stock Today: MISC Gains 0.41% Amid Offshore Contract Win

title: Stock Today: DKSH Malaysia Halted Ahead Of Proposed Capital Reduction
body:
Shares of DKSH Holdings (Malaysia) Bhd (DKSH) were not traded as of midday, with the stock showing no activity and the last closing price standing at RM5.27, reflecting a lack of market movement. The trading halt comes as DKSH announced that its major shareholder, DKSH Resources (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, has requested the company to undertake a selective capital reduction (SCR) and repayment exercise under Section 116 of the Companies Act 2016. The proposed SCR will see a cash repayment of RM6.15 per ordinary share to all shareholders of DKSH Malaysia, excluding DKSH Resources (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd. The entitlement date for the exercise will be determined and announced at a later stage. Investors are likely awaiting further announcements regarding the SCR and the entitlement date, which could influence the stock’s liquidity and market activity once trading resumes. Related

title: SGX Opens Slightly Higher Ahead Of FOMC Decision
body:
Singapore’s stock market opened slightly higher on Tuesday, with the Straits Times Index (STI) up 2.69 points, or 0.06%, at 4,509.77 as investors awaited the Federal Reserve’s policy update later this week. Market breadth was positive, with 94 advancers outnumbering 54 decliners, while total trading volume stood at 59.26 million shares, valued at S$82.98 million. Major banks saw modest gains, with DBS rising 0.22% to S$54.09, while UOB and OCBC remained largely flat. Key blue chips including Singtel, Genting Singapore, ComfortDelGro and Seatrium saw mixed movements in early trading. Regional markets showed cautious optimism ahead of the Fed meeting. Japan’s Nikkei 225 futures rose to 50,480, while FTSE China A50 Index futures were at 15,320. Taiwan and broader APAC tech futures also tracked higher, signalling investor caution tempered by hopes of a potential rate cut. The MSCI Singapore Index Futures were trading at 436, in line with the modest gains seen at the open. Market watchers noted that sentiment was influenced by expectations of an 89% chance of a 25-basis-point rate cut by the Fed this week, according to CME FedWatch data, while global yields and US equities remain under close observation. Investors are also watching regional REITs and technology plays, with the iEdge S-REIT Index at 1,097.84 and the iEdge Southeast Asia+ TECH Index trading at 5,165.51 in USD terms. With the Fed decision looming, early Singapore market activity reflects a cautious approach, balancing steady domestic fundamentals against potential global policy shifts. Related

title: Ringgit Opens Slightly Lower Ahead Of FOMC Meeting, Trades In Narrow Range
body:
The ringgit opened marginally weaker against the US dollar this morning, trading at 4.1120/1220, compared with 4.1100/1145 at yesterday’s close, as market participants awaited the start of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) two-day meeting. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid noted that the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.10% to 99.087 points ahead of the meeting. “US Treasury bond yields were also higher as fixed income traders and investors become increasingly wary about what could be said and projected when the FOMC meeting concludes tomorrow,” he told Bernama. He added that a 25-basis-point US rate cut is widely expected, based on current labour market, business, and consumer data, though the interest rate path for 2026 remains uncertain. “The new Fed chairman could lean towards monetary easing,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit also weakened slightly against the British pound to 5.4797/4930 from 5.4729/4789, edged down versus the euro to 4.7868/7984 from 4.7873/7926, but rose modestly against the Japanese yen to 2.6384/6450 from 2.6429/6460. Against regional currencies, the ringgit strengthened versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1687/1769 from 3.1698/1735 and advanced against the Thai baht to 12.8822/9224 from 12.9006/9204, while slipping slightly against the Indonesian rupiah to 246.2/247.0 from 246.1/246.5. It remained largely unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.97/7.00. Bernama Related

title: HSIF Pulls Back, Stay Positive On Uptrend
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd has maintained its positive trading bias on the Hang Seng Index Futures despite the contract slipping into a corrective phase on Monday. The index fell 370 pts to settle at 25,777 pts after opening at 26,142 pts. It touched an intraday high of 26,207 pts and a low of 25,772 pts before closing with a bearish candlestick, signalling pressure near the 26,000-pt psychological level. During the evening session, it eased a further 14 pts to 25,763 pts. RHB Research described the pullback as an orderly consolidation that does not threaten the broader upward structure. It noted that the RSI has drifted lower and is hovering around the 50% level, indicating that underlying bullish momentum remains. The research house also highlighted that both the 20-day and 50-day moving averages continue to trend higher, supporting a constructive technical backdrop. According to the report, the uptrend remains intact as long as the HSIF holds above the 25,000-pt support level. RHB Research continues to advise traders to maintain the long position initiated at 21,416 pts on 14 April, with the stop-loss set at 25,000 pts. The research house pegged immediate support at 25,000 pts followed by 24,300 pts. Resistance is seen at 26,500 pts and subsequently 27,400 pts. Related

title: Gold Holds Steady In Malaysia As Global Market Consolidates
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia continued their gradual ascent, with one troy ounce trading at RM17,241.17, up RM12.30 or 0.07% at the time of writing. The price per gram was RM554.32, while a kilogram of gold reached RM554,316.43. Over the past year, gold in Malaysia has surged 44.43%, reflecting both domestic demand and broader global trends. In the last six months, the commodity has climbed 22.43%, while long-term gains over 20 years stand at a remarkable 764.89%. Silver has also recorded solid growth, rising 0.40% to RM0.95 per gram and showing a 68.07% increase over the past year. Globally, gold has been consolidating, with COMEX Gold trading slightly lower at US$4,217.70 per ounce on Monday, after a session range of US$4,204 to US$4,247.90. Analysts at RHB Investment Bank Bhd noted that “the negative price action, coupled with the downward-rounding RSI, shows that consolidation is still in play.” Despite the temporary sideways movement, both the 20- and 50-day SMA lines are trending upwards, supporting a bullish technical outlook. COMEX Gold may resume an upward movement towards US$4,400, while strong support lies at US$3,800. The rise in gold prices comes amid sustained global interest in the safe-haven asset. In 2025, annual gains in gold have been strong across major currencies: +59.6% in US$, +53.6% in CAD, +50% in GBP, +68.1% in INR and +58% in JPY, signalling robust investor confidence worldwide. Analysts suggest that as long as gold remains above key support levels, the positive trading bias will continue. With demand in Malaysia and globally showing resilience, gold remains a preferred investment for hedging against economic uncertainty, currency fluctuations and inflationary pressures, reinforcing its role as a long-term store of value. title: Global Equity Market Mixed As Asian Indices Open Lower
body:
Global equity markets showed a mixed performance on Tuesday, with most major Asian indices opening lower, while US stocks retreated overnight and European markets ended the session largely flat. In Asia, China’s key benchmarks slipped at the open, with the Shanghai Composite Index down 0.19% to 3,916.51 and the Shenzhen Component Index falling 0.26% to 13,295.62. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 dipped 0.21% to 8,606.60, and South Korea’s KOSPI declined 0.60% to 4,129.77. The S&P 500 slipped 0.35% to 6,846.51, the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 0.45% to 47,739.32, and the Nasdaq Composite eased 0.14% to 23,545.90. European stocks were mixed at Monday’s close. Germany’s DAX edged up 0.07% to 24,046.01, while the UK’s FTSE 100 fell 0.23% to 9,645.09. France’s CAC 40 slipped 0.08% to 8,108.43. Related

title: Bursa Edges Up Ahead Of Fed Verdict As Orkim Debut Drags
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened marginally higher, with all major indices showing modest gains as investors positioned themselves ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) two-day meeting in the US, which begins today. The benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBMKLCI) opened at 1,613.06 points, edging up 0.28 points or 0.02% from Monday’s close, with intraday moves ranging between 1,612.63 and 1,620.73. The broader FBM70 gained 10.25 points (+0.06%) to 16,662.29, while the FBM Emas Index rose 3.40 points (+0.03%) to 11,928.87. Other key indices, including the FBM Shariah and F4GBM, also posted slight improvements of 0.02–0.03%. Top gainers in early trade included Nestle (FBMKLCI constituent) rising 0.5 points to 113.00, Petronas Gas (+0.24 to 17.26), and FCW (+0.20 to 2.00). Meanwhile, Orkim, the newly listed transportation and logistics company, slipped 3.5 sen to 0.885, while DLADY and HL Bank also recorded minor declines. Trading activity was led by Orkim, which saw 30.3 million shares exchanged, reflecting continued investor interest following its oversubscribed IPO. Other actively traded counters included AHB, BMS, Tanco, and PMETAL. Market watchers are cautious ahead of the FOMC meeting, where investors are expecting a 25-basis-point US rate cut but remain focused on guidance for 2026. Regional markets have shown mixed openings: Singapore’s STI rose 0.06% to 4,509.77, while futures for Nikkei 225 and FTSE China A50 suggested muted moves. Brent crude held near US$62 per barrel, with oil markets stabilising after recent fluctuations, adding another layer of cautious optimism. As of 9.13 am, overall market sentiment remained tepid, with 94 advancers outnumbering 54 decliners across Bursa Malaysia, as investors awaited further cues from the FOMC and upcoming economic data from the US and Asia. title: Aussie Dollar Rises As RBA Holds Rates Ahead Of Fed Meeting
body:
The Australian dollar strengthened after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) kept interest rates on hold, as investors await the US Federal Reserve’s policy meeting later this week. The Australian currency advanced 0.2% to $0.6639 after the central bank maintained rates for a third consecutive month at 3.6%, as widely expected, and cautioned that a pickup in inflation could be persistent. “The RBA didn’t try to tamp down hawkish market expectations,” said Sim Moh Siong, currency strategist at Bank of Singapore. “What was said in the meeting matches the market expectations that the RBA has tilted a bit more on the hawkish direction.” RBA Governor Michele Bullock added in a press conference that more rate cuts were not needed, helping the currency extend its gains. title: Asian Markets Slip As Investors Brace For Fed Signals
body:
Asian equities retreated on Tuesday as traders grew increasingly cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s final meeting of the year. With a rate cut on Wednesday seen as a foregone conclusion, attention has shifted to what policymakers project for 2025. Much of the focus now centres on the Fed’s “dot plot”, which will outline the expected path of interest rates. Investors will also scrutinise the statement released after the meeting and Jerome Powell’s press conference for any hints of the debate playing out among central bank officials. Market sentiment, once buoyed by hopes of a string of reductions next year, has softened. Bloomberg reported that traders are now pricing in two cuts in 2025 instead of the three anticipated just a week earlier. “This decision is unlikely to be unanimous, with dissent expected from hawks and doves,” wrote Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at City Index. “The focus will be on economic projections and the dot plot to provide further insight into the Fed’s plans for next year. The market sees two rate cuts by the summer. Should the Fed’s dot plot differ from this, there could be volatility.” Expectations for more aggressive easing had climbed in recent weeks thanks to data signalling a cooling labour market, which helped counter fears of persistent inflation. That optimism also received a boost last month after reports suggested President Donald Trump’s top economic aide Kevin Hassett was the frontrunner to take over the Fed once Powell’s term concludes. But some analysts warn that internal divisions at the Fed could complicate the road ahead. Pictet Wealth Management senior US economist Xiao Cui said, “We expect solid growth, above-target inflation, and a slowing labour market to increase internal divisions at the (policy board) and make 2026 a particularly challenging year for policymakers. Downside risks to the labour market should lead the Committee to cut once more in December, before shifting to a quarterly pace of cuts in March and June.” She added that her team “see risks that Fed cuts are delayed into the second half of 2026”. Asian markets struggled following declines across Wall Street’s major indexes. Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Seoul, Wellington, Taipei and Manila all drifted lower, while Tokyo, Singapore and Jakarta managed to edge into positive territory. Chip-makers traded in mixed fashion after Trump said he had reached an agreement with China’s President Xi Jinping to allow Nvidia to sell advanced artificial intelligence chips to China, in a shift away from the restrictions imposed under Joe Biden. Those rules had required semiconductor firms to design downgraded versions tailored specifically for the Chinese market. Tokyo-listed Renesas climbed more than 2 per cent, with Advantest also higher and SoftBank extending gains. In contrast, Samsung in Seoul shed more than 1 per cent and SK hynix lost nearly 2 per cent. TSMC slipped 1 per cent in Taipei. CNA Related

title: Stock Today: VS Industry Dips 1.06%, Eyes Remain On The Prize
body:
VS Industry Bhd saw its share price slip 1.06% to RM0.465 as of 11.55 am, with 16.9 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM0.475, touched a high of RM0.480 and a low of RM0.460, with the last done slightly below the last closing price of RM0.470. The electronics manufacturing services provider recently reported its first quarter results for FY26, posting revenue of RM1.08 billion, down marginally from RM1.11 billion a year ago due to weaker sales in Indonesia. Profit after tax and non-controlling interest came in at RM30.6 million, in line with the same period last year, and marked a rebound from a net loss of RM33 million in 4QFY25. Quarter-on-quarter, revenue rose 25.6% from RM858.8 million, aided by higher sales orders and a reversal of impairment losses on trade receivables. Analysts remain positive on the stock despite the modest share price dip. RHB Investment Bank has maintained a BUY rating with a target price of RM0.65, citing improving operations in Malaysia and the Philippines, alongside new customer wins. CIMB Investment Bank upgraded VS Industry from Hold to BUY with a slightly higher target of RM0.66, highlighting operational improvements and trade diversion opportunities as key drivers. The company’s Malaysian division sustained pre-tax margins of 4.6%, while Philippine operations narrowed losses and are expected to break even by year-end with the commencement of a second production line. New floorcare and haircare lines in Malaysia are projected to contribute RM900 million–1 billion annually once fully operational, representing up to 25% of group revenue in FY26. A newly secured pool-cleaning customer contract worth RM300 million per annum will further support growth from March 2026. With the stock trading at 12 times CY26F P/E, near 1.5 standard deviations below its five-year mean, analysts see VS Industry at a potential inflection point, with re-rating catalysts from stronger contributions in the Philippines and a gradual recovery in global consumer spending. title: Stock Today: Sunway Climbs 2.39% As Healthcare Listing Gains Momentum
body:
Sunway Bhd traded higher at midday as investors continued to react to fresh progress on the upcoming listing of its healthcare arm, Sunway Healthcare Holdings (SHH). As of 2.34 pm, the counter rose 2.39% to RM5.56, adding RM0.13 from the previous close. It opened at RM5.48 before moving within a range of RM5.46 to RM5.57, with more than 2.33 million shares changing hands. The latest gain follows the Securities Commission Malaysia’s approval on 4 December for SHH’s proposed Main Market listing, a move that positions the exercise as one of the largest healthcare IPOs planned in the country. The approval includes a significant share split that will expand SHH’s base from 1.21 billion to 10.93 billion shares, alongside a two-step distribution exercise involving 676.04 million SHH shares. These shares will be distributed to eligible Sunway shareholders via a dividend-in-specie at a ratio of one SHH share for every 10 Sunway shares held, excluding treasury shares. The final amount will depend on Sunway’s share base on the entitlement date. SHH is expected to list with 11.5 billion issued shares on Bursa Malaysia once the exercise is completed. Sunway last traded at RM5.56. Related

title: Stock Today: IJM Dips 1.33% Amid Mixed Earnings Report
body:
IJM Corporation Bhd (IJM) closed at RM2.22, down 1.33% from the previous session, with 23.03 million shares traded as of 4.04 pm. The stock opened at RM2.25, hitting a high of RM2.26 and a low of RM2.22 during the day. The decline comes after the group reported 1HFY3/26 core earnings of RM222 million, down 11% year-on-year, representing 40% of CIMB Securities’ previous full-year forecast and 41% of consensus estimates. The earnings shortfall was largely due to weaker property and port contributions, with property pre-tax profit dropping 51% to RM34 million and Kuantan Port pre-tax profit falling 40% to RM72 million. title: Bursa Opens On A Positive Note As Markets Track Asia
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened slightly higher on Monday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI rising 2.63 points or 0.16% to 1,621.76, as investors weighed regional market cues at the start of the week. The broader market indices also edged up, with the FBM Emas Index climbing 17.27 points to 12,051.34 and the FBM Small Cap Index rising 3.81 points to 16,930.65. Meanwhile, the FBM Ace and FBM EMAS Shariah indices gained 1.23 points and 15.53 points, respectively. Among the most active stocks, MMAG led trading with 12.9 million shares, while PHARMA, ECA, IAB, and DNEX followed closely in volume. Top gainers included F&N (+0.58), MPI (+0.26), PETDAG (+0.18), FCW (+0.06), and VSTECS (+0.06). title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Rebound As Market Sentiment Improves
body:
The crypto market staged a notable rebound on Nov 10, with Bitcoin and Ethereum leading gains as investor sentiment brightened and institutional inflows returned to the sector. Bitcoin climbed around 4% to hover near US$106,000, while Ethereum rose 7% to about US$3,640, extending a short-term recovery after several weeks of cautious trading. The rebound coincides with easing political uncertainty in the US, where traders increasingly expect a resolution to the looming government shutdown. The reduction in risk premium helped crypto assets regain momentum alongside broader market optimism. Technically, Bitcoin is consolidating around the US$106,000 level, with key support seen near its 50-week exponential moving average of US$100,900. A sustained break below that zone could undermine the uptrend, while a weekly close above current levels would reinforce the bullish structure. Ethereum’s setup appears stronger, with the token defending the US$3,600 region and building a potential base for a move toward US$4,000. However, analysts note that Ethereum’s gas fees have fallen to multi-year lows, a sign of efficiency, but also a reminder that on-chain activity and network revenues remain subdued. For corporates and institutional investors, Bitcoin’s stabilising trajectory underscores its gradual evolution from a speculative asset to a portfolio hedge and treasury instrument. Should the inflow trend persist, more companies may revisit the idea of limited balance-sheet exposure to digital assets. Ethereum, meanwhile, continues to underpin the broader blockchain ecosystem powering tokenisation, decentralised finance platforms and infrastructure development. A sustained rally could benefit firms offering Ethereum-based products and services. Key risks remain: US Federal Reserve policy shifts, regulatory developments and global risk-off sentiment could all quickly dampen the rally. Traders are also watching this week’s US macro data and on-chain flow metrics to gauge whether the current momentum can hold. Bottom Line: Bitcoin and Ethereum are back in recovery mode — steady, not euphoric. Institutional confidence is returning, volatility is easing and the market is cautiously rebuilding trust. But with macro and regulatory uncertainties still in play, the next move will test whether this rebound can evolve into a sustained bull trend. Related

title: Crypto Market Review: Bitcoin, Ethereum Struggle Amid Volatility
body:
The digital asset markets ended the week on a cautious note, as Bitcoin and Ethereum faced technical resistance and broader market uncertainty. Bitcoin dropped below US$108,000 early in the week, testing support around US$105,000, while Ethereum fell nearly 8%, trading close to US$3,560. By Nov 7, both assets showed signs of stabilisation, but gains remained muted. Analysts highlighted that Bitcoin’s decline below its 200-day moving average (~US$109,800) was a key technical red flag. At the same time, outflows from crypto funds and hedge-fund rotation into safer assets dampened risk appetite. Macroeconomic uncertainty also weighed on sentiment, as interest-rate developments and global market volatility affected risk-on assets, including cryptocurrencies. Moving forward, market watchers expect consolidation rather than a new bull run in the coming week, with key factors to monitor including Bitcoin’s ability to reclaim support around US$105,000-US$110,000, Ethereum stabilising above US$3,300 and any institutional inflows or renewed macro catalysts that could shift sentiment. Overall, the crypto market remains active but fragile, with volatility likely to persist until clear market triggers emerge. Related

title: Wall Street Ends Mixed As Shutdown, Tech Woes Weigh
body:
US stocks ended a turbulent week on a mixed note, with the Nasdaq closing lower while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones eked out modest gains, as investors grappled with economic uncertainty, a record-long government shutdown and stretched tech valuations. Reuters reported that the Dow rose 74.80 points (0.16%) to 46,987.10, the S&P 500 added 8.48 points (0.13%) to 6,728.80, while the Nasdaq slipped 49.45 points (0.21%) to 23,004.54. All three benchmarks ended the week in the red, with the Nasdaq suffering its steepest weekly drop since early April amid mounting concerns over inflated artificial intelligence-driven stock prices. Optimism crept back into markets late in the session after reports of progress in congressional talks to end the longest federal shutdown in US history. The impasse has already clouded the economic outlook, with the University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index plunging to a three-year low and assessments of current conditions hitting the most pessimistic level on record. The shutdown’s data blackout has also complicated the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook, limiting visibility on jobs and inflation trends. On the corporate front, earnings season neared its end, with 83% of S&P 500 companies beating expectations, fuelling forecasts of 16.8% year-on-year profit growth for the third quarter, up from 8% a year earlier. Among major stock movers, Expedia soared 17.6% on strong business-to-business bookings, while Tesla fell 3.7% after shareholders approved Elon Musk’s record-breaking pay package. Microchip Technology tumbled 5.2% following weak sales guidance, and Block slid 7.7%, with Take-Two Interactive dropping 8.1% after delaying the release of Grand Theft Auto VI to November 2026. On the NYSE, advancers led decliners by a 1.44-to-1 ratio, while the Nasdaq saw a 1.1-to-1 edge for gainers. Trading volume came in slightly below average at 20.15 billion shares. Despite the late rebound on Nov 7, Wall Street closed the week bruised, a reminder that high valuations and political gridlock remain the market’s biggest hurdles heading into year-end. Related

title: Seoul Stocks Extend Losses As Tech Rout, Rate Jitters Weigh
body:
South Korean shares fell sharply on Nov 7, with the Kospi sliding 1.8% to close at 3,953.76, as investors dumped heavyweight tech stocks amid renewed worries over lofty valuations and fading hopes for near-term rate cuts. Foreign investors were net sellers for a fifth straight session, dragging the Korean won to a seven-month low against the US dollar. Analysts said global risk-off sentiment deepened after Wall Street’s Nasdaq posted another decline overnight, pressuring Asia’s tech-heavy markets. Chipmakers led the downturn as Samsung Electronics fell 2.4%, while SK Hynix dropped 3.1%, with traders questioned whether the recent artificial intelligence-driven rally had gone too far. Losses also extended to platform and battery stocks, with Naver and LG Energy Solution down more than 2% each. The Kosdaq index also slipped 1.2%, tracking the broader decline. Institutional investors stayed on the sidelines, awaiting clarity from the Bank of Korea’s policy meeting later this month, where policymakers are expected to maintain rates amid persistent inflation concerns. Despite the sell-off on Nov 7, strategists said downside pressure could ease if US inflation data next week supports expectations of monetary easing early next year. Turnover on the main board was ₩12.4 trillion, with decliners outnumbering advancers by more than three to one. Related

title: HLIB Downgrades Axis REIT To ‘Hold’ Despite Strategic RM800M Penang Acquisition
body:
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has downgraded Axis REIT to HOLD from Buy with an unchanged target price of RM2.25, while MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) maintained its NEUTRAL call and target price of RM2.07. Both research houses cited the trust’s latest RM800 million industrial property acquisition in Penang as a key move that will lift long-term earnings but add near-term gearing pressure. Axis REIT announced that it has accepted a letter of offer from Ann Joo Steel Bhd (AJSB) to acquire a freehold industrial property located in Seberang Perai Tengah, Penang. The property spans 135.5 acres and comprises land and industrial buildings that will be leased back to AJSB for eight years, with a fixed monthly rental of RM4.16 million. According to MBSB Research, the deal will increase Axis REIT’s total assets by 15% and deliver a gross acquisition yield of 6.2%, higher than its average financing cost of 4.1%. The research house expects the acquisition to lift FY26–FY27 earnings by about 7%, though it noted that gearing will rise from 0.33 times to 0.42 times, potentially triggering a private placement exercise. HLIB described the transaction as positive for Axis REIT’s long-term income stability due to the property’s strategic location within the Prai Industrial Estate, near Penang Island, the North–South Expressway, and Penang Port. The house highlighted that the RM800 million purchase price, translating to RM134.2 per sq ft, represents a 62% discount to the median industrial property price of RM351.1 per sq ft recorded over the past 12 months. The acquisition will be fully funded by debt, pushing the gearing ratio to 46.8% based on HLIB’s FY27 forecast. While yield-neutral in the short term, it is expected to boost FY27 distribution income by 6.2%, with meaningful earnings contribution expected to begin from the first quarter of 2027. Despite the positive fundamentals, HLIB said the recent rally in Axis REIT’s unit price has limited near-term upside, tempering its earlier bullish stance. It added that while Axis REIT’s proactive acquisition strategy and exposure to key logistics and industrial hubs continue to support its long-term outlook, investors should expect modest returns in the near term. Both MBSB Research and HLIB maintained that the proposed acquisition aligns with Axis REIT’s long-term strategy to grow its industrial asset base, though current yields of around 4.2% to 4.5% remain less attractive compared to broader market opportunities. Axis REIT’s counter closed its trading session on Nov 7 at RM2.15, after declining one sen with around 12 million shares traded. Related

title: Ringgit Nears One-Year High As BNM Holds Rate Steady
body:
The ringgit rose towards a one-year high against the US dollar on Friday morning, after Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) left the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75%. At 8am, the local note traded at 4.1760/1865 against the US dollar, up from Thursday’s close of 4.1820/1845. The level was close to its previous peak of 4.1730/1790, recorded on Oct 2 last year. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the central bank’s decision to hold its policy rate while the United States faces the prospect of easing monetary policy could benefit ringgit-denominated assets. “With BNM standing pat on the OPR, the prospect of lower interest rates in the United States would gradually make ringgit-denominated assets more attractive as interest rate differentials narrow,” he said. “As such, we expect the ringgit to trade between 4.17 and 4.19 today.” The US Dollar Index (DXY) fell below the 100-point mark to 99.720 as the American labour market continued to show weakness. “US data showed more than 150,000 job cuts in October, the largest reduction in 20 years. Hence, the case for an interest rate cut is building for the December meeting,” Afzanizam added. IPPFA Sdn Bhd director of investment strategy and country economist Mohd Sedek Jantan noted that the greenback’s recent upward run appeared to be losing steam, with the ringgit strengthening against the dollar, Thai baht, and Singapore dollar. “Market attention has rotated back to the United States’ fiscal outlook, coinciding with a broad sell-off in US Treasuries and steadier performance in global equity indices,” he said. Mohd Sedek added that fiscal pressures remain a recurring issue in the US, though data indicate the economy has yet to slip into a sharp slowdown. “While we continue to view December as the likeliest timing for a Federal Reserve rate cut, the path beyond that remains subject to evolving macro signals.” He said the ringgit’s stronger opening reflected both the easing of the dollar’s momentum and a firmer tone across regional currencies. At the same time, the ringgit was mixed against other major currencies. It eased against the yen to 2.7305/7375 from 2.7202/7220 and slipped against the British pound to 5.4864/5002 from 5.4696/4729. It also weakened versus the euro to 4.8220/8342 from 4.8143/8172. However, the local note strengthened across most ASEAN currencies, rising against the Singapore dollar to 3.2017/2103 from 3.2034/2055 and improving against the Thai baht to 12.8829/9285 from 12.9178/9311. It also gained on the Indonesian rupiah to 250.0/250.7 from 250.3/250.6 and the Philippine peso to 7.08/7.10 from 7.09/7.10 previously. BNM maintained the OPR at its final Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting of 2025 yesterday. Bernama Related

title: Hong Kong Futures Climb Past Moving Averages, RHB Backs Ongoing Rebound
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the index surged 598 points to close at 26,533 points on Wednesday, signalling a strong return of bullish momentum. The index opened at 25,949 points and briefly slipped to 25,873 points before rebounding sharply to an intraday high of 26,538 points. It eventually settled near its peak, forming a strong bullish candlestick pattern. During the evening session, it eased 97 points to last trade at 26,436 points. According to RHB Research, the latest movement confirms a decisive rebound as the index closed above both the 20-day and 50-day simple moving average (SMA) lines. The firm said the bulls have taken control, with the HSIF poised to test its immediate resistance at 27,400 points, followed by 28,500 points. “The RSI has also crossed above the 50% level, showing that bullish momentum is reaccelerating. Therefore, we maintain our positive trading bias,” it said in a note. RHB Research advised traders to hold their long positions initiated at 21,416 points, the closing level on 14 April. To mitigate risks, the stop-loss threshold remains at 25,000 points. The report identified the first support level at 25,000 points and the next at 24,300 points, reaffirming confidence that the index could extend its uptrend if buying interest persists. Related

title: Dollar Steadies Amid Weak Chinese Trade Data
body:
The dollar found footing in Asia on Friday, supported by broad market sentiment, as sterling and the yen lost ground and weaker-than-expected Chinese trade data weighed on regional markets. The dollar index, which tracks the currency against six major peers, rose 0.1% to 99.796, recovering some of its earlier losses, though it remained within the trading range it has held since August. Markets are relying on limited data due to the ongoing U.S. government shutdown, which has postponed the release of the monthly non-farm payrolls report. Traders have turned to private sector data showing job losses in October within the government and retail sectors, while cost-cutting and AI adoption have also contributed to layoffs. “Markets are flying blind because we only have private sector data to rely on,” said Christopher Wong, currency strategist at OCBC in Singapore. “There isn’t a clear big trend in the dollar, and that’s why in Asia currencies are taking cues from the broad market sentiment.” The uncertainty has led traders to increase bets on a U.S. rate cut. Trading in Fed funds futures now implies a 70% chance of a cut at the Federal Reserve’s next meeting on 10 December, up from 62% the previous day. Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee warned on Thursday that the lack of official inflation data “accentuates” his caution, telling CNBC: “When it’s foggy, let’s just be a little careful and slow down.” In Asia, the dollar strengthened 0.2% to 153.27 yen following data showing Japanese household spending in September rose 1.8% year-on-year, below the median forecast of 2.5%. The Australian dollar was flat at $0.64785, while the New Zealand dollar dipped 0.2% to $0.5620. Sterling fell 0.2% to $1.31195 after the Bank of England held interest rates steady on a 5-4 vote, with Governor Andrew Bailey casting the deciding vote. Meanwhile, British finance minister Rachel Reeves has indicated that a rise in personal taxation is among the “major measures” being prepared for the upcoming budget, according to The Times. The euro edged down 0.1% to $1.1535, retreating from a one-week high, as global investors weighed the impact of weak trade data and ongoing uncertainties in major economies. Reuters Related

title: Bursa Opens Softer As Investors Digest BNM’s OPR Decision
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened marginally lower as investors took a cautious stance following Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision yesterday to keep the overnight policy rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75%. At 9.17am, the FBM KLCI stood at 1,618.89, easing slightly from Thursday’s close of 1,618.94. The benchmark index moved between 1,616.61 and 1,618.89 in early trade, mirroring the cautious sentiment seen across regional markets. The broader market was also softer, with the FBM 70 slipping 40.81 points to 16,901.93 and the FBM Emas Index down 11.26 points to 12,026.63. Market breadth was negative, with decliners outpacing advancers, while total volume stood at 213.42 million shares worth RM409.39 million. Top active counters included MMAG, which declined 1 sen to 8.5 sen, and Pertama Digital, slipping 6.5 sen to 4.5 sen, while PTRANS and Pharmaniaga added half a sen each to 27 sen and 24 sen respectively. Among blue chips, Hong Leong Industries rose 14 sen to RM14.88, Heineken Malaysia advanced 12 sen to RM21.76, while IHH Healthcare gained 7 sen to RM8.29. Meanwhile, Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI) fell 36 sen to RM29.84, Petronas Dagangan slid 24 sen to RM22.30, and United Plantations lost 12 sen to RM25.46. The central bank’s decision to maintain its policy rate signalled a steady approach to balancing growth and inflation, though investors are likely awaiting clearer cues from upcoming US economic data before making bolder moves. The ringgit’s appreciation to near a one-year high against the US dollar following the OPR announcement may also have contributed to the cautious tone, as exporters could face short-term currency headwinds. Elsewhere in the region, trading sentiment was mixed, with investors watching developments in China’s policy measures and US labour data. As the day progresses, market observers expect the benchmark index to hover within the 1,615 to 1,625 range, supported by selective buying in heavyweights but capped by profit-taking after recent gains. title: Bursa Malaysia Holds Steady Amid Mild Buying Interest
body:
Bursa Malaysia remained in positive territory at midday as mild buying emerged late in the morning session, cushioning losses amid weaker regional markets. At 12.30 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.75 points, or 0.05%, to 1,619.69, after opening 1.31 points lower at 1,617.63. The benchmark moved between 1,616.50 and 1,620.08 in morning trading. Turnover stood at 2.27 billion shares worth RM1.04 billion, with market breadth weaker at 598 losers against 296 gainers. Hong Leong Investment Bank said the market is expected to remain range-bound amid US market volatility, citing concerns over stretched tech valuations, diverging US Federal Reserve rate-cut expectations, and the US Supreme Court’s stance on President Donald Trump’s tariffs. “In the near term, upside may be capped around the 1,632–1,640 resistance zone as investors gauge the impact of the prolonged US government shutdown and the upcoming Sabah state election,” it added. Among heavyweights, Maybank and Public Bank were flat at RM9.92 and RM4.26, respectively. title: Bitcoin, Ethereum Stumble As Market Awaits Next Catalyst
body:
Bitcoin and Ethereum slipped on Nov 6, extending a volatile week for the world’s two largest cryptocurrencies as traders weighed macroeconomic headwinds, profit-taking and shifting ETF flows. Bitcoin hovered near US$101,500, down about 1.5%, after touching an intraday high of US$104,100 and a low of US$100,400. Ethereum, meanwhile, eased to around US$3,317, losing 2.5% on the day. The moves come as sentiment in global markets remains risk-averse, with investors bracing for fresh US inflation data and possible signals from the Federal Reserve on future rate paths. Analysts say Bitcoin is sitting at a crucial crossroads. The US$100,000 mark has emerged as a key support level, one that could determine whether the benchmark crypto stabilises or slips deeper into correction territory. On-chain data, however, offers a glimmer of optimism. The MVRV ratio, a measure of market value versus realised value, suggests selling pressure may be nearing exhaustion, indicating a potential accumulation phase among long-term holders. Still, persistent ETF outflows and a “risk-off” tone across global markets have capped upside momentum. In the meantime, Ethereum is facing its own hurdles, trading near US$3,300 after a steady week of outflows from ETH-based exchange-traded funds. Despite near-term weakness, some analysts believe the token may be nearing a pivot point. Technical indicators show Ethereum could rebound if it manages to reclaim US$3,500-US$3,600. A breakout above that range could pave the way toward US$4,000 by month-end. Failure to hold current levels, however, could send the asset sliding toward the US$3,000 support zone. Despite the pullback, institutional participation in crypto markets remains robust. A recent Reuters survey found that 55% of global hedge funds maintain some form of crypto exposure, mostly through derivatives or structured products, and plan to increase allocations over the next year. That trend suggests the current weakness may reflect tactical repositioning rather than a long-term exodus. Moving forward, market watchers say Bitcoin’s ability to defend the US$100,000 line will be key in shaping sentiment across the digital-asset complex. For Ethereum, sustained consolidation above US$3,300 could signal that the correction phase is nearing its end. With US macro data and ETF flow reports due in the coming days, traders are bracing for another round of volatility. Related

title: A Spirited QoQ Earnings Recovery For Heineken, Analysts Say
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have maintained their BUY calls on Heineken Malaysia Bhd (HEIM), setting a target price of RM26.50, representing an upside potential of about 23% and a projected FY26F yield of around 7%. Both research houses said Heineken’s latest quarterly results showed a spirited quarter-on-quarter recovery, supported by margin expansion and premiumisation strategies that continue to drive earnings growth and dividend payout. RHB Research noted that Heineken’s results for the first nine months of 2025 were broadly within expectations, with a net profit of RM318 million, down 2% year-on-year. This figure accounted for 68% and 71% of the firm’s and consensus forecasts, respectively. The research house expects a stronger fourth quarter in line with seasonal patterns, maintaining its dividend discount model (DDM)-derived target price of RM26.50, which includes a 6% ESG premium and implies a 17 times price-to-earnings ratio for FY26F, on par with its five-year mean. Heineken’s 9M25 revenue was flat at RM2 billion as effective marketing and enhanced distribution helped offset softer consumer sentiment and the earlier timing of Lunar New Year. Profit before tax rose 2% to RM419 million, driven by cost optimisation and price adjustments, expanding margins by 0.6 percentage points. However, net profit fell 2% after normalising for a higher effective tax rate compared to the previous year. On a quarterly basis, the third-quarter revenue jumped 22% to RM656 million, aided by improving consumer sentiment following the weakness in the previous quarter caused by global tariff uncertainties. This lifted its PBT margin to a record 22.7%, with net profit surging 36% quarter-on-quarter to RM113 million. Both RHB Research and HLIB expect demand to be front-loaded in October before the excise duty hike takes effect in November. Although volumes may soften thereafter, they anticipate breweries ramping up marketing and promotional efforts to stimulate consumption. The upcoming Visit Malaysia Year 2026 is also expected to bolster sales through increased tourist arrivals, while efficiency gains, favourable input costs, and stable foreign exchange conditions should help sustain profit margins. The research houses added that the company’s dividend payout is likely to remain generous, supported by strong fundamentals and consistent earnings. The recent excise duty increase, while negative in the short term, is likely already priced in, given brewery stocks are trading below historical averages. RHB Research and HLIB highlighted that Heineken’s focus on premiumisation, disciplined cost management, and sustainable growth positions it well to navigate near-term challenges. However, they cautioned that risks remain, particularly from regulatory changes and potential loss of market share. As of 3pm, the stock price is down 22 sen to RM21.42. Related

title: Stock Today: SD Guthrie Rises 1.33% As Bullish Calls On Land Monetisation And Industrial Growth
body:
Shares of SD Guthrie Bhd climbed 1.33% at midday to RM5.35 as investors reacted to a series of bullish calls from research houses following its strong third-quarter performance and rising contributions from the group’s industrial property segment. At 12.09pm, the counter rose 7 sen from its previous close of RM5.28, with 6.28 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM5.30 and touched a high of RM5.38 before easing slightly. RHB Investment Bank Bhd maintained its BUY call with a higher target price of RM6.95, citing a 32% upside potential. It said SD Guthrie’s nine-month core earnings of RM1.89 billion had exceeded expectations, boosted by RM378 million in maiden contributions from land sales in Bukit Pelandok, Negeri Sembilan. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd also reaffirmed its positive view with a raised target price of RM6.01, highlighting “triple tailwinds” from stronger palm oil prices, robust land monetisation and solid ESG positioning. It noted that the company’s 9M25 core net profit of RM1.53 billion had beaten forecasts on higher palm kernel prices and industrial gains. Meanwhile, MBSB Investment Bank Bhd upgraded SD Guthrie to BUY from HOLD, increasing its target price to RM6.15 from RM5.43. It expects recurring profit from land monetisation of around RM500 million annually over the next five years, supported by improving upstream productivity and stronger crude palm oil prices. Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd reiterated its BUY call with an unchanged target price of RM5.76, noting sustained earnings momentum and stable production costs. Analysts said the group’s performance continues to be underpinned by a growing industrial portfolio, resilient upstream yields and steady land sales, with average crude palm oil prices expected to hover around RM4,300 per tonne in FY26. At its current level, SD Guthrie trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of about 15.6 times, at the lower end of its peer range. Related

title: Stock Today: Kelington Rises As Taiwan Legal Victory Ends Years-Long Dispute
body:
Shares of Kelington Group Bhd (KGB) edged higher by 1.13% to RM5.38 as at 4.27pm, following news that its subsidiary, Kelington Taiwan, had secured a favourable ruling from the Supreme Court of Taiwan, bringing an end to a prolonged legal battle. The counter saw active trading, with 1.24 million shares exchanged. It opened at RM5.32 and moved between RM5.27 and RM5.40 during the session. Kelington announced that the Supreme Court of Taiwan had dismissed the appeal filed by Hui Neng Mechanical & Electrical Engineering Co., thereby upholding earlier rulings that ordered Hui Neng to pay Kelington Taiwan NTD28.07 million (approximately RM4.11 million), along with 5% annual interest from 2018 until full settlement. The decision marks the conclusion of a legal dispute that began in 2016, reaffirming Kelington’s position in a contractual disagreement that went through several levels of appeal before the final verdict. The company said the judgment brings closure to a multi-year case, with the financial impact expected to be positive following the enforcement of the award. Related

title: Ringgit Opens Higher Ahead Of Budget 2026
body:
The ringgit started Tuesday on a stronger note against the US dollar, buoyed by renewed buying interest and optimism that the government will uphold fiscal discipline in Budget 2026. At 8 am, the local currency rose to 4.2100/2205 against the greenback from Monday’s closing of 4.2135/2180. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said investors are keeping a close watch on the Budget 2026 announcement scheduled for Friday, which is likely to steer market sentiment this week. “Traders are watching this space. On that note, the ringgit is likely to trade between RM4.21 and RM4.22 today,” he told a local news outlet, adding that stimulating domestic demand remains key. Against other major currencies, the ringgit traded mixed in early session. It weakened against the euro to 4.9295/9418 from 4.9155/9207 and slipped versus the British pound to 5.6768/6909 from 5.6608/6691. However, it strengthened slightly against the Japanese yen to 2.7996/8067 from 2.8019/8051. The local note also gained against most ASEAN currencies. It appreciated versus the Thai baht to 12.9614/9994 from 12.9810/13.0009, rose against the Indonesian rupiah to 253.8/254.6 from 254.0/254.4, and advanced against the Philippine peso to 7.21/7.24 from 7.22/7.23. However, it edged lower vis-à-vis the Singapore dollar to 3.2603/2687 from 3.2562/2599 at Monday’s close. Related

title: Muted Start For Bursa Despite Cheeding’s Stellar Debut
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened lower this morning, tracking the cautious sentiment across regional markets as investors awaited key US economic data and oil market signals following OPEC+’s latest supply move. At 9.20am, the benchmark FBM KLCI fell 6.07 points to 1,632.02 after touching an intraday high of 1,636.50. The broader market also turned softer, with the FBM70 declining 59 points to 16,955.42, while the FBM Emas Shariah Index slipped 46.60 points to 12,151.11. Market breadth was mixed, with 130 gainers against 76 decliners, and trading volume at 175.55 million shares worth RM188.61 million. Cheeding Holdings Bhd, which made its debut on the ACE Market today, emerged among the top gainers, soaring 39 sen to 75 sen with nearly 95 million shares traded. Other notable gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI), up 42 sen to RM31.42, and Heineken Malaysia (HEIM), which added 14 sen to RM21.20. On the downside, Nestle Malaysia slipped 30 sen to RM97, Kuala Lumpur Kepong (KLK) eased 18 sen to RM20.22, and United Plantations (UTDPLT) dropped 18 sen to RM23.30. Regionally, Singapore’s Straits Times Index rose 0.43% in early trade to 4,440.91, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 futures edged higher to 48,275.00. However, sentiment remained fragile following a modest rebound in oil prices and concerns that US data later this week could influence the Federal Reserve’s policy path. Analysts said Bursa’s cautious start reflected “profit-taking and regional risk recalibration” after recent gains in energy and industrial counters, with trading expected to remain range-bound ahead of Budget 2026 on Friday. body:
Bursa Malaysia remained in negative territory at midday, weighed down by persistent selling in blue-chip counters as regional markets tracked Wall Street’s overnight losses. At 12.30 pm, the FBM KLCI fell 12.33 points or 0.75% to 1,625.76 after moving between 1,624.35 and 1,636.50 earlier in the session. The broader market was also weaker, with the FBMEMAS Index easing 84.47 points to 12,096.45, while the FBM70 dropped 87.76 points to 16,926.66. The FBMSHA Index slid 0.73% to 12,108.49. Market breadth remained negative, reflecting cautious sentiment amid concerns over slower global growth and higher-for-longer US interest rates that continued to weigh on investor appetite across Asia. Among heavyweights, Gamuda shed 21 sen to RM5.26, IHH Healthcare fell 20 sen to RM8.15, and Kluang Rubber Company dropped 20 sen to RM5.50. Meanwhile, Chee Ding Holdings surged 37 sen to 73 sen to top the gainers’ list, followed by Nestlé Malaysia which rose 26 sen to RM97.56, and UMS Holdings which added 21 sen to RM4.99. On the most active list, Borneo Oil and KNM Group were unchanged at half a sen, while Tanco Holdings eased 2.5 sen to 86 sen. Across the region, markets were mostly lower, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 down 0.9%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index declining 0.6%, and Singapore’s Straits Times Index slipping 0.4%, mirroring weaker sentiment ahead of key US economic data releases later this week. title: Japanese Stocks Soar As Asian Market Extends Rally
body:
Japanese stocks hit another record on Tuesday (Oct 7), building on the previous day’s surge following the election of a pro-stimulus advocate to lead the country’s ruling party, while gold also pushed to a new high amid the United States government shutdown and French political upheaval. The election of Sanae Takaichi, who is expected to become Japan’s prime minister this month, came as a surprise but ramped up optimism that she will embark on a campaign on monetary easing.That sent the Nikkei 225 soaring almost 5 per cent on Monday and hammered the yen as investors began questioning the likelihood that the Bank of Japan will continue its interest rate hikes. And the index continued its run-up on Tuesday, while the yen held losses.Takaichi’s victory “removes uncertainty about the country’s policy direction”, said Saxo Markets’ Charu Chanana. “Her agenda is expected to continue a blend of fiscal support and ultra-easy monetary policy. “For investors, that continuity means no abrupt tightening and ongoing coordination between the government and the Bank of Japan.” Yields on 30-year Japanese bonds hit their highest level, reflecting fears the country’s already colossal debt will balloon further. Adding to the buying sentiment was an announcement by Advanced Micro Devices and OpenAI of a partnership to develop AI data centres. The deal comes after OpenAI and US powerhouse Nvidia signed a contract for more than US$100 billion in equipment. And this week, OpenAI struck deals with South Korean semiconductor giants Samsung and SK hynix for chips and other equipment that will be used in its Stargate project. Traders continued their rush into tech firms, which have led a global advance this year that has seen several markets hit record highs. Related

title: Takaichi’s Win Lifts Market Hopes, Yen Slides
body:
Japan’s yen weakened sharply as markets reacted to the ruling Liberal Democratic Party’s decision to elect pro-stimulus lawmaker Sanae Takaichi as its new leader, paving the way for her to become Japan’s first female prime minister. Nikkei stock futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange surged over 4%, reflecting optimism that Takaichi’s expansionary policies will boost demand-driven sectors. The yen slipped as much as 1.4% against the dollar, nearing the key 150 level, and touched record lows versus the euro. Oil prices also advanced after OPEC+ agreed to restore just 137,000 barrels per day of previously halted output — a slower pace than in earlier months — while S&P 500 futures edged higher in tandem. Investors had largely expected the premiership to go to Shinjiro Koizumi, a political scion seen as more fiscally restrained and likely to let the Bank of Japan pursue policy normalisation. In contrast, Takaichi has pushed for fiscal expansion, saying in a Kyodo survey that interest rates should remain unchanged for now. While her stance has bolstered growth expectations, it has raised concerns over potential increases in government bond supply and reduced prospects of a Bank of Japan rate hike this month. “It might be more of a positive surprise for equities,” said cross-asset investment strategist Anna Wu of VanEck Australia. “I won’t be too surprised if the long-end yields go up a bit on Monday, given her overarching fiscal policy,” she added, while noting that Takaichi is unlikely to overstimulate and market volatility should remain limited. Elsewhere in Asia, futures point to modest gains in Australia but slight declines in Hong Kong. Mainland Chinese markets remain closed for the holidays, while Sydney’s public holiday may amplify movements in local trading. In global markets, US equity futures advanced after the S&P 500 ended little changed on Friday amid a tech-led selloff. Bitcoin reached another record high over the weekend, buoyed by optimism around the so-called “Uptober” trend and easing concerns about a US government shutdown. Attention will also turn to Europe, where traders are eyeing French bond futures following President Emmanuel Macron’s decision to retain much of his previous cabinet. Roland Lescure was named finance minister and now faces the challenge of steering the national budget through a divided parliament. The euro slipped early Monday amid a stronger US dollar. title: Stock Today: Solarvest Edges Lower As Analysts Maintain Strong Buy Ratings
body:
Solarvest Holdings Bhd slipped 0.34% to RM2.93 as of 3.50 pm today, with a total traded volume of 1.532 million shares. The counter opened at RM2.95, reaching an intraday high of RM2.96 and a low of RM2.89. Despite the minor dip, both RHB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd have maintained their BUY calls on the company, citing strong earnings visibility following Solarvest’s latest milestone in Sarawak. RHB Research lifted its target price to RM3.58, while HLIB kept its valuation at RM3.50, indicating potential upside of more than 20% from the current level. The positive sentiment is underpinned by Solarvest’s 60% stake in the 100MWac Mukah Solar Powerplant, a first for the company in Borneo. The facility has entered a 30-year power purchase agreement with Syarikat Sesco Sdn Bhd and is expected to commence commercial operations in November 2027. RHB Research projects the plant could contribute an average annual net profit of RM6.5 million, representing up to 9% of the company’s FY2026 earnings. HLIB highlighted that the Mukah project adds around RM300 million worth of EPCC works to Solarvest’s existing RM1.2 billion unbilled orderbook, bringing the company closer to its RM3 billion target by FY2026. The project also increases Solarvest’s effective ownership of utility-scale solar assets to 490MWp, potentially lifting recurring revenue to RM110 million annually. Analysts noted that the expansion positions Solarvest strategically within Sarawak’s renewable energy roadmap, aligning with Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap and the state’s ambition to boost solar capacity to 1.5GW by 2035. title: Stock Today: Sime Darby Property Edges Higher Amid Positive Outlook
body:
Shares of Sime Darby Property Bhd (SDPR) rose slightly in Monday’s afternoon trade, continuing to draw investor interest following upbeat analyst sentiment over its long-term growth prospects. As of 2.48 pm, the counter was up 0.69% or 1 sen to RM1.45, with 5.96 million shares changing hands. It opened at RM1.45, hitting an intraday high of RM1.46 and a low of RM1.43. Last week, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) reaffirmed its BUY call on Sime Darby Property with a target price of RM2.33, suggesting a 62% upside from its last traded price. The research house cited the company’s ongoing transformation into a full-fledged real estate group, with a stronger emphasis on industrial assets and recurring income streams. RHB Research noted that management has intensified its push into the industrial segment through new developments and potential partnerships, while also exploring landbank expansion in Iskandar Malaysia and Malaysian Vision Valley 2.0 (MVV 2.0). The firm added that three key projects, Vision Business Park, Bandar Bukit Raja Business Park and Elmina North, will underpin Sime Darby Property’s industrial property momentum from 2026 onwards, supported by rising demand from Chinese manufacturers seeking facilities in Malaysia. RHB Research maintained that Sime Darby Property’s strategic roadmap, ESG focus and execution strength position it well for sustainable growth, with potential re-rating catalysts coming from new industrial and data centre ventures. title: Stock Today: IHH Healthcare Rises 2.09% On Positive Outlook After India Regulatory Approval
body:
Shares of IHH Healthcare Bhd rose 2.09% to RM8.30 at 11.46 am, extending recent gains as investor sentiment remained buoyant following renewed optimism over its expansion prospects in India. The counter climbed 17 sen from its previous close of RM8.13, with 8.2 million shares traded. It opened at RM8.13 and touched an intraday high of RM8.32 before easing slightly. The buying momentum came after RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) both reaffirmed their BUY calls on IHH, with an upgraded target price of RM9, citing stronger growth potential following regulatory developments in India. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) recently approved for IHH to proceed with its long-delayed mandatory takeover offers (MTO) for Fortis Healthcare Ltd and Fortis Malar Hospitals Ltd, ending a seven-year regulatory overhang. RHB Research said the decision “reopens IHH’s growth story in India”, noting that if the open offers are fully accepted, IHH’s stake in Fortis would rise from 31% to about 57%, cementing its control over the hospital chain. CIMB Securities said the approval “effectively ends a seven-year stalemate”, adding that it raised its target price for IHH to RM9 from RM8.50 after adjusting subsidiary valuations and profit forecasts. Both research houses remain positive on IHH’s long-term outlook, backed by its diversified regional portfolio, strong execution record, and premium positioning across key markets. At current levels, IHH’s share price is up nearly 5% over the past month, reflecting investor confidence in its strategic direction and earnings resilience ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026, which is expected to boost medical tourism. title: Stock Picks: CIMB, Crest, QES And MBSB
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has highlighted CIMB Group Holdings Bhd, Crest Builder Holdings Bhd, QES Group Bhd and Malaysia Building Society Bhd (MBSB) as counters poised for further gains following bullish technical setups. According to its latest technical report, CIMB Group is attempting to extend its upside movement after breaking past the RM7.50 resistance level. The counter printed a bullish candlestick and closed above that level, suggesting that a positive trend is underway. RHB Research expects follow-through price action to test the next resistance at RM8 and subsequently RM8.30, while a drop below RM7.20 would trigger a correction phase. Similarly, Crest Builder is eyeing further gains after staging an upside breakout above the RM0.275 resistance. RHB Research said increasing trading volume in tandem with the price movement reflects strong bullish momentum, which could propel the stock towards RM0.30 and RM0.32. However, a fall below RM0.25 would reverse the upward bias. QES Group also showed signs of extending its bullish trajectory after jumping above the RM0.415 resistance on strong volume. With its 21-day simple moving average line trending upward, RHB Research expects the counter to test RM0.44 and RM0.47 next, provided it stays above the RM0.39 support level. Meanwhile, MBSB may continue its upward trend after breaking past the RM0.755 resistance. The stock, which RHB Research said has gained strong technical momentum, could move towards RM0.775 and RM0.80. A breach below RM0.735, however, would negate the bullish setup and open the door for corrections. Related

title: STI Kicks Off Week In The Green As Asian Markets Rally
body:
Singapore shares opened slightly higher on Monday as regional markets started the week on a positive note, supported by steady sentiment in Asia following gains in Japan and China. At 9.10am, the Straits Times Index (STI) rose 6.42 points or 0.15% to 4,418.37, with 124 gainers against 75 decliners. Turnover stood at 134.37 million securities worth S$108.04 million. Among active counters, DBS gained 0.17% to S$53.03, while UOB traded at S$35.35 and ST Engineering rose to S$8.74. Sembcorp Industries opened at S$6.21, and YZJ Shipbuilding was unchanged at S$3.37. Genting Singapore remained flat at S$0.725. The broader indices also showed resilience, with the iEdge-OCBC Singapore Low Carbon Select 40 Capped Index at 3,615.76, and the iEdge S-REIT Leaders Index steady at 1,134.50. Across the region, Japan’s Nikkei 225 Index Futures climbed to 47,705.00, reflecting sustained investor confidence in Tokyo’s equity market. In China, FTSE China A50 Index Futures edged higher to 15,160.00, suggesting optimism despite ongoing property market concerns. Hong Kong markets were mixed, with the FTSE China H50 Index Futures trading at 18,807.50, while Taiwan’s futures hovered at 2,188.50. Analysts said the STI’s modest rise mirrors the cautious optimism across Asia as investors digest signals of stabilising growth in key economies and monitor upcoming US economic data for clues on future rate moves. Commodities and FX futures on SGX also traded steadily, with total derivatives volume at 29,250 contracts as of 9am. Market watchers expect Singapore equities to continue tracking regional sentiment, with banking and industrial stocks likely to lead near-term movements. Related

title: Ringgit Eases Ahead Of Budget 2026 As Traders Stay Cautious
body:
The ringgit opened slightly weaker against the US dollar as traders turned cautious ahead of the tabling of Budget 2026, with markets closely watching the government’s fiscal deficit targets to be announced later this week. At 8.08 am, the local note eased to 4.2110/2180 against the greenback compared to last Friday’s close of 4.2055/2125. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range of RM4.21 to RM4.22 today as investors await fiscal clues from the budget. “All eyes are on Budget 2026 this week. We expect the government to maintain fiscal discipline, with a further narrowing of the budget deficit next year,” he told a local news outlet, adding that spending is likely to remain stable, supporting domestic demand through both consumption and investment. He said sentiment towards the ringgit should stay broadly positive as the government balances fiscal prudence with measures to stimulate growth. In early trade, the ringgit was mostly higher against major currencies. It strengthened versus the euro to 4.9336/9418 from 4.9360/9442, edged up against the British pound to 5.6571/6665 from 5.6577/6671, and appreciated against the Japanese yen to 2.8158/8206 from 2.8537/8586. However, the local note slipped against most ASEAN currencies. It fell against the Thai baht to 13.0005/0282 from 12.9807/13.0084, weakened versus the Indonesian rupiah to 254.2/254.7 from 253.9/254.4, and eased against the Philippine peso to 7.27/7.29 from 7.26/7.28. The ringgit, however, advanced slightly against the Singapore dollar to 3.2598/2657 from 3.2621/2678. Related
