title: Potential Upside For Solarvest After Sarawak Venture
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both maintained their BUY calls on Solarvest Holdings Bhd, citing strong earnings visibility following the company’s latest milestone in Sarawak. RHB Research raised its target price to RM3.58 from RM3.26, while HLIB maintained its RM3.50 valuation, reflecting a potential upside of more than 20% from the counter’s last traded price of RM2.94. RHB Research said the latest win, the development and operation of a 100MWac large-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) plant in Mukah, Sarawak marks Solarvest’s first asset in Borneo and underscores its growing portfolio of income-generating renewable energy assets. The research house said the project reinforces Solarvest’s position as one of Malaysia’s leading solar players, with its record-high engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) orderbook and robust project pipeline supporting future earnings. Solarvest will hold a 60% stake in Mukah Solar Powerplant (MSP), which has entered into a 30-year power purchase agreement (PPA) with Syarikat Sesco Sdn Bhd, the utility arm of Sarawak Energy, to develop and operate the 100MWac facility. The remaining 40% will be held by Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd. Commercial operation is expected by November 2027, with total capital expenditure estimated at RM380 million, funded mainly through internally generated funds. RHB Research projected that Solarvest could generate an average annual net profit of around RM6.5 million from the project, representing up to 9% of its FY2026 earnings, assuming an internal rate of return (IRR) of 7% to 8% and a debt-to-equity ratio of four times. The expansion, it said, is aligned with the company’s goal of achieving 30% recurring income contribution, with full earnings from the project expected by FY2029. HLIB similarly highlighted that the Mukah project adds about RM300 million worth of EPCC works to Solarvest’s existing unbilled orderbook of RM1.2 billion, bringing the company closer to its RM3 billion target by the end of FY2026. It added that the latest development will increase Solarvest’s effective ownership of utility-scale solar assets to 490MWp from 336MWp previously, potentially lifting recurring revenue to RM110 million annually. The research house also noted that the project strategically positions Solarvest within Sarawak’s renewable energy expansion plan, as the state targets to raise installed generation capacity from 5.7GW to 10GW by 2030 and 15GW by 2035, including 1.5GW of solar capacity. HLIB said Solarvest’s deepening presence in Sarawak is timely, given the state’s growing demand from industries and data centres and its ambition to become a regional renewable energy hub. Both RHB Research and HLIB agreed that Solarvest is well placed to benefit from Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), which supports private sector participation in renewable energy projects. They said Solarvest’s solid execution record, expanding regional footprint and strong partnerships underpin its long-term growth outlook despite potential risks from competition, policy shifts and higher project costs. Solarvest’s stock price decreases 1.36% to RM2.90 as of 10.18 am. Related

title: Market Ends Lower As Decliners Outpace Gainers
body:
The stock market closed on a softer note on Oct 6 as profit-taking pressure weighed on blue chips and mid-cap counters, with overall market breadth turning negative amid cautious regional sentiment. At the closing bell, decliners outnumbered gainers 729 to 403, while 464 counters were unchanged, 968 untraded and seven were suspended. Market turnover slipped to 3.69 billion shares worth RM2.61 billion, from 4.03 billion shares valued at RM2.5 billion recorded on Oct 3. Dealers said investors adopted a defensive stance ahead of key global economic data releases this week, with renewed concerns over US interest rate direction and regional growth outlook dampening risk appetite. Among the top decliners, Heineken Malaysia Bhd shed 36 sen to RM21.06, followed by KSL Holdings Bhd and Petronas Dagangan Bhd, which dropped 34 sen to RM2.99 and RM23.04 respectively. Other notable laggards include Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd, which lost 22 sen to RM31, and Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd, which eased 20 sen to RM16.60. On the flipside, PPB Group Bhd led the advance, rising 30 sen to RM10.52, while Nestlé (M) Bhd gained 28 sen to RM97.30. Petronas Gas Bhd climbed 24 sen to RM18.82, and IHH Healthcare Bhd added 22 sen to RM8.35, supported by continued institutional buying interest in healthcare plays. Technology-related stock PIE Industrial Bhd also rose 23 sen to RM3.49 amid moderate trading volume. Analysts said the local market is expected to stay range-bound in the near term as investors await fresh catalysts from Budget 2026 and US inflation data later this week. The analysts added that sentiment is also expected to be guided by movements in the ringgit and crude oil prices, with global risk appetite still fragile amid monetary policy uncertainty. Related

title: KLCI Inches Higher At Midday As IHH, PPB And PetGas Lift Sentiment
body:
Bursa Malaysia traded in mixed territory at midday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI inching up 1.39 points or 0.09% to 1,636.45 as gains in healthcare and consumer heavyweights helped offset weakness in select blue chips. The index moved between 1,629.93 and 1,637.70 throughout the morning session, reflecting cautious sentiment ahead of global market catalysts and the upcoming Budget 2026 tabling. Broader market tone, however, remained subdued — the FBM 70 lost 0.48% to 17,008.64, while the FBM Emas eased 0.11% to 12,168.78. The Shariah Index (FBM Shariah) slipped marginally by 0.15 points to 12,193.58. On the scoreboard, Petronas Gas and PPB Group were the top gainers, each rising 24 sen to RM18.82 and RM10.46 respectively. IHH Healthcare added 18 sen to RM8.31 after analysts reaffirmed their BUY calls with a higher target price of RM9, citing renewed optimism following the group’s regulatory breakthrough in India. Among laggards, Petronas Dagangan fell 28 sen to RM23.10, Malaysian Pacific Industries (MPI) shed 26 sen to RM30.96, while Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia dropped 18 sen to RM16.62. KNM Group remained the most actively traded counter, with more than 1.9 billion shares exchanging hands at 0.5 sen, followed by NEXG at 52.5 sen and VS Industry at 55.5 sen. Market breadth was negative, in line with regional peers, as investors took a wait-and-see approach amid concerns over slowing global growth and potential policy easing in Asia. At 12.30 pm, total trading volume stood at over 3.8 billion shares worth about RM1.6 billion. Related

title: Hang Seng Index Futures’ Pullback A Breather, Not A Breakdown
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), noting that despite a mild pullback, the overall outlook remains bullish. On Friday, the HSIF retreated 201 points to close at 27,181 points after fluctuating between 27,410 and 27,003 points. During the evening session, it shed another 28 points to 27,153 points, forming a bearish candlestick. RHB Research said the index’s technical setup still supports an upward bias, as it continues to trade above its 20-day and 50-day simple moving average (SMA) lines. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) also remains above the 50% threshold, signalling that bullish momentum persists, though at a slower pace. “The index is consolidating sideways after surpassing the 27,000-point resistance. title: Gold Hits Record High As Safe-Haven Demand Soars
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia climbed sharply in tandem with the global rally, rising 1.37% to RM533.07 per gram as of 3.43 am New York time, according to data from GoldPrice.org. In ringgit terms, the price per kilogram stood at RM533,074.73, up RM7,228.76 from the previous session. The surge reflected strong investor demand for the safe-haven asset amid renewed fears of a US government shutdown and expectations of further interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. Globally, spot gold smashed through the US$3,900 mark for the first time in history, trading at US$3,910.09 per ounce, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.7% to US$3,935, Reuters reported. Over the past year, gold prices in Malaysia have surged 44.38%, while the six-month gain stood at 23.04%. The rally has been further fuelled by a weaker US dollar and growing geopolitical uncertainties, prompting investors to flock to bullion as a hedge against volatility. Silver also saw strong gains, climbing 1.49% to RM3.01 per gram, extending a 48.29% rise over the past year. Analysts said gold’s upward trajectory may continue if the Federal Reserve confirms further monetary easing, with the record high reinforcing its status as a global store of value. Related

title: Bursa Slips As Investors Brace For Budget 2026
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened slightly lower on Monday as investors adopted a cautious stance ahead of the tabling of Budget 2026 later this week, while regional markets traded mixed amid subdued sentiment. At 9.13 am, the benchmark FBM KLCI slipped 1.90 points or 0.12% to 1,633.16, after opening at 1,636.14. The broader market also weakened, with the FBM 70 down 0.16% to 17,063.68 and the FBM Emas Index easing 0.08% to 12,171.90. Market breadth was slightly positive, with 124 gainers and 75 losers, while 134.37 million shares worth RM108.04 million changed hands. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said traders are staying defensive as they await fiscal details that could influence market direction and corporate sentiment. “Investors are looking for clarity on the government’s deficit reduction path and growth measures under Budget 2026. Market movements are likely to remain range-bound until then,” he said. He added that expectations of fiscal discipline, coupled with sustained development spending, could lend medium-term support to equities. Among the most active stocks were KNM (down 2.5 sen to 0.005), NEXG (up 0.5 sen to 0.525), XOXTECH (down 0.5 sen to 0.110) and ERDASAN (up 1 sen to 0.135). Across the region, sentiment was mixed. Singapore’s Straits Times Index gained 0.15% to 4,418.37, buoyed by financial and REIT counters, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 futures edged higher at 47,705.00, reflecting steady optimism in Tokyo markets. China’s FTSE A50 Index Futures slipped 0.2% to 15,160.00 as investors awaited key economic data this week. Analysts noted that while external cues remain moderate, domestic catalysts such as the upcoming budget and expectations of continued infrastructure investment could drive selective buying on the local bourse. The broader market was mixed, with the FBM70 retreating 0.44% to 17,014.42, while the F4GBM index inched up 0.05% to 984.71. Trading was dominated by small-cap activity, with KNM Bhd leading in volume, despite a sharp 0.025 drop to 0.005. Asian peers closed lower as investors digested a series of Chinese manufacturing data, while the Nikkei 225 in Japan gained modestly following encouraging corporate earnings reports. Meanwhile, Wall Street’s S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures pointed to a cautious start on Monday, with investors awaiting US inflation figures later this week, which could influence central bank policy expectations. Analysts highlighted that local investors were also keeping an eye on commodity-linked stocks, given the ongoing movements in crude oil and palm oil markets. title: Weekly Review: Singapore Shares Steady as STI Gains Cautiously
body:
The Singapore Market traded more softly over the week of Sept 29 to Oct 3, as investors turned cautious amid mixed global cues and profit-taking following recent gains. The Straits Times Index (STI) began the week on a steady note, supported by selective buying in financial and industrial counters. However, gains proved fleeting as sentiment weakened midweek, with the benchmark easing to close at 4,411.95 points by Oct 3, reflecting consolidation after a modest rally in prior sessions. Analysts said the local bourse displayed a sideways-to-slightly-negative bias, constrained by global growth concerns and uncertainty surrounding central bank policy paths. Defensive and yield-focused stocks, such as REITs and telecoms, attracted buying interest, while cyclical sectors, including technology and transportation, saw mild selling pressure. Market activity remained subdued, with investors on the sidelines ahead of upcoming economic data releases in the U.S. and China. Broader market performance was mixed, as modest advances in select blue chips were offset by declines in mid-cap and small-cap counters. “Investors are reassessing risk exposure as global markets pause for direction,” one analyst noted, adding that the STI may continue to trade within a narrow band in the near term amid subdued catalysts. Looking ahead, traders are expected to monitor regional PMI data, U.S. inflation prints, and corporate developments for fresh leads. Market observers said a clear move above the 4,450-point resistance could signal renewed momentum, though downside risks persist if external sentiment deteriorates. Related

title: Weekly Recap: Hong Kong Shares End Flat After Mixed Week
body:
Hong Kong stocks ended mixed over the week of Sept 29 to Oct 3, as profit-taking in technology and property counters offset early gains spurred by optimism over potential policy support from Beijing. The Hang Seng Index (HSI) edged lower by 0.4% for the week to close at 27,221.46 points, retreating from intraday highs above 27,800 as investors turned cautious ahead of key economic data from China. The Hang Seng Tech Index also eased after a brief rally earlier in the week, weighed down by weakness in internet and electric vehicle shares. Gains in energy and financial counters provided some cushion, but overall sentiment remained fragile amid lingering concerns over global interest rate trajectories and uneven signs of recovery in the mainland economy. “Investors appear to be in a wait-and-see mode, balancing hopes for fresh Chinese stimulus against caution on global policy uncertainty,” one strategist said, adding that the recent consolidation likely reflects short-term positioning rather than a shift in fundamentals. Market breadth was subdued, with trading volumes thinning ahead of China’s upcoming data releases. Analysts said the market remains supported by expectations of targeted policy easing, though upside could be capped by persistent external headwinds. Looking ahead, market focus will turn to China’s manufacturing and services PMI, property sector announcements, and global inflation data, which could provide cues on regional risk appetite. Analysts added that a decisive move above the 27,500 level could reignite momentum, while weakness below 26,800 may signal renewed downside pressure. Related

title: US Shutdown Sparks Bitcoin Surge to $125,689 Record
body:
Bitcoin has reached a new all-time high, climbing to as much as $125,689 on Sunday in Asia. This surge is part of a wider risk rally sparked by concerns over the US government shutdown, which began on Wednesday. The rise was supported by gains in US equities and renewed inflows into Bitcoin-linked exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Investors are viewing the shutdown as a factor driving demand for safe-haven assets, a trend some market participants refer to as the “debasement trade.” Bitcoin’s performance this year has been strong, gaining more than 30% and exceeding its previous high of $124,514 set on August 14. The largest digital asset by market value has steadily appreciated over the past year, helped by the supportive legislative environment in Washington under President Donald Trump. Public companies, notably Michael Saylor’s Strategy, have boosted demand by stockpiling Bitcoin as a corporate asset, a strategy that has spread to other cryptocurrencies like Ether, lifting digital assets broadly. Joshua Lim, co-head of markets at crypto prime brokerage FalconX, noted that Bitcoin’s rise fits within a broader trend where various assets including equities, gold, and even collectibles like Pokémon cards are hitting record levels, driven by concerns over the weakening value of the US dollar. October is also historically a strong month for Bitcoin, nicknamed “Uptober,” with the token having posted gains in nine of the last ten Octobers. This seasonal pattern adds to the bullish sentiment surrounding the cryptocurrency. US stocks also touched record highs on Friday, driven by major artificial intelligence deals and partnerships, offsetting concerns over a prolonged government shutdown and weak business activity. Treasuries and the dollar fell, while gold was on track for a seventh consecutive weekly gain, bolstered by central bank purchases amid declining US interest rates and ongoing inflation concerns. Geoff Kendrick, global head of digital assets research at Standard Chartered Plc, said the current shutdown could have a greater impact on Bitcoin than previous ones. He noted that during the 2018–2019 shutdown, Bitcoin traded less in line with traditional risk assets, but now it appears to respond more closely to broader market trends. Bloomberg Related

title: Market Review: Seoul Stocks Ease After Record Highs
body:
South Korean shares extended gains over the week of Sept 29 to Oct 3, driven by strong performances in technology and semiconductor stocks, though profit-taking toward the end of the week tempered overall advances. The Kospi benchmark index surged past the 3,500-point level for the first time, reaching an intraday high of 3,549.21 on Oct 2 amid renewed optimism surrounding the AI and chip sectors. Tech giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix led the rally following reports of collaborations with global AI firms, boosting confidence in South Korea’s semiconductor growth prospects. However, momentum eased on Oct 3 as investors booked profits after the sharp gains, with the index ending the week slightly off its highs. Analysts said the mild retreat reflected consolidation after a strong run-up rather than a reversal in sentiment. “Valuations in the tech sector have expanded quickly, and investors are taking a breather ahead of key global data releases,” one strategist said, adding that foreign inflows and export optimism continue to underpin the broader market tone. Gains were broad-based, with chipmakers, battery producers, and industrial exporters leading advances, while automakers and consumer names saw mixed movement. Trading volumes moderated toward the end of the week as investors awaited direction from overseas markets. Looking ahead, market participants are expected to monitor trade figures, global inflation trends, and corporate earnings updates, particularly in the semiconductor space. Analysts noted that while short-term volatility is likely after the recent rally, the medium-term outlook remains supported by robust foreign buying and improving earnings momentum. Related

title: Market Recap: Bursa Malaysia Holds Steady In Sluggish Week
body:
Bursa Malaysia traded on a firmer footing over the week of Sept 29 to Oct 3, supported by gains in energy and solar-related counters, though profit-taking towards the end of the week capped overall advances. The FBM KLCI opened higher on Sept 29 in tandem with upbeat regional sentiment, before edging up 0.06% to close at 1,611.88 points on Sept 30. The benchmark later climbed past 1,637 points midweek, buoyed by strength in renewable energy and refinery stocks following fresh contract announcements and fund inflows. However, the momentum eased on Oct 3 as investors locked in profits after the recent uptrend, with the index retreating 2.74 points, or 0.16%, to 1,635.06. Analysts said the pullback reflected a natural consolidation phase after a steady climb in the preceding sessions. Market participants noted that sentiment remained broadly constructive, underpinned by continued foreign buying and sustained activity in the primary market. As of Sept 30, Bursa Malaysia recorded 41 IPOs raising about RM4.36 billion, reflecting a healthy appetite for domestic equities despite external headwinds. Analysts observed that trading continued to display a sideways-to-positive bias, supported by selective interest in energy, utilities, and large-cap stocks. Nevertheless, lingering global growth concerns and cautious investor positioning limited further upside. Looking ahead, market watchers expect Bursa Malaysia to remain range-bound in the near term, with direction likely guided by global economic data releases, regional market trends, and upcoming domestic policy developments. title: Japanese Markets Eye Gains After Takaichi LDP Win
body:
Japan’s stock market is likely to gain support following the surprise victory of pro-stimulus Sanae Takaichi in the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) leadership election, while the yen and long-term government bonds could come under pressure. Investors and strategists, including those at Pepperstone Group Ltd. and Nomura Securities Co., expect the yield curve to steepen as a result. Takaichi, a strong advocate of easy fiscal and monetary policy, is expected to raise concerns over rising bond issuance, while lowering expectations of a Bank of Japan (BOJ) rate hike later this month. “This was very much a surprise result and not the one that markets had been discounting,” said Michael Brown, senior research strategist at Pepperstone. He added that Takaichi’s win is “likely to be yen negative, on the dovish BOJ repricing, coupled with a steeper JGB curve given her looser fiscal views, though both of those combined should be a boost for the Nikkei.” Takaichi is set to become Japan’s first female prime minister later this month in a parliamentary vote. Investors had expected the leadership to go to political scion Shinjiro Koizumi, who was seen as more fiscally cautious and supportive of BOJ rate normalisation. Bank stocks are likely to struggle amid expectations that rate hikes will be delayed, while domestic demand and small-cap shares could see a “significant tailwind” in the short term, said Richard Kaye, co-head of Japan equity strategy at Comgest Asset Management. Market participants, including foreign investors, are likely to welcome any signs of a return to Abenomics, the economic policies of the late former prime minister Shinzo Abe. As a protege of Abe, Takaichi has advocated for cash handouts and tax rebates to help households grappling with inflation, and has openly supported additional bond issuance to finance fiscal stimulus. Before Takaichi’s win, bond investors had been cautious about fiscal spending, particularly with opposition calls for tax cuts and speculation over BOJ rate hikes. This caution pushed 10-year yields near their highest levels since 2008 and strengthened the yen against the dollar in the past week. Meanwhile, the Nikkei 225 hit a fresh all-time high, benefiting from a global rally in technology stocks. According to Mari Iwashita, executive rates strategist at Nomura Securities, Takaichi’s unexpected victory is likely to revive a market trend characterised by a weaker yen, higher stock prices, and a steeper yield curve. With the prospect of an October BOJ rate hike fading, she expects the central bank to hold off on increasing rates in the near term. However, Rong Ren Goh, fixed income portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments, cautions that any yen weakness resulting from her win may be limited due to narrowing Japan-US interest rate differentials and continued uncertainty over the Federal Reserve’s policy direction. Takaichi faces challenges in implementing her domestic agenda, as her party no longer holds a majority in either house of parliament. She is also expected to face an early diplomatic test with a reported visit from former US President Donald Trump later this month. Looking ahead, Richard Kaye expresses optimism about Japan’s stock market, highlighting that a shift in perception towards Japan could drive new approaches in deregulation, monetary policy, and Japan-US trade relations. He suggests this could mark a turning point and present a significant opportunity for the country. Bloomberg Related

title: Wall Street Posts Record Weekly Gains as Dow and S&P 500 Close at New Highs
body:
Dow and S&P 500 hit record closing highs on Friday, while the Nasdaq fell in a volatile session, Reuters reported. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 238.56 points, or 0.51%, closing at 46,758.28. The S&P 500 eked out a gain of 0.44 points, or 0.01%, to 6,715.79, marking a record closing high despite choppy trading. However, the Nasdaq Composite slipped 63.54 points, or 0.28%, to 22,780.51. Market sentiment was bolstered by expectations of potential interest rate cuts from the Federal Reserve amid ongoing concerns that the U.S. government shutdown was entering its third day. The shutdown delayed the release of key economic data, such as September’s U.S. nonfarm payrolls report. Still, a separate survey from the Institute for Supply Management showed continued contraction in services employment, reinforcing hopes for easing rates. Sector-wise, the S&P 500 technology sector softened, with Applied Materials shares dropping 2.7% after the company forecasted a $600 million revenue hit for fiscal 2026. Tesla shares declined 1.4%, while utilities led the day’s sector gains, rising 1.2%. For the week, the Dow and S&P 500 both rose 1.1%, while the Nasdaq gained 1.3%. Despite a typical market resilience to government shutdowns, strategists caution that a prolonged closure could delay or obscure crucial economic data, impacting investment decisions and Federal Reserve policy. Elsewhere, USA Rare Earth jumped 14.3% after its CEO said the company was in close contact with the White House. Market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by a 1.72-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. Trading volume reached 20.47 billion shares, above the 20-day average of 19.01 billion. While shutdowns have historically had limited market impact, some strategists cautioned that a prolonged closure could delay key economic data and complicate Fed policy decisions. “The market generally looks past government shutdowns,” said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial. “But the longer it goes… it could cloud some of the data we will eventually get because the collection wasn’t happening.” Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, meanwhile, signalled caution on committing to a series of rate cuts, citing persistent inflation pressures. title: Wall Street Left Waiting as Payroll Data Frozen by US Shutdown
body:
The typically unmissable U.S. jobs data release will not happen this Friday due to the government shutdown, leaving traders with unexpected free time but also a challenge in reading the economic landscape. With deep partisan divisions preventing a funding deal, the U.S. Labour Department has suspended its economic data releases, including the closely watched monthly employment report. This disruption has quietened trading floors and investment firms that normally focus intently on the jobs report at 8:30 am. Michael Brown, a senior research strategist in London, joked that Friday now “has all the makings of a rather long lunch,” highlighting how the usual suspense has vanished. Matthew Miskin, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments, noted the unusual calm, saying it would be a relief for market watchers not to have their eyes glued to the screen waiting for the report. The absence of payroll data—the so-called “king of the numbers”—is particularly striking given its importance. Investors rely heavily on labour market statistics to gauge the Federal Reserve’s potential moves on interest rates. Recent volatility, including a surprise weak jobs report that led to the firing of a top Labour Department official by President Donald Trump, has made this data even more crucial. Beyond trading desks, the jobs report fuels widespread discussion on social media. Typically, tens of thousands of posts tagged #NFP flood platforms around the release, reflecting intense public and professional interest. Without the data, regular contributors like Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, say they will have an unusually quiet morning, while others warn that missing data could increase market uncertainty. James Cordier, a veteran commodities trader, cautions that if the data drought extends beyond mid-October, some traders may have to close positions early due to excessive risk. Karl Schamotta, chief market strategist at Corpay, warns that the void may be filled with misleading rumours and incomplete private data, potentially causing overreactions in the markets. This shutdown-driven data gap is reminiscent of the last government shutdown in 2013 that delayed the employment report by weeks. Until the government reopens fully, investors and traders alike must navigate heightened uncertainty without one of their most critical economic indicators. Reuters Related

title: Oil Prices Slide 8% Weekly Amid Expected OPEC+ Supply Boost
body:
Oil prices posted an 8.1% weekly loss despite settling higher on Friday amid news of potential increases in OPEC+ supply. Brent crude futures closed up 42 cents, or 0.7%, at $64.53 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 40 cents, or 0.7%, to $60.88. However, both benchmarks faced their highest weekly declines in over three months, with Brent down 8.1% and WTI tumbling 7.4%. The expected increase in OPEC+ production, combined with the resumption of flows from the Iraq/Kurdish pipeline after a two-year shutdown, is maintaining selling pressure on crude. Eight OPEC+ countries are to raise output in November, with Saudi Arabia advocating a significant boost to regain market share, while Russia favors a more moderate rise. Analysts warn that higher OPEC+ supply, alongside seasonal drops in demand and ongoing refinery maintenance, will weigh on oil market sentiment. Rystad Energy highlighted weakening demand indicators in the Atlantic Basin as summer ends, pointing to an over-supplied market from October onwards. JPMorgan also forecasted a turning point in September, anticipating a sizeable oil surplus through the fourth quarter and into next year. Additional downward pressure came from U.S. data showing higher crude, gasoline and distillate inventories last week, as refinery activity and demand softened, the Energy Information Administration reported. Oilfield services firm Baker Hughes stated producers cut two rigs this week, bringing the total oil rig count down to 422. Separately, a fire broke out overnight at Chevron’s El Segundo refinery in California, one of the largest on the U.S. West Coast. Local officials said the blaze was contained to one area, and analysts noted the incident was unlikely to have a significant impact on the wider oil market. Reuters Related

title: Kospi Climbs 2.7% Ahead of Chuseok Holiday on Tech Optimism
body:
Seoul shares closed sharply higher on Oct 2, with the benchmark KOSPI jumping 2.7% (93.38 points) to 3,549.21, lifted by gains across heavyweight technology and financial stocks. The index opened at 3,525.48 and traded firmly higher through the session, touching an intraday peak of 3,565.96 — also its 52-week high — before paring back slightly into the close. The rally was driven primarily by significant gains in semiconductor stocks, notably Samsung Electronics, which surged over 4%, and SK Hynix, which soared nearly 11%, following reports of a new partnership with OpenAI to supply advanced memory chips for AI data centers. This collaboration highlights South Korea’s pivotal role in the global artificial intelligence supply chain. Despite stronger inflation data showing consumer prices rose 2.1% in September—above market expectations—investors remained optimistic about the technology sector’s prospects and the overall market outlook. The KOSPI’s gains reflect a broader trend of robust growth, with the index up over 11% in the past month and more than 38% year-on-year. With the upcoming Chuseok holiday closure from October 3 through October 9, market participants positioned themselves ahead of the break, balancing enthusiasm from corporate developments with caution over inflation and policy implications from the Bank of Korea. Looking ahead, investors will closely watch economic data releases and the central bank’s policy stance as they navigate the balance between supporting economic growth and maintaining price stability. title: Wall Street Climbs To Fresh Highs On Tech Momentum
body:
US stocks extended their record-breaking run on Thursday, driven by gains in technology shares despite political headwinds from the government shutdown. The S&P 500 inched up 0.1% while the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.4%, both reaching new highs. The rally was bolstered by an OpenAI share sale valuing the company at US$500 billion, which spurred demand for chip stocks. “Tech momentum shows no sign of fading — as if gravity doesn’t exist — with headwinds brushed aside and every AI headline sparking bursts of euphoria,” said Hebe Chen, analyst at Vantage Markets in Melbourne. Treasuries edged higher, with the 10-year yield easing to around 4.08%, while the dollar strengthened 0.1% after three days of losses. title: Tech Surge Lifts Nikkei As US Rate-Cut Hopes Offset Shutdown Fears
body:
Tokyo’s Nikkei led Asian equities higher on Friday (Oct 3), rising 1.9% as investors headed into the weekend, buoyed by hopes of further US rate cuts despite a partial government shutdown in Washington. Other regional markets, including Sydney, Singapore, Bangkok, Wellington, Taipei, Jakarta and Manila, also closed higher, while Hong Kong fell 1% after gaining over 4% in the previous three sessions. Shanghai remained closed for a holiday. The rally has been largely driven by massive investment in artificial intelligence, pushing valuations of major tech firms to record levels, with Nvidia surpassing US$4 trillion. Recent news of South Korean chipmakers Samsung and SK hynix striking a preliminary deal with OpenAI for its Stargate project added momentum to the sector. On Friday, Japan’s Hitachi announced a strategic partnership with OpenAI to collaborate on AI and energy projects, sending its shares up more than 9%. Renesas followed with a similar gain, while Sony rose 2.8%, Advantest over 3%, and SoftBank more than 3%. Data suggesting a slowdown in the US labour market has further fuelled the rally, signalling the Federal Reserve may continue cutting borrowing costs. Analysts noted that the government shutdown, which has halted some services and delayed key jobs data, is unlikely to prevent the Fed from a second rate cut this month. Pepperstone’s Chris Weston said, “The shutdown could shave US$15-$20 billion off US GDP, but it will largely be backfilled and should have only a negligible lasting impact.” In company news, Japanese brewer Asahi fell more than 1% after a cyberattack disrupted its ordering and delivery system, forcing production stoppages at several factories. Shares have dropped around 7% this week. The positive sentiment has also lifted bitcoin, which regained levels above US$120,000 for the first time since mid-August, when it reached a record US$124,515. AFP Related

title: Stock Today: TNB Eases Despite Tax Win By Subsidiary
body:
Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) traded slightly lower on morning despite news that its subsidiary Southern Power Generation Sdn Bhd (SPG) had won a judicial review against the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN) over RM78.49 million in additional tax assessments. As at 11.35 am, TNB slipped 0.15% or two sen to RM13.44, with 2.4 million shares changing hands. The stock opened at RM13.50, touched a high of RM13.50, and dipped to a low of RM13.32. Market interest showed 8,900 shares queued to buy at RM13.44, against 58,900 shares on the selling side at RM13.46. On Thursday, TNB disclosed in a Bursa Malaysia filing that the High Court had ruled in favour of SPG, which operates two 720-megawatt combined cycle gas turbine power plants in Johor. SPG, 70% owned by TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd, successfully argued that the LHDN had no legal basis to issue the disputed tax notices. The tax assessments, dated 26 May 2023, covered the years of assessment 2017 to 2021. Collectively, they amounted to RM78.49 million. Despite the favourable ruling, TNB’s share price reaction remained muted, with investors likely eyeing broader market sentiment and utility sector trends. Related

title: Stock Today: SunCon Dips Slightly Amid Strong Sector Outlook
body:
Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SUNCON) closed at RM5.94 on Friday, down 9 sen or 1.49% from its previous close, with a total trading volume of 1.24 million shares. The counter opened at RM6.01, reaching a high of RM6.04 and a low of RM5.90 during the session. Despite the minor setback, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) maintains an OVERWEIGHT stance on the construction sector, reaffirming its BUY rating on Sunway Construction with a target price of RM6.70. The research house highlighted that domestic contract awards remained robust in the first nine months of 2025, rising 24% year-on-year to RM39.7 billion, marking the highest level since 2016. HLIB noted that data centres and public sector projects including roads, railways, and water infrastructure, were key drivers of the sector. While third-quarter awards fell 16% quarter-on-quarter to RM10.7 billion, full-year projections remain strong, with expected contract awards around RM50 billion for 2025, up from RM44.2 billion in 2024. The quarter also saw significant wins, such as Gamuda’s RM2.14 billion data centre project in Puncak Alam and a RM1.13 billion Northern Coastal Highway contract in Sarawak through a joint venture with Naim Holdings. IJM Corp secured a RM1.4 billion hyperscale data centre project in Johor. HLIB expects the construction momentum to carry into the final quarter, with pending data centre contracts, East Malaysian road projects, renewable energy EPCC jobs, and Penang LRT subcontract packages potentially boosting activity. Large-scale water project awards are anticipated in 2026. While commercial and residential projects softened due to the removal of the SST exemption for construction services in July, HLIB projects the sector’s growth cycle to extend into 2026, supported by delayed mechanical, electrical, and plumbing works for data centres, though risks remain from slower property activity, potential AI chip demand restrictions, and subsidy rationalisation. title: Ringgit Rises On Fed Policy Bets Amid US Shutdown Concerns
body:
The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, lifted by expectations that a prolonged US government shutdown could pressure the Federal Reserve (Fed) into easing monetary policy. At 8 am, the local note rose 30-pip to 4.2010/2150 from Thursday’s close of 4.2040/2090. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar-ringgit exchange rate was likely to remain steady, trading between 4.20 and 4.22 during the day. “Market participants expect economic uncertainty from the shutdown to pressure the Fed to cut interest rates in the coming months, easing demand for the greenback and supporting emerging market currencies such as the ringgit,” he told Bernama. He added that traders and investors are increasingly turning to private company surveys of the labour market to gauge economic conditions following the suspension of official data. Mohd Afzanizam recalled that the longest US shutdown, which lasted from Dec 22, 2018 to Jan 25, 2019, reduced US gross domestic product growth by 0.1 and 0.2 percentage points in the fourth quarter of 2018 and the first quarter of 2019, respectively. In early trade, the ringgit was also firmer against major currencies. It strengthened to 4.9248/9412 versus the euro from 4.9410/9468, advanced against the British pound to 5.6482/6671 from 5.6741/6809, and climbed to 2.8543/8640 against the Japanese yen from 2.8669/8705. Performance against ASEAN peers was mixed. The ringgit appreciated to 12.9409/9920 versus the Thai baht from 12.9829/13.0040, and firmed against the Singapore dollar to 3.2596/2707 from 3.2665/2707. It was unchanged at 253.0/254.0 against the Indonesian rupiah from 253.2/253.6, and flat at 7.23/7.26 against the Philippine peso from 7.23/7.25. Related

title: Gold Rises To RM523 per Gram, Tracks Global Upswing
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia climbed to RM523.18 per gram on Friday, up RM3.35 or 0.64%, in line with gains seen across global markets. Per kilogram, the metal was priced at RM523,176.01, while on a per-ounce basis, gold stood at RM16,272.59. In the past 30 days, gold in Malaysia has risen 7.82%, while on a one-year basis it surged 44.68%. Over a five-year span, prices have more than doubled, advancing 103.3%. Comparatively, international markets also showed strong momentum. Year-to-date, gold in US dollar terms has advanced 46.5%, with significant gains also seen in the Australian dollar (+37.4%), Canadian dollar (+42.1%) and Indian rupee (+51.9%). In euro terms, prices rose 29.4%, while in Japanese yen, the metal added 37%. Silver prices in Malaysia also registered a notable increase, rising 1.91% today to RM3.74 higher. Over six months, silver surged nearly 47%, mirroring gold’s strong performance. Gold’s rally has been fuelled by persistent geopolitical uncertainties, currency volatility and sustained investor demand for safe-haven assets. Related

title: Bursa Opens Softer In Cautious Regional Trade
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened lower as the FBM KLCI slipped 3.81 points or 0.23% to 1,633.99, tracking the cautious tone across Asian markets after Wall Street eased from record highs. The broader market was also softer, with the FBM70 down 0.05% to 17,063.78, the FBMEMAS shedding 0.16% to 12,170.60 and the F4GBM easing 0.19% to 983.31. The Shariah Index dipped 0.08% to 12,212.53. Market activity was led by small-cap counters. Sarawak Consolidated Industries (SCIB) surged 21% to 21 sen on heavy volumes, while TWL Holdings edged up 0.005 to 3 sen. NexG Bina and Borneo Oil were actively traded at 9.5 sen and 0.5 sen respectively, while Zetrix slipped marginally to 85 sen. The softer open mirrored moves in regional markets. Futures in Japan’s Nikkei 225, Taiwan and China’s A50 all showed mild declines, while Singapore’s Straits Times Index fell 0.43% in early trade. The weakness followed a pullback in the US overnight as investors turned cautious ahead of upcoming economic data and OPEC+ supply decisions. Analysts noted that while market sentiment remains supported by Wall Street’s recent strength, profit-taking across Asia suggests investors are seeking fresh catalysts before taking on more risk. title: Asian Stocks Seen Lower As Markets Pause After Wall Street Rally
body:
Asian equities were set for a weaker open on Friday, with futures in Australia, Japan and Hong Kong pointing lower, suggesting global stocks may take a breather after Wall Street’s record-setting performance. The softer start comes amid lingering concerns over supply imbalances in oil markets and political risks in the US. Markets in China and South Korea remain closed for holidays. Traders will focus on regional data including S&P Global PMIs for Australia and Singapore, as well as Japan’s jobless rate. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda is also scheduled to speak in Osaka, which may provide clues on the central bank’s stance as markets digest signs of slowing global demand. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent meanwhile signalled optimism on US-China trade talks, predicting a “pretty big breakthrough” in the next round. However, investors remain cautious as the prolonged US government shutdown threatens to delay key economic releases, including nonfarm payrolls. Bloomberg Related

title: Winning Full NYC Gambling License Could Boost Genting’s Fair Value
body:
CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained its HOLD call on Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) with an unchanged sum-of-parts (SOP) based target price of RM2.15, as its wholly owned Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) moves closer to securing one of three Downstate New York (DNY) full casino licences. The brokerage noted that RWNYC received unanimous approval from the Community Advisory Committee (CAC) on 25 September to redevelop its existing slots facility into a US$5.5 billion (RM23.1 billion) integrated resort. The approval followed overwhelming support at two public hearings, leaving RWNYC among just four remaining applicants vying for the licences. Other shortlisted contenders include MGM’s Empire City Casino, Bally’s Bronx and Steve Cohen-Hard Rock’s Metropolitan Park, while four other proposals were rejected. The Gaming Facility Location Board (GFLB) will now evaluate submissions based on criteria such as economic activity and business development, which carry a 70% weighting. CIMB Securities believes RWNYC has an edge over rivals due to its ability to begin offering table games within six months of receiving a licence, a full year ahead of MGM and several years ahead of new entrants. RWNYC’s proposed development also stands out in scale, with plans to feature 6,000 slots, 800 tables, 2,000 hotel rooms, a 7,000-seat entertainment venue, more than 30 food and beverage outlets and extensive convention space by 2030, making it the largest integrated resort in the United States. The decision by the GFLB is expected by 1 December, with licences issued by the Gaming Commission by year-end. CIMB Securities estimates that winning a full casino licence could boost GENM’s fair value by 52 sen per share, equivalent to a 24% upside to its target price. In terms of financing, RWNYC’s remaining US$3.9 billion (RM16.4 billion) investment, after accounting for US$1.1 billion already spent, is projected to be deployed over 2026–2030, averaging US$780 million (RM3.3 billion) per year. CIMB Securities expects 70% of this to be debt-funded, with the remainder to be covered by RWNYC’s internally generated funds. Additional support could also come from potential asset disposals, such as the sale of GENM’s Miami land, although the timing remains uncertain. However, the research house cautioned that GENM may skip paying dividends in FY2025 and FY2026 to conserve cash, potentially saving RM567 million annually. Its earnings outlook also remains subdued in the near term, with core net profit projected to fall to RM367 million in FY2025 before recovering gradually in FY2026–2027. CIMB Securities concluded that while RWNYC’s casino licence bid offers significant upside potential, the risks of dividend suspension and execution challenges warrant a neutral stance. GENM’s shares closed at RM2.12, just shy of the target price of RM2.15. Genting Malaysia’s stock price is currently down by 0.47% as of 9.58 am to RM2.110. Related

title: Tech Surge Lifts Asia As Weak US Jobs Data Fuels Fed Cut Bets
body:
Asian stock markets advanced on Thursday, led by technology shares, while gold hovered close to record highs and the dollar remained subdued, as weak US labour data bolstered expectations of interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. The Philadelphia SE semiconductor index jumped more than 2 per cent overnight, lifting Wall Street to fresh records and setting the tone for Asia. Japan’s Nikkei gained about 0.5 per cent, Taiwan’s tech-heavy bourse rose 1.5 per cent, and South Korea’s KOSPI climbed 2.8 per cent after Samsung and Hynix announced partnerships to supply OpenAI data centres. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng added 0.5 per cent. The rally came after the private ADP employment report showed the US economy unexpectedly shed jobs in September, with August figures also revised lower. The data convinced traders that quarter-point rate cuts at the Fed’s final two meetings this year were all but certain, despite the US government shutdown halting the release of the official payrolls report on Friday. “The ADP report suggests the US economy is in almost dire need for further policy support,” said Kyle Rodda, analyst at Capital.com. “As a result, the markets are discounting a much higher probability of rate cuts in October and December.” Rodda added that the shutdown itself had little immediate impact. “After some initial jitters, the markets shrugged off the US government shutdown, at least for now. Historically, the impact of shutdowns has been trivial, although the delay of critical economic data could increase uncertainty about the path forward for US monetary policy – and therefore lift volatility,” he said. The shutdown began on Wednesday after political gridlock in Washington prevented Congress and the White House from reaching a funding deal, threatening a prolonged standoff. Meanwhile, gold surged to a new record of US$3,895.09 an ounce overnight before easing to around US$3,865. US Treasury yields fell sharply, with the two-year yield dropping to 3.531 per cent in Tokyo trading, its lowest in two weeks. The dollar index languished near a one-week low of 97.459, last seen at 97.672. The greenback steadied at 147.01 yen after a three-day slide, while the euro edged up to US$1.1738 and sterling rose to US$1.34835. Oil prices also found support, with Brent crude futures gaining 0.2 per cent to US$65.50 a barrel and US West Texas Intermediate crude climbing 0.2 per cent to US$61.92, as markets weighed the potential of tighter sanctions on Russian crude. Reuters Related

title: Singapore Market Opens In Green, Echoing Asian Uptrend
body:
Singapore shares started on a positive note, with the Straits Times Index (STI) rising 14.71 points or 0.34% to 4,337.83 at 9.03 am. Market breadth was firm, with 108 advancers outpacing 59 decliners, while trading volume stood at 124.61 million units worth S$110.06 million. Among the index heavyweights, DBS gained 0.29% to S$51.73, UOB traded at S$34.74, and OCBC held steady at S$16.50. Singtel was flat at S$4.16, while Keppel opened at S$9.00. The positive tone on SGX tracked overnight gains on Wall Street, where the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both closed higher despite lingering concerns over the US government shutdown. Treasuries rallied and investors priced in the likelihood of more Federal Reserve rate cuts later this year. Across the region, sentiment was broadly upbeat. Futures pointed higher in Japan and Australia, while Hong Kong resumed trading after a holiday with the Hang Seng expected to open firmer. Meanwhile, Chinese markets remained closed, limiting direct cues from the mainland. Derivatives trading on SGX also reflected cautious optimism, with the FTSE China A50 Index Futures last quoted at 15,153, while the Nikkei 225 Futures held firm at 44,805. Investors will keep an eye on regional macro data releases including South Korea’s inflation and Australia’s trade figures, which may set the tone for the rest of the session. Related

title: Ringgit Strengthens As US Shutdown Weighs on Dollar
body:
The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday, buoyed by sustained buying interest amid the United States’ first government shutdown in nearly seven years. At 8.02 am, the local note stood firmer at 4.2000/2100 against the greenback compared with Wednesday’s close of 4.2045/2095. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the shutdown has curtailed key US government services, including the release of statistical data. “The key question is how quickly the impasse between Republicans and Democrats over spending programmes and concessions can be resolved. In the meantime, the shutdown is dollar-negative. The dollar-ringgit could make another attempt to pierce the RM4.20 psychological level today,” he told Bernama. The ringgit was broadly stronger against major currencies in early trade. It gained to 4.9279/9396 versus the euro from 4.9327/9386 on Wednesday, edged up to 5.6603/6738 against the British pound from 5.6605/6672, and firmed to 2.8542/8612 versus the Japanese yen from 2.8561/8597. Regionally, the local currency also advanced, strengthening to 3.2611/2694 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2623/2665, while climbing to 12.9478/9870 against the Thai baht from 12.9929/13.0128. It also appreciated to 7.22/7.24 versus the Philippine peso from 7.23/7.24, and inched up to 252.4/253.2 against the Indonesian rupiah from 252.7/253.1. Related

title: PetGas Reorganisation Plan Should Lead To Greater Shareholder Value
body:
MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained its Neutral call on PETRONAS Gas Bhd (PETGAS) with an unchanged target price of RM19.25, noting that while the company’s internal reorganisation is expected to bring long-term operational and shareholder benefits, the near-term impact on earnings remains minimal. PETGAS announced it had received approval from the Ministry of Finance for a tax exemption to facilitate the restructuring of its business segments into regulated and non-regulated activities through a members’ scheme of arrangement. Under the plan, the company will transfer its gas transportation, gas processing and utilities operations into wholly owned subsidiaries via business transfer agreements. The gas transportation arm will be moved to PG Transco Sdn Bhd, gas processing to PG Gas Processing Sdn Bhd, and the utilities business to PG Utilities East Sdn Bhd, which falls under holding company PG Energia Sdn Bhd. The group expects to make the necessary application within three months, with completion targeted for the third quarter of 2026, barring any unforeseen delays. According to MBSB Research, the exercise is aimed at streamlining operations, reducing redundancies and optimising processes, which will ultimately allow PETGAS to better focus on regulatory and compliance standards. The analysts added that the restructuring will enhance transparency and accountability across divisions, as each unit will be required to manage its own operational and financial records. This, they said, will provide clearer visibility into the performance of individual segments. title: Near-Term Cost For KPJ’s Latest Digitalisation Efforts
body:
MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has maintained a NEUTRAL call on KPJ Healthcare Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM2.65, noting that the group’s latest move to adopt a secure digital communication platform aligns with its broader digitalisation strategy but carries operational and cost-related risks. The research house said KPJ will implement NetSfere’s secure communication system across all 30 of its hospitals, following an initial rollout at its Pasir Gudang and Ampang Puteri specialist facilities. The platform provides healthcare professionals with encrypted messaging, voice and video calls, secure file sharing and administrative controls designed to comply with the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) and international healthcare standards. MBSB Research highlighted that NetSfere, hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), is a global provider of enterprise messaging and collaboration solutions often adopted in highly regulated industries such as healthcare. The system is also designed to meet international regulatory frameworks, including HIPAA, GDPR and SOX, while ensuring that complete data is stored within Malaysia in line with local requirements. The research firm said the initiative supports KPJ’s ongoing efforts to enhance hospital management and patient experience through digitalisation. By replacing consumer-grade messaging apps with a compliant and secure alternative, the platform is expected to streamline clinical workflows while allowing the use of personal devices, which could help the group optimise hardware costs. However, MBSB Research cautioned that such platforms come with potential challenges. These include stringent protocols that may slow urgent communication, the need for staff training during the transition, risks of information overload, high implementation and maintenance costs, as well as IT management complexities for personal devices. Cybersecurity threats remain a persistent risk, though the analysts noted NetSfere’s enterprise-grade security should provide sufficient safeguards. As digitalisation forms part of KPJ’s long-term strategic plan, the analysts said the adoption of NetSfere had already been factored into their valuation. With no material changes to earnings forecasts, the Neutral call and RM2.65 target price remain unchanged. KPJ Healthcare’s stock price is down 0.72% to RM2.770. Related

title: MPI Leads Bursa Advances
body:
Malaysian stocks closed largely higher, with MPI [S] emerging as the top gainer, climbing RM2.84 to RM31.74, followed by SAM [S] (+RM0.37 to RM4.28) and TENAGA (+RM0.36 to RM13.46). Other notable performers included ALLIANZ (+RM0.34 to RM18.74) and IHH [S] (+RM0.32 to RM8.26), driven by strong buying interest in healthcare, utilities, and industrial segments. On the downside, NESTLE [S] led the losers, slipping RM0.28 to RM97.12, followed by AJI (-RM0.16 to RM13.82) and F&N (-RM0.16 to RM27.24). HLIND (-RM0.12 to RM13.88) and HUMEIND (-RM0.11 to RM3.32) also posted declines. The session reflected broader regional trends, as investors weighed mixed signals from Chinese and US markets. While Asian peers including Hong Kong’s Hang Seng (+0.7%) and Taiwan’s TAIEX (+0.5%) advanced, commodity-linked and consumer staples stocks faced profit-taking pressure. Trading activity remained focused on liquid counters, with MPI seeing 21.85 million shares exchanged, SAM 46.90 million, and TENAGA 78.74 million shares, signalling continued investor appetite for blue-chip and resilient sectors. title: Markets Scale New Highs As Investors Downplay US Shutdown Risks
body:
Global equities surged to record levels on Wednesday, as traders shrugged off the first United States government shutdown in almost seven years and placed stronger bets on further interest rate cuts from the Federal Reserve. The S&P 500 rose 0.3% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 added 0.5%, lifting both indices alongside an MSCI global benchmark to fresh highs. The rally extended into Asia, with early Thursday trading showing gains in futures for Australia, Japan and Hong Kong. Treasuries advanced after a weaker-than-expected private payrolls report suggested the labour market is cooling, reinforcing speculation that the Fed will ease policy further. The 10-year yield slipped five basis points to about 4.1%. Gold inched up to a new peak, while the dollar held steady. “The market is going to have to focus on independent private sources to get a sense of what’s going on,” said Brij Khurana, portfolio manager at Wellington Management, noting that the shutdown could delay crucial government data. The ADP report revealed an unexpected fall in September payrolls at US companies, adding to signs of labour market softness. Factory activity contracted for a seventh consecutive month, according to ISM figures. Traders increased wagers on two more Fed rate cuts this year, with Berenberg economist Atakan Bakiskan saying officials would have “enough information about the labour market” to deliver another 25-basis-point reduction in October even if nonfarm payroll data is delayed. While investors remained calm over Washington’s political standoff, concerns are mounting about the possibility of prolonged disruption. Vice President JD Vance told reporters he did not expect the shutdown to last long, though he cautioned layoffs would follow if it extends beyond days. White House Budget Director Russell Vought indicated non-essential federal staff could be swiftly dismissed. Analysts noted this shutdown carries unique risks. “What sets this shutdown apart is the threat of permanent layoffs for non-essential federal staff, which, while possibly political bluster and subject to legal challenges, could prolong the drag on public sector payrolls,” said Thomas Ryan, North America economist at Capital Economics. Still, some strategists remain unfazed. Citigroup’s head of US equity trading strategy Stuart Kaiser said equity markets are unlikely to be hit unless the shutdown drags on significantly, creates large-scale job losses or triggers instability in bond markets. In the corporate sector, BYD Co. reported its first monthly sales decline in more than a year and a half. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix secured initial deals to supply chips and equipment for OpenAI’s Stargate artificial intelligence project. Oil prices slipped after a volatile session as investors weighed prospects of OPEC+ accelerating output increases, even as US crude inventories expanded. West Texas Intermediate hovered at US$61.70 a barrel, while Brent settled near US$65. Gold traded around US$3,860 an ounce. Bitcoin rose slightly to US$117,893, while Ether fell to US$4,320. Former Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers cautioned that the shutdown fight was “all about the future of American healthcare,” warning that millions could face losing access to affordable coverage if political brinkmanship deepens. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Poised To Test 27,000 Resistance
body:

title: Global Market Rally As Asia, Europe, And Wall Street Extend Gains
body:
Major stock markets across Asia, Europe, and the United States traded higher on Thursday, buoyed by improving investor sentiment amid hopes of further monetary easing in the U.S. and optimism surrounding global growth drivers such as technology and trade. Asia-Pacific markets started the day on a positive note, with most key indices opening higher. In Japan, the Nikkei 225 advanced 185.18 points, or 0.42%, to 44,736.03, extending its strong momentum as investors shrugged off concerns over potential rate hikes by the Bank of Japan. South Korea’s KOSPI surged 2.02% at the open to 3,525.48, lifted by robust demand in technology and semiconductor stocks. Elsewhere, Australia’s benchmark S&P/ASX 200 rose 1.19% to 8,951.10, supported by gains in mining and energy counters, while Singapore’s Straits Times Index opened 0.36% higher at 4,338.50. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index added 0.23% to 26,918.30, as optimism around Chinese tech companies outweighed persistent concerns over the property sector. Trading in mainland Chinese markets, however, remained closed for the holiday period. On Wall Street, all three major indices ended at record highs overnight. The S&P 500 gained 22.74 points, or 0.34%, to close at 6,711.20, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 43.21 points, or 0.09%, to 46,441.10. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite advanced 95.15 points, or 0.42%, to finish at 22,755.16. The rally came on the back of softer U.S. economic data, including weaker job market signals, which bolstered expectations for two potential interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve later this year. Investors also appeared to discount short-term risks from a potential U.S. government shutdown, betting instead on policy easing to sustain economic momentum. European bourses also mirrored the positive trend. Germany’s DAX Index climbed 232.90 points, or 0.98%, to settle at 24,113.62, led by industrial and automotive names. London’s FTSE 100 advanced 96.00 points, or 1.03%, to 9,446.43, while France’s CAC 40 rose 71.01 points, or 0.90%, to close at 7,966.95. The broad gains came as eurozone inflation showed further signs of cooling, raising expectations that the European Central Bank may hold off on additional tightening. Outlook : Analysts say the latest upswing in global equities reflects improving risk appetite, driven by optimism around central bank policy pivots, a resilient global economy, and continued strength in technology and energy. However, they caution that risks remain, including U.S.-China trade frictions, geopolitical uncertainties, and the trajectory of crude oil prices Related

title: Dollar Falls As Traders Assess Govt Shutdown, Poor Jobs Data
body:
The dollar fell to near a one-week low on Thursday as traders weighed the impact of a U.S. government shutdown, while poor jobs data boosted expectations the Federal Reserve will cut interest rates two more times this year. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of six currencies, fell 0.2 per cent to 97.52.After four straight days of losses for the dollar, traders were weighing how long the U.S. government shutdown might last, its effect on economic data releases, and how that will play into the Fed’s decision making. The ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday that U.S. private employment shrank by 32,000 jobs last month after a downwardly revised 3,000 decline in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast private employment to increase by 50,000.”U.S. ADP employment data triggered dollar weakness,” said Kit Juckes, Societe Generale’s chief currency strategist. “The sense is that the market was happy to react to yesterday’s figures but will not be comfortable taking the dollar too far on less reliable data,” he said. The jobs report came amid a U.S. government shutdown, which has put the brakes on the flow of federal economic data at a moment of uncertainty and division among policymakers. The Trump administration on Wednesday froze $26 billion for Democratic-leaning states, following through on a threat to use the shutdown to target Democratic priorities. “With many major U.S. data releases withheld due to the government shutdown, alternative measures (yesterday’s ADP, today’s Challenger data) are set to have a longer-lasting impact on markets than usual,” said Francesco Pesole, FX strategist at ING. Data also showed on Wednesday that U.S. manufacturing activity edged up in September, though new orders and employment were subdued as factories grappled with the fallout from President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs. In the meantime, the U.S. Supreme Court said it would hear arguments in January over Trump’s attempt to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook. Money markets are expecting two further Fed interest rate cuts this year. Elsewhere, the euro rose 0.2 per cent to $1.1756 after data showed on Wednesday that euro zone inflation accelerated last month on higher services prices and a smaller decline in energy costs, likely reinforcing bets on the European Central Bank keeping interest rates on hold for some time. “Data is vindicating the ECB’s cautious stance, and could keep dovish voices in the governing council quiet,” Pesole said. The Wall Street Journal reported that the U.S. will provide Ukraine with intelligence for long-range missile strikes on Russia’s energy infrastructure. Reuters Related

title: Camaroe Leads Actives As Bursa Starts On Firm Footing
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened stronger, mirroring positive sentiment across regional markets as investors shrugged off overnight volatility on Wall Street and looked towards Asia for momentum. At 9.37 am, the benchmark FBM KLCI advanced 9.32 points, or 0.57%, to 1,630.19 after opening at 1,621.68. Broader market indices were also in positive territory, with the FBM70 climbing 0.89% to 16,998.54, the FBMEMAS adding 0.66% to 12,134.75, while the FBMSHA rose 0.75% to 12,168.65. On the active stocks list, newly-listed Camaroe Bhd continued to draw attention on its second day of trade, topping activity with 487.9 million shares changing hands. The counter climbed 2 sen to 16 sen, after hitting a high of 16.5 sen earlier in the session. Other actively traded counters included VS Industry, up 2.5 sen to 62.5 sen, and SNS Network, which rose 4 sen to 73 sen. Across the region, major Asian bourses also traded higher in early sessions. Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose on the back of a weaker yen, while South Korea’s Kospi and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index both posted modest gains as investors assessed China’s manufacturing data released earlier in the week. Analysts noted that the stronger opening in Malaysia was supported by bargain-hunting and sustained foreign inflows, while global risk appetite appeared to improve despite lingering concerns over the US government shutdown. Market watchers expect Bursa to remain range-bound but tilted towards the upside, in tandem with Asia’s momentum and firming ringgit movements. Related

title: Bursa Surges On Midday Gains Amid Regional Optimism
body:
Malaysian shares climbed steadily by midday, tracking gains across regional markets as investors reacted positively to strong tech and industrial performances in Asia. The benchmark FBM KLCI rose 10.93 points, or 0.67%, to 1,631.80, while the broader FBM70 and FBM EMAS indexes gained 1.03% and 0.76% respectively. Mid-cap stocks also lifted the FBM Small Cap index by 0.83% to 12,178.17. Trading activity was concentrated in small-cap and high-volume counters, with VS leading the volume chart at 100.8 million shares, up 3.3% to RM0.62. Camaroe, Pharma, SNS, and CBHB also saw strong buying interest, contributing to the market’s upward momentum. Regional sentiment supported Bursa’s gains, following a rally in Japan where the Nikkei rose 0.5% and Taiwan’s tech-heavy Taiex jumped 1.5% on positive semiconductor deals. South Korea’s KOSPI surged 2.8% as Samsung and Hynix inked partnerships to supply AI data centres, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng added 0.5%. Analysts noted that investor optimism over U.S. Federal Reserve easing, as signalled by a weak ADP employment report, bolstered Asian equities alongside local market buying. With the global backdrop showing continued resilience in technology and industrial sectors, Bursa is on course to extend gains into the afternoon session, with liquidity concentrated in active small-cap and mid-cap stocks. title: Wall Street Futures Slip As Shutdown Fears Cloud Economic Outlook
body:
US stock index futures edged lower on Tuesday as investors grew cautious over the looming risk of a government shutdown, while awaiting key labour market and consumer sentiment reports that could shape the Federal Reserve’s policy stance. At 5:07 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis fell 104 points, or 0.22%, S&P 500 E-minis slipped 11.25 points, or 0.17%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis lost 39 points, or 0.16%. Analysts noted that while shutdowns typically result in short-lived disruptions, the timing of the current threat is more delicate given uncertainties around growth and inflation. “Shutdowns are more apt to be a temporary disruption rather than a permanent drag where the short-term economic impacts are often recouped over time,” said Jack Janasiewicz, lead portfolio strategist at Natixis Investment Managers. “However, the length of any shutdown can impact the collection and release of important economic data, especially at a time when the economy is at a crucial juncture.” The Federal Reserve’s data-dependent approach has heightened the importance of upcoming releases, with investors looking closely at the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August and the Conference Board’s consumer confidence index later in the day. A busy slate of Fed speakers, including Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and regional presidents Susan Collins, Austan Goolsbee and Lorie Logan, is also on watch for policy cues. Despite the jitters, equities have held firm through the third quarter. The S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow are all set to post gains for a second straight quarter, heading into what is historically a strong fourth quarter driven by year-end positioning and holiday spending. Corporate updates are expected to play a bigger role in the coming weeks. Nike is due to report earnings after Tuesday’s close, offering insights into consumer demand and margins at a time of price hikes. In other moves, Wolfspeed surged 49% a day after exiting bankruptcy, while Firefly Aerospace tumbled 10.7% following a testing mishap that destroyed the core booster of its Alpha rocket. title: Stock Today: V.S Industry Edges Higher Despite Weak FY25 Earnings
body:
V.S Industry Bhd’s (VSI) share price inched up in early trade today, rising 0.85% to RM0.595 at 11.58 am, despite analysts maintaining cautious views following the group’s disappointing fourth quarter and full-year FY25 performance. The counter added half a sen from the previous close of RM0.590, with 39.3 million shares traded. It opened at RM0.590 and touched an intraday high of RM0.620 before paring gains. Buy and sell queues stood evenly balanced, with 2.48 million shares on the bid and 1.84 million on the offer side. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both reiterated Hold calls on VSI, lowering their target prices to RM0.64 and RM0.54 respectively. VSI had slipped into a core net loss of RM6 million in 4QFY25, reversing from a RM23.7 million profit in the preceding quarter. The group also posted a net loss of RM33 million for the quarter compared with a RM23.1 million net profit in 3QFY25. No dividend was declared. For the full year, VSI’s core net profit plunged 69.6% year-on-year to RM62.5 million, while revenue dropped 10.8% to RM3.79 billion, missing both CIMB’s and consensus forecasts. Analysts attributed the slump to weaker orders from a US customer, the loss of Customer Y, rising Malaysian labour costs, and expansion-related losses in the Philippines, where operations recorded a pre-tax loss of RM24.9 million. HLIB noted that FY25 core profit after tax and minority interest stood at RM38.1 million, down 79.5% year-on-year and well below expectations at only a third of its forecast. Losses at the Philippines plant, cost-down initiatives, and impairments linked to HT Press were the key drags. Looking forward, both CIMB and HLIB revised down their FY26–27 earnings projections by up to 43%, citing ongoing demand uncertainty, inflationary pressures, and risks tied to reciprocal US tariff measures. Nonetheless, CIMB highlighted early signs of recovery with improved order flows in 1QFY26 and new models entering mass production, while management aims for breakeven in the Philippines by FY26. HLIB also expects losses at the plant to narrow by March 2026, though recovery may be slower than initially hoped. Related

title: Stock Today: PPB Slips Slightly Despite Upgrade To Buy
body:
PPB Group Bhd closed at RM10.14 as of 4.08 pm, down 6 sen or 0.59% from its previous close, with 826,400 shares traded. The stock opened at RM10.20, reaching a high of RM10.44 and a low of RM10.14 during the session. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd recently upgraded its call on PPB to BUY from NEUTRAL, raising the target price to RM11.02 from RM9.01. The research house cited the conclusion of a major litigation involving PPB’s associate, Wilmar International, as a key factor in removing overhangs on the stock. The litigation verdict required compensation of approximately US$708.9 million plus a fine of US$298,000, already deposited with Indonesia’s Attorney General’s Office and set to be transferred to the State Treasury. While this will cause Wilmar to report a net loss in Q3 FY25, the fine is not considered material relative to its typical quarterly earnings of US$300–400 million. MBSB Research revised Wilmar’s FY25 earnings forecast down 49.3% year-on-year to US$730.2 million (RM579.3 million), which led to a 38.1% cut in PPB’s earnings projection to RM778.4 million. Dividend forecasts were also trimmed to 25 sen per share, yielding 2.5%. Despite these near-term impacts, the research house expects Wilmar’s rebound from FY26 to support PPB’s long-term growth. Improvements in most of Wilmar’s divisions, alongside stabilising wheat prices and prudent feedstock procurement, are projected to sustain recovery. PPB’s core businesses are expected to maintain operating profits above RM360 million annually over the next three years. Related

title: Stock Today: Maybank Edges Higher At Midday, Backed By Resilient Sector Outlook
body:
Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) saw its shares trade marginally higher at midday, rising 0.20% to RM9.93 with 29.4 million shares changing hands as of 2.55 pm. The counter touched an intraday high of RM9.97 before easing slightly. The movement comes as analysts maintain a steady outlook on the banking sector. Both RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) have reiterated a NEUTRAL stance, though Maybank remains among their preferred picks alongside Hong Leong Bank, CIMB and Public Bank. RHB Research highlighted that banking system loans grew 5.4% year-on-year in August, in line with its full-year target of 4.5–5%. Growth was supported by a 5.7% expansion in household loans, particularly in mortgages and auto financing, as well as a 5% rise in non-household loans from finance, transport, communications and wholesale trade sectors. Deposits also posted steady growth, up 4% year-on-year, largely driven by current and savings accounts (CASA), which rose 6% and lifted the CASA ratio to 31.4%. Fixed deposit rates have trended lower since June, easing funding pressure on banks and helping to manage net interest margins. Meanwhile, asset quality across the sector remains stable, with gross impaired loan ratios holding at about 1.4%. Liquidity coverage ratios stayed elevated at 146–147%, while capital buffers were maintained with a CET1 ratio of 14.5%. Looking ahead, RHB Research expects stronger loan drawdowns from non-household segments towards year-end, supported by trade activity with the US. CIMB Securities, however, cautioned that the impact of July’s 25-basis-point policy rate cut on credit demand will take more time to materialise. Maybank, the country’s largest bank by assets, continues to be viewed by analysts as a resilient play given its scale, diversified earnings base and strong capital ratios. Related

body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) sees potential upside for several Bursa Malaysia counters, citing strong bullish momentum and breakout signals. KPJ Healthcare is sustaining above its 21-day SMA line, having closed above the RM2.73 resistance level. The research house noted that the counter could continue its upward trajectory towards RM2.86 and potentially RM3, while a drop below RM2.60 would negate the bullish setup and trigger a correction. title: STI Opens Higher As Regional Markets Track Cautious Optimism
body:
The Straits Times Index (STI) opened firmer on Wednesday, rising 17.21 points or 0.4% to 4,317.37 at 9.03 am, as investors digested overnight cues from Wall Street and tracked gains across Asian equities. Market breadth was positive, with 100 advancers outpacing 45 decliners, on a trading volume of 132.64 million securities valued at S$107.83 million. Among blue chips, DBS gained 0.55% to S$51.43, UOB edged up to S$34.78, while OCBC traded at S$16.52. Singtel was unchanged at S$4.15, and SGX added to S$16.63. The broader sentiment was buoyed by a modest rebound in US markets, though lingering concerns over a potential government shutdown and the Federal Reserve’s data-dependent stance capped risk appetite. Regionally, futures in Japan pointed higher, with the Nikkei 225 December contract at 44,735.00, while FTSE China A50 futures hovered at 15,115.00, reflecting cautious optimism after recent weakness in mainland shares. Taiwan and Hong Kong-linked futures were mixed, suggesting selective positioning ahead of key economic data releases. Analysts noted that while Singapore’s opening strength mirrored a generally positive tone across Asia, volatility is likely to persist given uncertainties over US fiscal developments and OPEC+ deliberations on supply.
