title: Ringgit Pushes Higher As US Shutdown Jitters Weigh On Dollar
body:
The ringgit extended its upward momentum against the US dollar on Wednesday, lifted by investor caution over a looming US government shutdown and expectations of softer American interest rates. At 8.02 am, the local currency was quoted at 4.1980/2190 against the greenback, stronger than Tuesday’s close of 4.2050/2090. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said persistent concerns about a shutdown in Washington were pressuring the dollar, opening room for the ringgit to test new levels. “The local note may attempt to break the psychological level of 4.20 after closing 0.25% higher yesterday,” he said. The ringgit also gained ground against a basket of major and regional currencies. It strengthened to 2.8348/8491 against the Japanese yen from 2.8420/8447 and advanced to 5.6417/6699 against the British pound from 5.6532/6586. The local unit also rose to 4.9251/9497 versus the euro from 4.9405/9452. In Asia, the ringgit improved to 3.2530/2695 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2604/2638, edged up versus the Indonesian rupiah at 251.9/253.2 from 252.3/252.6, gained on the Philippine peso at 7.21/7.25 from 7.22/7.24, and appreciated to 12.9265/9963 against the Thai baht from 12.9744/9927. Related

title: Gold Rises To RM523 per Gram, Tracks Global Gains
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia continued their upward momentum today, with the precious metal trading at RM523.45 per gram as of early Wednesday, up RM3.10 or 0.59% from the previous session. On a per ounce basis, gold was priced at RM16,281.09 while a kilogramme traded at RM523,448.81. The rise mirrors broader global sentiment, as investors remain drawn to safe-haven assets amid uncertainty in global markets. Over the past month, gold in Malaysia has gained 8.58%, while six-month performance shows a 16.24% increase. Year-on-year, prices have surged 46.45%, reflecting one of the strongest rallies in recent years. Silver also climbed higher, advancing 1.34% to RM2.62 per gram. The metal has outperformed gold in annual terms, rising 48.12% over the past year, with a five-year gain of nearly 97%. Globally, gold has posted strong annual returns in multiple currencies. In US dollar terms, the metal has risen 46.5% so far in 2025, its steepest climb since 2020. Gains were also notable in other major markets, with prices up 41.7% in Canadian dollars, 42.9% in Chinese yuan, and 52.1% in Indian rupees. Robust central bank purchases, steady demand from Asia, and ongoing geopolitical risks are key drivers of the rally. With inflationary concerns persisting and rate cuts from major central banks on the horizon, traders expect gold to remain well-supported heading into the final quarter of the year. Related

body:
Bursa Malaysia opened on a firmer note on the first day of October, tracking a mixed but generally steady performance across regional markets. At 9.17 am, the FBM KLCI rose 2.73 points or 0.17% to 1,614.61, after moving between 1,612.62 and 1,615.22 in early trade. The broader market was also positive, with the FBM 70 up 20.46 points to 16,767.05, while the FBM Emas gained 19.71 points to 12,005.60. The FBM Shariah Index advanced 18.88 points to 12,035.43. The local bourse’s cautious gains were in tandem with regional sentiment, as investors weighed signs of resilience in Asian markets against concerns over a potential US government shutdown. Singapore’s Straits Times Index opened 0.4% higher at 4,317.37, while futures in Japan’s Nikkei and China’s FTSE A50 were steady ahead of key economic data releases. On Wall Street overnight, US stock futures slipped as traders braced for labour market reports and the uncertainty surrounding Washington’s budget deadlock. Analysts noted that the political standoff could disrupt data releases crucial to the Federal Reserve’s policy outlook. Market participants in Malaysia are expected to stay cautious but opportunistic, tracking both external risks and domestic corporate developments as the final quarter of 2025 gets underway. Related

title: Stock Today: Genting Malaysia Hovers Amid NYC Casino Licence Race
body:
Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) was last done at RM2.10 as of 4.10 pm, down 0.47% or RM0.01, with 2.9 million shares traded so far. The stock opened at RM2.11, reaching an intraday high of RM2.13 and a low of RM2.09. Investors are closely monitoring Genting Malaysia’s unit, Resorts World New York City (RWNYC), which has emerged as a frontrunner in New York City’s bid for up to three new casino licences. RWNYC recently received unanimous backing from the Community Advisory Committee (CAC), a key step before proposals advance to the state’s Gaming Facility Location Board. Of eight submissions lodged in June, only RWNYC and MGM Resorts’ bids have received unanimous local support. RWNYC’s USD5.5 billion proposal offers faster delivery and larger scale compared with MGM’s USD2.3 billion bid, with an expected opening by mid-2026. Analysts at Kenanga Research said the project ticks three major boxes — speed, scale, and safety — but noted Genting may still require USD2–3 billion in additional funding to complete the project, which could involve debt, asset disposals, or equity issuance, adding execution and dilution risks. GENM currently has net debt of RM11.3 billion and limited additional borrowing headroom. Past attempts to sell non-core assets, including a Miami land parcel valued at USD1.2 billion, have yet to materialise. Kenanga maintained its Market Perform rating and RM2.00 target price, noting that a successful licence bid could potentially lift GENM’s valuation by RM0.50 per share, though risks remain from funding, execution, and macroeconomic headwinds. So far today, the stock has seen a buy volume of 845,800 shares against a sell volume of 385,600 shares, reflecting investor interest as RWNYC’s licence bid progresses. Related

title: Stock Today: Gamuda Edges Up Near 1% Amid Singapore Land Win
body:
Gamuda Bhd’s stock rose 0.91% to RM5.57 as of 2.53 pm, with 8.73 million shares traded, following the group’s recent acquisition of a prime land parcel in Singapore’s Chencharu Close. The stock opened at RM5.52, reaching a high of RM5.63 and a low of RM5.52, reflecting steady investor interest. MBSB Investment Bank Bhd and Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) have both maintained their BUY calls on Gamuda, with target prices of RM6.35 and RM6.88 respectively. Analysts cited the company’s all-time high order book of RM35.8 billion, diversified portfolio across construction, property and utilities, and strong recurring income prospects as key positives. The Chencharu Close project, won by a consortium led by Gamuda’s wholly owned subsidiary Gamuda (Singapore) Pte Ltd with Evia MCS Pte Ltd and H108 Pte Ltd, was secured for S$1.01 billion (RM3.33 billion), 19.8% above the next bid. The 29,450 sq m site carries a 99-year leasehold tenure and is earmarked for an integrated residential and commercial development, including 875 homes, 12,600 sq m of commercial space, a bus interchange, and a hawker centre. Gamuda holds a 50% stake in the joint venture. HLIB highlighted that the mixed-use parcel represents a quick-turnaround development with meaningful earnings potential, projecting Gamuda’s profit share from the project to reach RM380 million to RM520 million at low to mid-teens margins. Earnings contributions are expected to begin in FY27, with the project slated for launch in November 2026. MBSB Research said the acquisition complements Gamuda’s portfolio of quick-turnaround projects, supporting a sales target of RM5.5 billion for FY26, driven by Vietnam projects and new mid-upper range launches in Malaysia. Both research houses kept earnings forecasts unchanged, with HLIB slightly revising FY27 core profit after tax and minority interest (PATAMI) upwards by 3.2% following the inclusion of the project. Investors appear confident that Gamuda’s regional expansion, coupled with strong momentum in its construction and property segments, will sustain growth, reinforcing the stock’s appeal amid attractive valuations. title: Stock Today: AEON Credit Climbs 2.6% As Investors Look Past Profit Slip
body:
AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd’s (AEON Credit) shares gained 2.62% at midday, closing at RM5.49, up 14 sen from the previous close of RM5.35, with 6.88 million shares changing hands. The stock traded between RM5.31 and RM5.49 during the session. The buying interest came despite weaker quarterly earnings, as AEON Credit’s 2QFY26 net profit slipped 6.9% quarter-on-quarter to RM72.2 million, though it edged up 1.5% year-on-year. Higher impairment provisions on financing receivables and losses from AEON Bank weighed on the bottom line, bringing first-half profit to RM149.8 million, down 15.7% from a year earlier and below expectations. CIMB Investment Bank Bhd (CIMB Securities) has maintained a HOLD rating with a target price of RM5.70, citing mixed credit quality and persistently high net credit costs, which climbed to 5.02% from 4.98% in the preceding quarter. While AEON Credit declared a dividend of 13 sen, lower than 14.25 sen a year earlier, its non-performing loan ratio improved marginally to 2.49% from 2.57%. CIMB Securities noted that the stock’s current valuation of 0.9 times FY26 price-to-book value is below its five-year average of 1.2 times but considers the discount fair given limited catalysts for a re-rating. Key risks flagged include further AEON Bank losses, funding cost pressures, and potential asset quality deterioration, though upside could come from stronger receivables growth. Related

title: Ringgit Edges Higher Against US Dollar
body:
The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Tuesday, standing at 4.2125/2210 compared with Monday’s close at 4.2150/2200. The local note was supported by concerns that a potential United States government shutdown could weigh on the greenback. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said a US government shutdown would be significant, as it could hamper the functioning of key agencies such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics. “If materialised, it would result in difficulties in discerning the latest trend in the US labour market at a time when the Federal Reserve (Fed) has highlighted increased downside risks to employment,” he told a local news outlet. He noted that the release of important data points, such as the nonfarm payroll report due this Friday, might be delayed. Mohd Afzanizam said the US Dollar Index (DXY) was down about 0.25% to 97.906 points. He added that the ringgit, which gained 0.12% to RM4.2175 against the US dollar yesterday, is expected to trade between RM4.20 and RM4.21 today. “Again, the ringgit could attempt to breach the psychological level of RM4.20, especially if the Fed proceeds with interest rate cuts should a government shutdown occur,” he said. At the opening, the ringgit was mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It firmed to 2.8340/8399 against the Japanese yen from 2.8365/8400 at Monday’s close, and increased to 5.6582/6696 against the British pound from 5.6612/6679. However, it slipped to 4.9404/9504 versus the euro from 4.9387/9446. The local note was also mostly higher against ASEAN currencies, except for the Thai baht. It advanced to 3.2653/2723 vis-à-vis the Singapore dollar from 3.2664/2706, edged up against the Indonesian rupiah at 252.5/253.1 from 252.6/253.1, and appreciated versus the Philippine peso at 7.24/7.26 from 7.25/7.26. It eased, however, to 13.0669/1002 against the Thai baht from 13.0649/0857 previously. Related

title: PETDAG Leads Gains While Nestle Tumbles In Bursa Session
body:
PETDAG surged 1.6% to RM22.94, emerging as the top gainer on Bursa Malaysia today, supported by steady volume of 5,077 lots, as investors sought exposure to energy and consumer-related stocks. Other notable risers included AYER (+4.6% to RM7.50), PPB (+2% to RM10.20), AEONCR (+3.4% to RM5.53), and PJBUMI (+6.9% to RM2.78). On the flip side, Nestle [S] slipped 0.9% to RM96.22, followed by MPI (-1.3% to RM28.72), HUMEIND (-4.4% to RM3.49), KLUANG (-2.6% to RM5.55), and PANAMY (-1.6% to RM8.40), reflecting profit-taking in defensive consumer names. The session’s movements align with broader regional sentiment, with Singapore’s Straits Times Index and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index showing modest gains, while investors kept an eye on US inflation data and Fed signals that may influence global capital flows. Market watchers highlighted that Malaysia’s energy, consumer, and industrial segments remain in focus, as investors position for both domestic corporate earnings and external market catalysts in the coming weeks. title: Hiap Teck Shines From China’s Steel Curb
body:
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) has maintained its BUY call on Hiap Teck Venture Bhd (HTVB) with a higher target price of RM0.36 from RM0.34 previously, citing stronger earnings prospects from its associate Eastern Steel Sdn Bhd (ESSB) and improving industry conditions. At the current price of RM0.295, the research house said the stock offers a potential capital upside of 22% and an expected total return of 25.4%, including dividends. For the financial year ended July 2025, HTVB’s core net profit rose 11% to RM101.8 million, mainly driven by higher contributions from ESSB, in which it holds a 27.3% stake. ESSB’s core earnings surged 81% to RM126.7 million from RM70.1 million a year earlier, supported by increased output from its new blast furnace, the commencement of hot-rolled coil (HRC) production in the third quarter of FY25 and lower production costs from improved economies of scale and cheaper inputs. These contributions helped offset weaker performances in HTVB’s trading and downstream businesses, which were affected by softer selling prices and subdued domestic construction activities. HLIB Research noted that steel prices have begun to stabilise following the Chinese Government’s announcement of a new steel industry action plan. The measures, which include a ban on additional capacity and the accelerated phase-out of outdated equipment, are intended to address persistent oversupply in the market. While previous attempts have had limited success, management at HTVB believes the likelihood of success is higher this time, pointing to early signs of capacity reduction in China. Looking ahead, HLIB Research said HTVB’s trading and downstream segments, currently impacted by the transitional effects of the extended Sales and Service Tax, are expected to recover from early 2026. This will be supported by upcoming infrastructure projects such as the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme and potential nationwide water pipe replacement initiatives, where HTVB is well-positioned with a sizeable pipe-making capacity of about 550,000 metric tonnes per annum. Meanwhile, utilisation at ESSB’s HRC plant, which began operations in December 2024, has increased to about 70% from 55% in the fourth quarter of FY25. Management aims to lift this rate to around 90% by the end of 2025, which would further lower unit conversion costs. In addition, the scaffolding business delivered a pre-tax profit of RM18 million in FY25 and is expected to strengthen further into FY26, supported by a pick-up in construction activity. HLIB Research raised its FY26–27 core net profit forecasts for HTVB by 15.4% and 15.2% respectively, to reflect higher earnings assumptions at ESSB. The research house said it continues to favour HTVB for its healthy balance sheet, with a net gearing of 0.26 times as at July 31 2025 and attractive valuations. At the current trading level, HTVB is priced at 4.9 times FY26 price-to-earnings and 0.33 times price-to-book, which are below its five-year historical averages. HLIB Research added that ESSB’s competitive cost structure has allowed it to sustain earnings despite a challenging environment and positions the company to benefit from demand recovery once market conditions improve. At 10.26 am, the stock price is stable at RM0.295. Related

title: Hang Seng Index Futures Stays In Bullish Lane With 28,500 On The Horizon
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its positive trading bias on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), citing firm upward momentum and improving market sentiment after the index surged 572 points to close at 26,705 on Monday. The index opened at 26,168 and briefly dipped to 26,124 before climbing steadily to a high of 26,746, eventually closing with a bullish Marubozu candlestick. In the evening session, the HSIF added another 30 points to last trade at 26,735. RHB Research said the strong price action reaffirms sustained bullish strength, with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) trending above the 50% level and both the 20- and 50-day simple moving average (SMA) lines continuing their upward slope. “As long as the 23,800-pt support holds, the index is expected to extend its upside movement towards the 27,000-pt resistance,” it said, adding that a breakout above this level could pave the way for a move towards 28,500. The research house advised traders to retain long positions initiated at 21,416 on 14 April, while keeping the stop-loss threshold at 23,800 to mitigate risks. Immediate support levels are seen at 25,000 and 23,800, while immediate resistance is marked at 27,000 and 28,500. Related

title: Gold Glitters As Global Uncertainty Boosts Prices
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia experienced a notable increase, reflecting a global trend driven by economic uncertainties and geopolitical tensions. In Malaysia, the price of gold per gram was reported at RM522.53, marking a daily rise of RM3.14 or 0.60%. This uptick is part of a broader upward trajectory, with gold prices increasing by 9.95% over the past 30 days and 45.44% over the past year. The price per kilogram stood at RM522,528.98, and the price per ounce was RM16,252.48. Globally, gold prices reached a record high, with the price per ounce climbing to $3,866.90, driven by investor demand for safe assets amid concerns over a potential U.S. government shutdown and expectations of further interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. This surge represents a 12.1% increase in September, marking the best monthly performance since August 2011. The SPDR Gold Trust, the largest gold-backed ETF, reported a 0.60% increase in holdings to 1,011.73 metric tons, the highest level since July 2022. In contrast, silver prices in Malaysia saw a slight decline, with the price per gram falling to RM6.37, a decrease of 0.41% from the previous day. Over the past year, silver prices have increased by 50.73%, indicating a strong long-term performance despite the recent dip. The rise in gold prices reflects a global trend where investors are turning to precious metals as a hedge against economic instability and currency fluctuations. Analysts suggest that the ongoing economic challenges and geopolitical uncertainties may continue to support the upward momentum in gold prices in the near term. Related

title: FBM KLCI Climbs Past 1,618, Defies Regional Jitters
body:
Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark FBM KLCI was up 7.20 points to 1,618.15, a gain of 0.45%, while broader indices also saw firm gains: FBM70 rose 0.19%, F4GBM gained 0.42%, FBMEMAS added 0.37%, and FBMSHA jumped 0.54%. The market rally is taking place amid a cautious regional mood, as Asian shares trade in a narrow range while investors monitor the risk of a US government shutdown that could disrupt key economic data releases. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng index held steady, while China’s Shanghai Composite added 0.4%, although factory activity data painted a soft picture. In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 inched down slightly. Back in Malaysia, investors appear to be favouring selective buying in key sectors. The most active counters included penny stocks such as Nexg Bina, which saw heavy volume. The upside momentum in Bursa reflects a modest confidence among market participants who are balancing potential global headwinds with local optimism. Related

title: Buy On PPB Group After Removal Of Key Overhang
body:
MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB Research) has upgraded its call on PPB Group Bhd to BUY from NEUTRAL with a revised target price of RM11.02 from RM9.01, noting that the conclusion of a major litigation involving its associate Wilmar International has removed a key overhang. At RM10.00, the stock offers an expected total return of 14.38%, inclusive of dividends. The research house said the final verdict on Wilmar International’s subsidiaries, collectively known as the Wilmar Respondents, required compensation of about US$708.9 million alongside a fine of US$298,000. The compensation, already deposited with Indonesia’s Attorney General’s Office and to be transferred to the State Treasury, covers profits gained, state financial losses and business and household sector damages. While the penalty will result in Wilmar recording a net loss in its third-quarter FY25 results, the fine itself is not considered material compared with Wilmar’s usual quarterly earnings range of US$300–400 million. Following the ruling, MBSB Research revised Wilmar’s FY25 earnings forecast lower by 49.3% year-on-year to US$730.2 million (RM579.3 million), which led to a 38.1% cut in PPB’s earnings projection to RM778.4 million. The dividend per share forecast was also trimmed to 25 sen from 35 sen, translating into a yield of 2.5%. Despite this near-term setback, MBSB Research said it sees most short-term risks as largely priced in, with PPB’s long-term outlook underpinned by Wilmar’s expected rebound from FY26 onwards. Improvements across most of Wilmar’s divisions, excluding plantation and sugar milling, are expected to sustain recovery, while moderating wheat prices and prudent feedstock procurement are set to support better crushing margins in the grains and agribusiness segment. The research house added that PPB’s core businesses are projected to maintain operating profit above RM360 million annually over the next three years. With risks from the litigation now cleared, valuations are seen as attractive relative to the group’s earnings potential, underpinning the decision to lift its recommendation to BUY. As of 10.30 am, the stock price is up by 1.20% to RM10.120. Related

title: Bursa Ends Flat As Global Cues Weigh On Investors
body:
The FBM KLCI closed virtually unchanged at 1,611.88 points, up 0.06% or 0.93 points, as cautious sentiment persisted among Malaysian investors amid mixed regional markets. While the broader FBM70 fell 0.22% to 16,746.59, and the FBMEMAS edged down 0.02% to 11,985.89, local market movements mirrored patterns in regional peers. Markets in Singapore and Hong Kong saw moderate gains earlier in the session, lifted by technology and consumer stocks, while Wall Street indices closed flat overnight, weighed by concerns over inflation data and mixed earnings results. Trading activity was moderate, with top volume leaders including NEXGBINA, ZETRIX, and VS, reflecting continued interest in small-cap and mid-cap counters despite broader market caution. It is noted that the local bourse is likely to remain range-bound in the near term, awaiting economic data from the US and China, as well as corporate earnings updates from key Malaysian sectors. title: Sony Financial Share Jumps 40% In Market Debut
body:
Shares in Sony Financial jumped as much as 40 per cent in their Tokyo trading debut on Monday, after the business was spun-off from entertainment and technology conglomerate Sony. Sony distributed shares in its finance arm, which includes banking and insurance, to shareholders through dividends in kind as it focuses on entertainment.It is the first partial spin-off in Japan taking advantage of a 2023 tax change and the first direct listing in more than two decades. The shares rose as high as 210 yen after changing hands for the first time at 10:13 a.m. in Tokyo, an hour and 13 minutes into the session, before trading at 201.6 yen as of 10:30 a.m. The reference price was 150 yen ($1.00).Sony Financial has said it will buy back up to 100 billion yen ($671.1 million) of its shares. Sony aims to expand its presence in entertainment from games to movies and music, and maintain its position as the leading manufacturer of image sensors. Reuters Related

title: Ringgit Stuck In Neutral As Fed Keeps Markets Guessing
body:
The ringgit opened unchanged against the US dollar on Monday, with traders cautious amid mixed messages from United States Federal Reserve (Fed) officials over the interest rate outlook. At 8.01 am, the local unit stood at 4.2200/2250, the same level as Friday’s close. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the conflicting Fed views had left investors uncertain on whether the central bank would lean towards prioritising growth or taming inflation, limiting gains for emerging market currencies such as the ringgit. “The US dollar has also strengthened, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) trading above the 98-point mark. On that note, the ringgit is expected to trade within the RM4.22 to RM4.23 range today,” he told a local news outlet. Against other major currencies, the ringgit was weaker at the opening. It eased to 2.8265/8301 against the Japanese yen from 2.8171/8206 at Friday’s close, slipped to 5.6599/6666 against the British pound from 5.6345/6412, and fell to 4.9416/9475 versus the euro from 4.9281/9340. The local note also weakened against several ASEAN currencies, trading lower at 3.2680/2721 against the Singapore dollar from 3.2630/2671, and at 13.0849/1081 against the Thai baht from 13.0587/1069. It, however, remained unchanged against the Indonesian rupiah at 252.1/252.5 and the Philippine peso at 7.25/7.27. Related

title: Market Ends Lower As Decliners Outpace Gainers
body:
The stock market closed lower on Sept 29 as profit-taking pressure dragged down key stocks, with overall market sentiment remaining cautious. Market breadth was negative, with 645 decliners outpacing 459 gainers, while 487 counters were unchanged, 1,057 untraded and 124 suspended. Turnover narrowed to 3.77 billion units worth RM2.47 billion compared to 4.16 billion units worth RM3.17 billion recorded on Sept 26. Among the day’s bright spots, Nestlé (M) Bhd rose RM1.06 to RM97.10, leading the gainers’ list. Plenitude Bhd climbed 36 sen to RM2.22 on strong volume of 3.23 million shares, while Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd added 35 sen to RM5.85. Country View Bhd advanced 22 sen to RM3 and Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd gained 18 sen to RM17.10. On the flip side, heavyweight brewers weighed on the market, with Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd slipping 30 sen to RM16.46 and Heineken Malaysia Bhd shedding 28 sen to RM21.30. Boustead Plantations’ parent Kuala Lumpur Kepong’s associate Batu Kawan Bhd eased 24 sen to RM18.80, while Malayan Cement Bhd fell 20 sen to RM6.95. Technology player Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd also lost 20 sen to RM29.10. Analysts said the mixed trading pattern reflects investors staying cautious ahead of key global economic data releases and domestic policy developments, with buying interest selective and rotational in nature. title: Dollar Slides As US Shutdown Fears Loom, Yen Strengthens Ahead Of Key Data
body:
The US dollar fell on Monday amid growing concerns over a potential government shutdown, with the yen outperforming the euro ahead of a series of US economic releases that could shed light on the Federal Reserve’s policy trajectory. The dollar index, which tracks the greenback against a basket of major currencies, declined 0.22% to 97.90, after rising 0.5% last week following data that tempered expectations for Fed rate cuts. Traders currently price in 40 basis points of easing by December and 110 basis points by the end of 2026, roughly 25 bps lower than mid-September levels. Investors are closely watching whether Congress will pass a funding bill before the fiscal year ends on Tuesday. Without approval, parts of the government would shut down on Wednesday, potentially disrupting the release of Friday’s non-farm payrolls report and other key economic data. Bob Savage, head of macro strategy at BNY, noted a prolonged shutdown could hinder markets’ ability to correctly price the Fed’s easing cycle. The dollar was down 0.6% against the yen at 148.67 but gained ground against the euro and sterling, which rose 0.25% to $1.1729 and 0.34% to $1.3445 respectively. Analysts highlighted that eurozone inflation data is unlikely to shift the policy outlook, while geopolitical tensions, particularly the war in Ukraine, remain key drivers. Investors are also monitoring the legal challenge over Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook’s potential removal, with the Trump administration seeking Supreme Court approval to fire her. Analysts say any threat to the Fed’s independence could pose a greater risk to the dollar than a government shutdown. Elsewhere, the Australian dollar was last up 0.35% at $0.6571 ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia’s rate announcement on Tuesday, where rates are expected to remain unchanged. Reuters Related

title: Correction Deepens In Hang Seng Index Futures, Long Bias Intact Above 23,800
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has advised traders to maintain their long positions on the Hang Seng Index futures (HSIF), despite the index slumping 402 points to close at 26,133 points on Friday. The index opened at 26,529 points, touched a high of 26,547 points and a low of 26,095 points before settling at 26,133 points with a long bearish candlestick. During the evening session, it recovered 157 points to last trade at 26,290 points. RHB Research noted that the price action reflects an ongoing correction, with the Relative Strength Index (RSI) turning lower and signalling a deceleration in bullish momentum. The index may drift towards the 20-day simple moving average (SMA), with a breach potentially triggering a deeper pullback towards the 50-day SMA. “Both moving averages are trending upwards, indicating the broader bullish structure remains intact. As long as the HSIF holds above the 23,800 points support, we will keep to a positive trading bias despite the current retracement,” the research house said. Traders are advised to stay on the long position initiated at 21,416 points on 14 April, with a stop-loss level at 23,800 points. The initial support is placed at 25,000 points, followed by 23,800 points, while immediate resistance is marked at 27,000 points and next at 28,500 points. Related

title: Bursa Opens Higher In Line With Regional Gains
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened firmer in line with gains across regional markets, as investors weighed mixed signals from the US Federal Reserve alongside steady sentiment in Asia. The benchmark FBM KLCI rose 3.39 points or 0.21% to 1,612.44 at 9.05 am, after touching a high of 1,613.53. Broader indices also advanced, with the FBM70 up 42.52 points to 16,892.87, the FBMEMAS adding 23.76 points to 12,017.20, and the F4GBM increasing 2.06 points to 970.17. Market breadth was positive, led by active counters such as MTOUCHE, which gained 1 sen to 7.5 sen with heavy volume, and SNS, which added 2 sen to 69 sen. EAH remained unchanged at half a sen but was the most traded stock, with over 115 million shares exchanging hands. Regionally, the Straits Times Index in Singapore edged 0.11% higher at 4,270.57, while Nikkei 225 futures in Japan traded at 45,000.00. Optimism in Asia came despite ongoing caution in global markets, as oil prices slipped and traders remained focused on upcoming US data that could guide interest rate expectations. Related

title: Bursa Malaysia Inches Lower At Midday On Mild Profit-Taking
body:
Bursa Malaysia traded marginally lower at midday on Sept 29 as investors took profits in selected blue-chip counters, leaving the broader market in negative territory. At 12.30pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slipped just 0.02 points to 1,609.03 compared to the closing of 1,609.05 on Sept 26. The benchmark index opened slightly firmer at 1,609.75 and moved between 1,606.76 and 1,613.53 during the morning session. Market breadth turned negative with 591 decliners outpacing 398 gainers, while 434 counters were unchanged, 1,225 untraded and 124 suspended. Turnover amounted to 2.54 billion shares worth RM1.23 billion. Among the heavyweights, CIMB and Mr DIY rose six sen each to RM7.31 and RM1.68 respectively, while CelcomDigi added five sen to RM3.71. Petronas Dagangan (PetDag) advanced 34 sen to RM22.76 and Axiata climbed three sen to RM2.63. In active trade, EA Holdings, MTouche and NexG were flat at 0.5 sen, 6.5 sen and 9.5 sen, respectively. Tanco slipped 1.5 sen to 88.5 sen, while SNS Network eased half a sen to 66.5 sen. On the broader market, the FBM Emas Index shed 13.29 points to 11,980.15, the FBM T100 Index fell 8.81 points to 11,716.23 and the FBM Emas Shariah Index lost 39.81 points to 12,008.65. title: Asia Stocks Cautious As US Shutdown Looms
body:
Asian markets opened the week on edge with investors preparing for a potential US government shutdown that could stall the release of September’s payrolls and other key economic data. President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet congressional leaders from both parties later on Monday to negotiate government funding. Without an agreement, a shutdown will begin Wednesday, coinciding with new tariffs on heavy trucks, pharmaceuticals and other goods. Bank of America analysts wrote, “If the shutdown lasts beyond the Fed meeting, the Fed will rely on private data for its policy decisions. On the margin, we think this may lower the likelihood of an October cut, but only marginally.” Markets currently price in a 90% chance of a Federal Reserve cut in October, with about a 65% probability of another in December. Analysts also noted that each week of closure would shave only 0.1 percentage point off growth, though permanent worker layoffs could weigh on payrolls and consumer sentiment. A prolonged shutdown may also leave the Fed “flying blind” at its October 29 meeting. Elsewhere, geopolitical focus turned to Quantico, Virginia, where Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth will convene U.S. generals and admirals on Tuesday, with Trump expected to attend. Despite the risks, analysts pointed to seasonal support, as the fourth quarter has historically been strong for equities. The S&P 500 has advanced in 74% of fourth quarters. S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures rose 0.2%, while Eurostoxx 50, FTSE and DAX futures each added 0.3%. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei fell 0.7% but still showed a 6% gain for September. South Korea’s market climbed 1.2% to bring monthly gains to 6.3%. MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.4%, up nearly 4% for the month. Bond markets saw Treasuries steady at 4.17% after upbeat US data last week curtailed expectations of deeper Fed cuts. The dollar index held at 98.134, with the euro at $1.1708 and the yen at 149.49. Gold traded just below record highs at $3,764 an ounce. Oil slipped after crude resumed flowing from Iraq’s Kurdistan to Turkey for the first time in 2½ years. Brent crude was down 0.8% at $69.57 per barrel, while U.S. crude eased 0.9% to $65.14. Reuters Related

title: Weekly Review: Singapore Stocks Ease As STI Slips On Cautious Sentiment
body:
Singapore shares ended the week slightly lower, with the Straits Times Index (STI) easing amid cautious investor sentiment and sectoral rotation as markets digested mixed global cues and interest rate uncertainties. The STI closed at 4,266 points on Sept 26, down 0.18% for the day, marking a weekly decline of around 0.9% as earlier gains faded. Banking heavyweights DBS Group Holdings, OCBC Bank and UOB led the pullback, as investors reassessed pressure on net interest margins and awaited further guidance on regional monetary policy. In contrast, selected REITs and industrial counters showed relative resilience, supported by bargain-hunting and defensive positioning. Market analysts described the retreat as a technical consolidation, noting that sentiment remained cautious ahead of key global economic data releases and corporate earnings updates. “The STI’s movement this week reflects broader investor hesitancy as markets weigh rate expectations and external growth risks,” one strategist said, adding that short-term direction will likely hinge on signals from the US Federal Reserve and China’s economic outlook. Trading activity, meanwhile, stayed moderate, with investors focusing on selective opportunities while maintaining a risk-off stance. Looking ahead, analysts expect the index to trade within a narrow range, with potential catalysts including regional policy measures, currency movements and upcoming earnings from Singapore’s blue-chip firms. title: Weekly Recap: Hong Kong Stocks Post First Weekly Decline In September
body:
Hong Kong stocks ended lower for the week, snapping a three-week winning streak, as renewed concerns over US tariff threats and stretched valuations prompted investors to pare back risk. The Hang Seng Index (HSI) fell 1.6% over the week to close at 26,128.20 points on Sept 26, down 1.4% for the day. The Hang Seng Tech Index slumped 2.9%, weighed by profit-taking in major technology names following a recent rally driven by optimism over artificial intelligence and expectations of US Federal Reserve (Fed) easing. Biotech and pharmaceutical counters were among the hardest hit after reports of potential US tariff measures targeting branded drugs. Consumer and tech stocks also retreated as investors reassessed valuations in light of global trade uncertainties. “Equity valuations that had been happily floating on the raft of lower-for-longer Fed hopes suddenly found the water rising beneath them,” one market strategist said, noting that sentiment has turned more cautious as investors weigh potential macro headwinds. Despite the pullback, analysts said the correction reflects consolidation rather than a fundamental shift, with investors awaiting fresh catalysts from upcoming economic data and policy signals. Market attention next week is expected to focus on China’s policy direction ahead of the Party Plenum and US inflation data, both of which could shape sentiment toward risk assets. Analysts added that sustained recovery in Hong Kong equities will depend on clearer growth support measures from Beijing and a more predictable global rate environment. Related

title: Market Review: Seoul Stocks Slip On Profit-Taking After Record Highs
body:
South Korean shares ended lower for the trading week of Sept 22 as investors took profits following a recent rally that pushed the market to record levels, with caution setting in amid mixed sector performances and external uncertainties. The Kospi benchmark index touched a fresh intraday high of 3,468.65 on Sept 22, buoyed by gains in technology and semiconductor stocks. However, momentum faded in subsequent sessions as investors locked in profits from high-flying names. By Sept 26, the index had declined 0.46%, or 16.06 points, to close at 3,445.24, marking a modest weekly loss. Technology, chemicals, and auto counters led the downturn, while financials and industrials showed mixed performance. Analysts said the pullback reflects a healthy consolidation after a sustained uptrend, rather than a shift in sentiment. “Investors are reassessing valuations after strong gains in recent weeks, especially in tech-heavy sectors,” one market strategist noted. Earlier optimism was driven by robust foreign inflows and strength in semiconductor stocks, which helped lift the index above the 3,400-point level for the first time in months. Market participants are now turning their focus to US economic data, China’s policy signals and corporate earnings, particularly in the tech sector, for direction in the coming weeks. “While short-term volatility is likely, the underlying outlook remains supported by steady foreign buying and improving earnings momentum,” analysts added. title: Market Recap: Bursa Malaysia Holds Steady In Sluggish Week
body:
Bursa Malaysia traded largely range-bound over the week of Sept 22 to 26, as investors adopted a cautious stance amid subdued catalysts and persistent global uncertainties. The FBM KLCI started the week on a positive note, climbing 0.32% to 1,603.34 points on Sept 22, supported by selective buying in blue-chip stocks. However, gains proved short-lived as sentiment softened midweek, with the benchmark slipping 0.07% to 1,598.47 points by Sept 25, reflecting profit-taking and weak external leads. Analysts said the local bourse continued to display a sideways-to-slightly-positive bias, capped by lingering macroeconomic concerns and a lack of strong domestic catalysts. Defensive and dividend-yielding counters drew interest, while cyclical sectors faced pressure amid slower global growth prospects. Market participation remained muted as investors awaited clearer policy signals and fresh economic data. Broader market breadth was mixed, with advances in select financial and consumer stocks offset by declines in technology and plantation counters. “Investors are treading carefully given global uncertainties and cautious sentiment ahead of upcoming economic indicators,” one analyst noted, adding that the index is likely to remain within a narrow trading band in the near term. Looking ahead, traders are expected to monitor domestic policy developments, corporate earnings announcements and regional market cues for direction. Market watchers said a decisive move above key resistance levels could set the tone for the next leg of trading, though downside risks remain if sentiment weakens further. Related

title: Wall Street Rises But Weekly Losses End Winning Streaks
body:
US stocks closed higher on Sept 26 as investors welcomed in-line inflation data, though all three major indexes ended the week in the red after a choppy stretch of trading, Reuters reported. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 299.97 points (0.65%) to 46,247.29, the S&P 500 rose 38.98 points (0.59%) to 6,643.70 and the Nasdaq Composite added 99.37 points (0.44%) to 22,484.07. For the week, the Dow slipped 0.2%, the S&P 500 fell 0.3% and the Nasdaq lost 0.7%, snapping three-week winning streaks for the latter two. The gains on Sept 26 followed the Commerce Department’s personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report for August, which showed inflation rising 0.3% on the month and 2.7% year-over-year, exactly matching forecasts. The PCE index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge, reinforced expectations that price pressures are cooling gradually even as consumer spending and incomes rose more than expected. The data comes as markets weigh a resilient US economy against prospects for further Fed rate cuts. The central bank lowered rates last week for the first time since December and signalled more easing ahead. In stock moves, Paccar rallied 5.2% after President Donald Trump unveiled new import tariffs, including on heavy-duty trucks, a segment where Paccar manufactures largely within the US Eli Lilly gained 1.4% after tariffs were also placed on pharmaceutical products. Electronic Arts surged 14.9% amid reports the video game maker is in advanced talks to go private. Meanwhile, Costco Wholesale fell 2.9% after posting quarterly results that disappointed investors. Investors now turn to the September jobs report due Oct 3, with a potential government shutdown looming as a wildcard for data releases and market sentiment. Market breadth was positive, with advancing issues outpacing decliners by 2.25 to one on the NYSE and 1.69 to one on the Nasdaq. Total trading volume reached 16.98 billion shares, below the recent 20-day average of 18.11 billion. Related

title: Ringgit Poised to Trade Within Narrow Band Versus US Dollar Next Week
body:
The ringgit is expected to trade narrowly between RM4.21 and RM4.23 against the US dollar next week, supported by steady demand for the local currency and key upcoming US economic data. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd’s chief economist, Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid, highlighted that market focus will be on US labour statistics, including the job openings and labour turnover survey, ADP employment change, and non-farm payroll figures. Domestically, attention will also turn to the tabling of Budget 2026 on October 10. Afzanizam said he expects the government to maintain an expansionary approach while continuing to narrow the fiscal deficit, a move that could lend medium- to longer-term support to the ringgit. On a weekly basis, the ringgit ended slightly weaker against the greenback, closing at 4.2200/2250 compared with 4.2040/2115 the previous week. However, the local note strengthened against several major currencies. It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.8171/8206 from 2.8419/8471, advanced versus the euro to 4.9281/9340 from 4.9447/9536, and appreciated against the British pound to 5.6345/6412 from 5.6775/6876. The ringgit also posted gains against regional peers. It improved against the Singapore dollar to 3.2630/2671 from 3.2744/2805, strengthened against the Philippine peso to 7.25/7.27 from 7.36/7.38, advanced against the Indonesian rupiah to 252.1/252.5 from 253.2/253.8, and climbed against the Thai baht to 13.0587/1069 from 13.1973/2271. title: Kospi Falls 2.45% On Tariff Jitters, Fed Rate Cut Doubts
body:
South Korea’s Kospi tumbled 2.45% to 3,386.05 on Sept 26, dragged down by renewed trade tensions and fading hopes for aggressive US rate cuts. Selling pressure intensified after US President Donald Trump demanded South Korea make “upfront” payments toward US investments and unveiled new tariffs on pharmaceuticals and industrial goods, heightening trade worries. Stronger-than-expected US inflation data also tempered expectations for further Federal Reserve (Fed) easing, prompting foreign and institutional investors to offload over 1.15 trillion won in shares. Samsung Electronics fell 3.25%, SK hynix dropped 5.61%, and Hyundai Motor slid 1.15%. The Korean won weakened to 1,412.4 per dollar, its lowest level since May. President Lee Jae Myung unveiled plans to shift the foreign exchange market to 24-hour trading to boost access and support Korea’s MSCI developed market ambitions. Analysts expect continued volatility as investors monitor US data, Fed signals and trade developments. Related

title: Hang Seng Tumbles 1.35% As Tariff Fears, Valuation Worries Take Hold
body:
Hong Kong equities closed sharply lower on Sept 26, with the Hang Seng Index falling 1.35 % to 26,128.20 amid fresh US tariff threats and concerns over frothy valuations. Heavy losses in the Tech and Pharma sectors dragged the broader market, as expectations for robust rate cuts by the US Federal Reserve cooled. The weekly picture wasn’t much brighter: The Hang Seng snapped its September momentum with a 1.6 % decline for the week. title: Wall Street Ends Lower As Data Clouds Rate-Cut Outlook
body:
US stocks finished weaker on Thursday as fresh economic data cast doubt on the pace of future interest rate cuts by the Federal Reserve. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 173.96 points or 0.38% to 45,947.32, the S&P 500 shed 33.25 points or 0.50% to 6,604.72, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 113.16 points or 0.50% to 22,384.70. Jobless claims fell by 14,000 to 218,000 last week, while revised figures showed faster US economic growth in the second quarter, supported by strong consumer spending and business investment. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warned against cutting rates too quickly, adding to market caution. The developments tempered expectations of another 25 basis-point cut in October, with the CME FedWatch Tool showing odds easing to 83.4% from 92% a day earlier. Investors now await Friday’s Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge. Most S&P 500 sectors closed in the red, though energy gained 0.9% and technology eked out a 0.03% increase as Intel surged 8.9% on reports of talks with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. CarMax plunged 20.1% after disappointing results, while Accenture slipped 2.7% despite beating revenue forecasts. The weakness on Wall Street is expected to weigh on Asian markets, with Singapore’s Straits Times Index opening marginally higher on Friday but broader sentiment cautious, while Hong Kong futures pointed lower and Japan’s Nikkei traded firmer. title: Ringgit Eases Against US Dollar As Strong US Data Lifts Greenback
body:
The ringgit weakened against the US dollar in early trade Friday, slipping to 4.2200/2300 from Thursday’s close of 4.2085/2120, as the greenback strengthened on upbeat US economic data. SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said a sharp drop in US weekly jobless claims and stronger second-quarter GDP growth at 3.8% had reinforced optimism over the US economy, easing concerns over President Donald Trump’s tariff policies. He noted the data could renew selling pressure on the ringgit as sentiment toward emerging markets stays defensive. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expects the ringgit to hover in the RM4.21 to RM4.22 range today, with the US Dollar Index maintaining its upward momentum. At the same time, the ringgit strengthened against the yen at 2.8146/8215, the euro at 4.9197/9313 and the pound at 5.6257/6390. It also firmed against the Singapore dollar and Thai baht, but slipped against the Philippine peso and was little changed versus the Indonesian rupiah. Related

title: Market Ends Higher As Malayan Cement, PetDag Lift Gains
body:
The stock market ended the trading day of Sept 26 on a firmer note as buying in selected blue chips and mid-cap stocks lifted sentiment, with market breadth turning positive despite profit-taking in heavyweight Nestle (M) Bhd. At the close, gainers narrowly outpaced losers 575 to 559, while 469 counters were unchanged, 1,047 untraded and 48 suspended. Turnover expanded to 4.16 billion shares worth RM3.17 billion, up from 3.55 billion shares worth RM2.77 billion yesterday. Malayan Cement Bhd emerged as the day’s biggest gainer, jumping 42 sen to RM7.15 on active buying interest with 27.2 million shares traded. Petronas Dagangan Bhd (PetDag) added 30 sen to RM22.42, while Country View Bhd advanced 23 sen to RM2.78. Dutch Lady Milk Industries Bhd rose 22 sen to RM27.28 and Ajinomoto (Malaysia) Bhd gained 20 sen to RM14.02. Meanwhile, Nestle led the losers’ list, sliding 56 sen to RM96.04. Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd slipped 30 sen to RM29.30, PPB Group Bhd lost 20 sen to RM10.12, while both Farm Fresh Bhd and Sunway Construction Group Bhd declined 14 sen each to RM2.27 and RM5.99, respectively. Analysts noted the improved trading value reflected stronger rotational play among investors, with interest seen in construction, consumer and cement-related counters. However, selling in select defensive plays capped further gains on the broader index. Related

title: Hang Seng Index Futures Extends Rally, Eyes Higher Ground At 28,500 Points
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) advised investors to maintain long positions on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) after the index posted a second consecutive rebound on Thursday, gaining 51 pts to close at 26,535 pts. The HSIF opened at 26,491 pts, reached a low of 26,368 pts and a high of 26,653 pts before settling at 26,535 pts, forming a bullish Doji candlestick. In the evening session, the index dipped 163 pts to 26,372 pts. Technical indicators remain supportive of the bullish trend. The RSI hooked higher, signalling improved momentum for the bulls, while the index continues to trade above the rising 20-day and 50-day SMA lines. Analysts noted that sustained positive strength could see the HSIF retest the 27,000-pt resistance, with a potential upside towards 28,500 pts. RHB Research recommended traders remain in long positions initiated at 21,416 pts (14 April close), with a stop-loss at 23,800 pts. The first support is identified at 25,000 pts, followed by 23,800 pts, while immediate resistance levels are pegged at 27,000 pts and 28,500 pts. Related

title: Gold Prices Hit New Highs Amid Global Gains
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia climbed to RM509,028 per kilogram (RM509.03 per gram) as of early Friday, 26 September 2025, reflecting a 0.42% increase or RM2,128 rise. On a daily basis, gold recorded a gain of RM61 per ounce, up 0.39%, while silver rose RM1.26 per gram, a 0.66% increase. The increase continues a broader upward trend, with gold up 9.48% over the past 30 days, 16.65% in six months, and 44.47% over the past year. Over five years, the price of gold has more than doubled, rising 101.13%, and in two decades it has surged 803.92%, highlighting its role as a long-term store of value. Silver mirrored this trend, rising 12.48% over the past month and 44.92% over the past year. Globally, gold has also been gaining. In US dollars, the annual increase for 2025 stands at 42.5%, while in euros it is 26.6% and in British pounds 33.8%. Gold has also recorded notable gains in other markets, with a 47.8% rise in India and 35.8% in Japan. Market observers note that ongoing economic uncertainty and global inflation pressures have driven demand for precious metals as a hedge, while fluctuations in currency rates continue to influence local prices. The Malaysian Ringgit’s performance against major currencies contributes to the upward momentum of gold domestically. Investors seeking exposure to precious metals in Malaysia can track prices per gram, kilogram, or ounce, with current market activity showing steady interest from both individual buyers and institutional players. Bursa Malaysia closed higher, with key indices rising modestly as gains were seen across blue-chip and mid-cap stocks. The benchmark FBMKLCI added 4.98 points, or 0.31%, to finish at 1,602.45, trading between 1,599.59 and 1,609.65 during the session. The FBM70 rose 60.08 points, or 0.36%, to 16,616.48, while the broader F4GBM index gained 3.71 points, or 0.39%, to 962.26. Trading was largely supported by broad-based buying in both consumer and industrial segments, while investors remained cautious ahead of upcoming corporate earnings announcements. Related

body:

title: KOSPI Gains On Bargain-Hunting, Tech And Defence Stocks Lead
body:
South Korean shares ended higher on Aug 22, lifted by bargain-hunting in heavyweight tech and defence stocks as investors looked ahead to signals from the US Federal Reserve (Fed). The benchmark KOSPI rose 0.86% to close at 3,168.73, with institutional and foreign investors buying a combined 339.7 billion won worth of shares, offsetting retail outflows of 458.5 billion won. Technology stocks led the rebound, with Samsung Electronics up 1.13% and SK hynix climbing 2.45% after a five-day losing streak. Turnover reached 8.21 trillion won on a volume of 233.9 million shares, with advancers outnumbering decliners 461 to 410. The Korean won also strengthened, closing at 1,393.65 won per US dollar compared to 1,398.30 won a day earlier. Analysts said the advance reflected investors positioning ahead of Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s Jackson Hole address, while lower stock valuations provided opportunities for selective buying. Related

title: Hong Kong Stocks End Higher As Fed Optimism Lifts Sentiment
body:
Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Aug 22, supported by renewed optimism over potential US interest-rate cuts and investor relief following the delisting of China Evergrande from the exchange. The Hang Seng Index rose 0.77% to finish at 25,339, tracking gains across Asia after US Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Jerome Powell hinted at the possibility of monetary easing during his Jackson Hole address. His remarks bolstered global risk appetite, with traders increasing bets on a September rate cut. The session also marked the formal delisting of China Evergrande, once the country’s largest property developer, capping years of turmoil linked to China’s property sector crisis. Markets took the move in stride, with analysts noting that the resolution helped ease lingering uncertainty over the sector. Investors said sentiment remained underpinned by external cues from the Fed, though caution persists as China’s economic recovery continues to show uneven momentum. Related

title: Dow Hits Record Close As Powell Signals Possible September Rate Cut
body:
Wall Street ended sharply higher on Aug 22, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average notching a record close after Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Jerome Powell hinted at a possible interest-rate cut as soon as September, Reuters reported. Powell, speaking at the Jackson Hole Symposium, underscored the need to watch upcoming jobs and inflation data but acknowledged conditions for easing policy were strengthening. Traders boosted bets on a September cut to nearly 90%, up from about 75% before his remarks. The Dow surged 846.24 points, or 1.89%, to 45,631.74, surpassing its previous record from December 2024. The S&P 500 climbed 1.52% to 6,466.91, while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.88% to 21,496.54. The Russell 2000 jumped 4.1% to a 2025 high, highlighting strong demand for rate-sensitive small-cap stocks. Gains were broad-based, with 10 of 11 S&P sectors rising. Consumer discretionary led with a 3.18% rally, while chipmakers powered the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index 2.7% higher. Tesla soared 6.2%, Intel gained 5.5% amid reports of a US government stake purchase, and Coinbase rallied 6.5% as crypto-linked shares caught a bid. The rally snapped a five-day losing streak for the S&P 500, which had been weighed down by profit-taking in megacap techs earlier in the week. For the week, both the Dow and S&P logged gains, while the Nasdaq slipped 0.6%. Investor sentiment was further buoyed by an upbeat outlook from UBS, which raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 for the second time in two months, citing resilient earnings, easing trade frictions and expectations of Fed support. Market breadth was overwhelmingly positive, with advancing stocks outpacing decliners by more than nine-to-one on the NYSE. Trading volume hit 17.93 billion shares, above the 20-day average. Related

title: Stock Today: SunCon Jumps 4.1% Following Strong Q2 Earnings
body:
Sunway Construction Group Bhd (SunCon) saw its stock climb 4.1% to RM6.09 as of 3.25 pm on Friday, with 12.1 million shares traded. The stock opened at RM5.96, hitting a high of RM6.20 and a low of RM5.96, reflecting robust investor interest after the company posted impressive second-quarter results. The construction firm reported a 127% surge in revenue to RM1,476.9 million for Q2 FY2025, up from RM651.2 million a year earlier. Profit before tax rose 144% to RM122.6 million, while net profit jumped 118% to RM83 million, driven primarily by accelerated progress on data centre projects. SunCon’s construction segment led the earnings growth, recording a 140% increase in revenue to RM1,433.5 million, with profit before tax climbing 159% to RM121.4 million. The strong performance was underpinned by peak construction activity across multiple data centre developments, boosting overall margins. For the first half of FY2025, the group more than doubled its revenue to RM2,877.4 million, compared with RM1,256.0 million in the same period last year. Profit before tax jumped 157% to RM235.8 million, from RM91.9 million previously, highlighting the company’s strengthened earnings visibility. SunCon also declared a second interim single-tier dividend of 7.25 sen per share for FY2025, bringing the total interim dividends for the year to 12.25 sen per share. As of June 2025, the group’s outstanding order book stood at RM6.72 billion, with new contracts worth RM3.81 billion secured, covering projects such as data centres, transit-oriented development, and prefabricated components. title: Stock Today: Citaglobal Climbs On New FT3 Road Upgrade Deal
body:
Citaglobal Bhd edged higher on Bursa Malaysia as of 4.09 pm, closing at RM0.820, up 0.61% or RM0.005, with 327,800 shares traded. The stock opened at RM0.820, touched an intraday high of RM0.820 and a low of RM0.815, while the last average closing price stood at RM0.815. The modest gain comes on the back of Citaglobal’s recent RM168.88 million contract award from Malaysia’s Public Works Department (JKR) for the FT3 Road Upgrade project. The contract adds to the group’s orderbook, now valued at RM1.3 billion, and covers the upgrading of existing roads, six bridges, five junctions, earthworks, geotechnical works, drainage, road pavement, road furniture, traffic management, road and traffic lights, and other miscellaneous works. The FT3 Federal road project will expand the Jalan Kota Bharu–Kuala Terengganu stretch from a two-lane single carriageway into a four-lane dual carriageway built to JKR standards. Spanning 739 kilometres from Rantau Panjang in Kelantan, bordering Thailand, down to Johor Bahru, the contract is scheduled for completion within 42 months from site possession. The new contract underscores Citaglobal’s growing presence in major infrastructure projects, providing investors with confidence in the group’s revenue visibility amid ongoing government development initiatives. title: Ringgit Edges Up Ahead Of Powell’s Jackson Hole Speech
body:
The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar on Friday as markets turned cautious before Federal Reserve chairman Jerome Powell’s address at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium later in the day. At 8 am, the local note stood at RM4.2200/2400 versus Thursday’s close of RM4.2235/2275. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit had appreciated 0.04% against the greenback yesterday and was likely to remain rangebound between RM4.22 and RM4.23 until Powell’s remarks provide fresh policy signals. The US Dollar Index was firmer at 98.619, up 0.41%, underpinned by stronger business sentiment. The US Flash Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index climbed to an eight-month high of 55.4, driven by services sector resilience and improving factory activity. However, survey responses pointed to higher import tariffs squeezing costs and margins, with many businesses set to pass them on to consumers. The ringgit was also stronger against other major currencies, rising to 5.6616/6884 against the British pound from 5.6899/6953, edging up to 2.8431/8568 versus the Japanese yen from 2.8595/8626, and at 4.8998/9231 against the euro from 4.9226/9263. Among ASEAN peers, the local note firmed to 3.2741/2899 against the Singapore dollar, 12.9139/9822 against the Thai baht, and 259.0/260.4 versus the Indonesian rupiah. It was unchanged against the Philippine peso at 7.40/7.44. Related

title: KLCI Opens Higher As Markets Eye Powell’s Jackson Hole Remarks
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened stronger on Friday, in line with cautious optimism across regional markets as investors awaited policy cues from US Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell’s speech at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium later tonight. At 9.11 am, the benchmark FBM KLCI rose 4.39 points or 0.28% to 1,597.26, after moving between 1,593.42 and 1,598.00. The broader market was also firmer, with the FBM70 up 0.33% at 16,591.13, the FBMEMAS advancing 0.28% to 11,833.51 and the FBMSHA gaining 0.30% at 11,752.85. The upbeat start on Bursa followed overnight declines on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all retreated as traders scaled back expectations of a September rate cut. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has maintained its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF), noting that the index continues to consolidate above key support levels while sustaining a bullish structure. Immediate support is set at 23,800 points, followed by 23,000 points. Related

title: Gold In Ringgit Retreats Slightly Amid Profit-Taking
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia edged lower on Friday, with the precious metal slipping 0.14% to RM452.81 per gram. On a daily basis, gold shed RM0.63 per gram, extending a modest decline in line with broader market trends. Over the past month, gold in ringgit terms fell RM98.57, representing a 0.69% decline, although longer-term performance remains strong. Year-to-date, gold has surged RM1,103.36 or 8.49%, while the past year has seen a jump of RM3,116.05, marking a 28.36% increase. Over five years, gold has added RM6,035.46, or 74.81%, and over two decades, the gain has been substantial at RM12,447.38, translating to a 751.54% rise. The retreat in gold prices reflects modest profit-taking amid a backdrop of mixed global economic signals, though the long-term trend continues to show the metal as a hedge against inflation and currency volatility. title: KLCI Edges Higher At Midday As Selective Buying Supports Market
body:
Bursa Malaysia traded slightly higher at midday on Thursday, supported by selective buying in heavyweights despite a mixed broader market. At 12.30 pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 2.97 points to 1,532.76 after moving between 1,529.71 and 1,533.08 earlier in the session. The broader market saw the FBMEMAS index adding 13.55 points to 11,508.09, while the FBM70 slipped marginally by 4.32 points to 16,639.77. The FBMSHA index gained 16.79 points to 11,533.27. Trading remained active with Nexgram Holdings (NEXG) leading the most active list at 52 sen with 379.9 million shares traded, followed by Zetrix Bhd at 92 sen, down 2.5 sen with 358.6 million shares. Tanco Holdings inched up 0.5 sen to 92 sen. title: Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher As Anwar’s Cash Aid And Fuel Price Cut Lift Sentiment
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened marginally higher today, buoyed by improved market sentiment following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement of a series of economic measures yesterday, including cash handouts and fuel price cuts. At 9.03 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.66 points to 1,531.45 from yesterday’s close of 1,529.79. The benchmark index moved between 1,531.73 and 1,531.05 in early trade. Broader market performance was also positive, with the FBM 70 adding 49.18 points to 16,693.27, and the FBM Emas rising 18.72 points to 11,513.26. Market participants remain optimistic after Anwar announced a one-off RM100 cash aid for all Malaysian adults via MyKad, doubling the allocation for Rahmah MADANI Sales to RM600 million, and fixing the RON95 petrol price at RM1.99 per litre under a new targeted subsidy plan. These measures are expected to ease cost-of-living pressures and boost consumer spending. Among the most active stocks in early trade were NexG Resources, unchanged at 52 sen with 279.8 million shares traded, TWL Holdings flat at 2.5 sen, and SFP Tech up 1 sen to 20.5 sen. Related

body:
US stock markets closed Tuesday on a mixed note as fresh trade developments and lacklustre corporate earnings tempered investor enthusiasm. The S&P 500 edged up 0.1% to another record high, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.4%, dragged lower by chipmakers including Nvidia. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.4%, or 179 points, buoyed by optimism surrounding international trade pacts. President Donald Trump announced new trade agreements with the Philippines and Indonesia, adding to a flurry of recent economic diplomacy. Investors are now closely watching for further announcements ahead of the 1 August White House deadline, which could see broader tariffs imposed on other countries. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted that US-China trade ties were in a “very good place,” suggesting a truce could be extended, but reiterated that the August deadline remains firm for new levies. Meanwhile, earnings season continued with mixed results from blue-chip companies. General Motors saw its profit shrink despite stronger sales, with automotive tariffs weighing heavily on margins. Its shares dropped 8.1% on the news. RTX also saw a hit to earnings, prompting the aerospace and defence giant to slash its annual profit forecast, sending its stock lower. Lockheed Martin and Coca-Cola also reported results, though market reaction remained relatively muted. With geopolitical tensions and trade policies driving corporate uncertainty, investors remain cautious on outlooks. Beyond equities, gold prices surged 1.1% to a record high of US$3,439.20 per troy ounce, supported by a weaker dollar and falling Treasury yields. The 10-year Treasury yield declined to 4.337%, offering some relief to rate-sensitive sectors. Bitcoin rose 2.2% to US$119,342, continuing its recent rally amid broader risk appetite. Global markets were mixed. Major European indices slipped, while Hong Kong and mainland China stocks posted gains as regional investors digested the latest global trade signals. title: Singapore Market Opens Calm, Eyes Global Cues
body:
The Straits Times Index (STI) opened marginally higher on morning, gaining 5.10 points or 0.12% to 4,213.36, buoyed by broader optimism in regional markets and sustained gains among heavyweight counters such as DBS and ST Engineering. Early trading saw 276.79 million securities changing hands with a total market turnover of S$219.48 million. Market breadth was positive, with 169 gainers against 79 decliners, signalling cautious optimism amid ongoing global and regional developments. Financial stocks led the morning upside, with DBS rising 0.53% to S$47.50 and OCBC inching up to S$17.14. The gains came as investors weighed the impact of OCBC lowering its 2025 inflation forecast for Malaysia to 1.5%, a move that could signal easing regional cost pressures and improved consumer sentiment. Meanwhile, ST Engineering continued to attract investor interest, trading at S$8.34, as defence-related sentiment remained elevated following Malaysia’s heightened engagement with Türkiye’s military sector. The developments may have stirred investor appetite for regional defence and engineering plays. Singtel and ComfortDelGro traded flat, while Genting Singapore hovered at S$0.745, with tourism-linked stocks showing mixed signals amid ongoing discussions over Southeast Asia’s recovery momentum. The iEdge suite of indices also reflected broader strength in ESG and regional financial segments, with the iEdge-UOB APAC Yield Focus Green REIT Index gaining, in tandem with a firm showing across Singapore REITs. Investor attention is expected to remain focused on upcoming US tech earnings and regional economic prints, particularly China’s stimulus signals and ASEAN trade data, which could provide further catalysts for SGX stocks in the days ahead. title: Hang Seng Index Futures Eyes 26,000 As Bulls Take The Reins
body:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has reiterated its long position on the Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) as the index continues to chart an upward path, closing 150 points higher at 25,134 during Tuesday’s trading. The index began the session at 24,986 and briefly touched a low of 24,916 before surging to a high of 25,168, ending near the peak with a strong bullish candlestick. This pattern further reinforces the ongoing uptrend. In the evening session, HSIF added another 187 points, last seen at 25,321. RHB Research noted that the bullish momentum remains intact, supported by the Relative Strength Index (RSI) staying above the 50% level and the upward slope of both the 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages (SMA). With these technical indicators aligned positively, the index is expected to head towards the 26,000 resistance level in the near term. The firm has advised traders to maintain their long positions, first initiated at 21,416 on 14 April, with a stop-loss set at 23,000 to manage downside risk. Immediate support is identified at 23,800, while resistance levels are seen at 26,000 and subsequently at 27,000 if the bullish trend continues. Related

title: Gold Price In Malaysia Slips 0.33% As Global Momentum Points To Further Upside
body:
Gold prices in Malaysia dipped slightly despite continued bullish sentiment in global markets, with the local rate for the precious metal easing by 0.33% or RM1.54 per gram to RM465.08 per kilogram as at 2.41 am New York time, according to data from GoldPrice.org. In daily terms, the metal saw a decrease of RM48.52. However, gold’s long-term trajectory remains positive, with a 3.04% gain over the past 30 days and a sharp 28.64% rise over the past year. Over five years, prices have soared by 79.17%, while 20-year gains stand at a staggering 803.42%. Globally, COMEX Gold extended its rally for the third consecutive session, surging US$37.30 to settle at US$3,443.70, having traded as high as US$3,447.50 during intraday movement. RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) noted the strong bullish momentum, backed by a rising RSI and long bullish candlestick patterns, indicating that an upside breakout could be imminent. The investment bank maintained its long position initiated at US$3,402.40, with expectations that the metal could break above US$3,450 and potentially reach US$3,600. Immediate support remains at US$3,250, with a stop-loss set at US$3,150. Despite today’s local dip, the broader bullish narrative continues to support gold’s haven appeal amid ongoing economic uncertainties and anticipated monetary policy shifts. Related

title: Bursa Opens On Cautious Note As Global Trade Talks Influence Markets
body:
Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark FBMKLCI opened with modest gains on Wednesday morning, climbing 1.38 points or 0.09% to 1,520.78, as cautious sentiment returned ahead of the new US tariff deadline looming on August 1 and fresh trade developments from Washington. The early session saw 276.79 million shares traded, valued at RM219.48 million, with 169 stocks advancing compared to 79 decliners, a modest preference for buying amid lingering regional uncertainties. Asian markets took their cue from mixed overnight US and European performance, as investors remain hesitant while awaiting progress in US trade talks with partners including Japan, the Philippines, and Indonesia. The unresolved tariff saga continues to cast a shadow, in contrast to earlier optimism when a US court blocked certain Trump-era tariffs, a decision that had briefly buoyed markets in May. On Bursa, small-cap and ACE Market stocks are drawing attention, notably NexG, which rose to RM0.52 on strong volume, echoing a resurgence in IPO and technology-focused counters as Malaysia anticipates more listings later this year. Financial shares remained relatively steady; however, sentiment is being tempered by global cost and trade pressures amid renewed US tariff concerns. Market analysts suggest the FBMKLCI may remain within the 1,510–1,530 range as investors await clarity from the US trade deadline, with eyes also on upcoming Wall Street earnings and the Fed’s policy signals. In the near term, Bursa will likely be influenced by any developments on the US trade front, domestic IPO momentum and movements in global equity markets, particularly in China and ASEAN, all factors that will shape investor sentiment for the remainder of the week. On Bursa, small-cap and ACE Market stocks are drawing attention, notably NexG, which rose to RM0.52 on strong volume, echoing a resurgence in IPO and technology-focused counters as Malaysia anticipates more listings later this year. Financial shares remained relatively steady; however, sentiment is being tempered by global cost and trade pressures amid renewed US tariff concerns. Market analysts suggest the FBMKLCI may remain within the 1,510–1,530 range as investors await clarity from the US trade deadline, with eyes also on upcoming Wall Street earnings and the Fed’s policy signals. In the near term, Bursa will likely be influenced by any developments on the US trade front, domestic IPO momentum and movements in global equity markets, particularly in China and ASEAN, all factors that will shape investor sentiment for the remainder of the week.
