title: Cuckoo Malaysia’s Bursa Listing: A Defining Moment For Consumer Wellness
body:
As a recognised disruptor and market innovator, CUCKOO International (MAL) Bhd (CUCKOO Malaysia) — known for its cutting-edge Korean-inspired home and wellness solutions — is poised to mark a major milestone with its upcoming debut on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia Securities. This listing signals the company’s ambitious expansion strategy and its intent to deepen its foothold in the Malaysian consumer tech space. Yet, the broader IPO landscape has not been as buoyant as in previous years. With subdued investor sentiment and mixed performances in the consumer appliance sector — as seen in the experiences of Senheng and Panasonic Malaysia — the spotlight is firmly on CUCKOO Malaysia. The key question: What unique value proposition does CUCKOO Malaysia bring to the table to reinvigorate investor confidence and stand out in a competitive market? Ahead of its listing, BusinessToday spoke with Chief Executive Officer Hoe Kian Choon to understand the rationale behind the timing, the earlier postponement from April and how CUCKOO Malaysia plans to distinguish itself as a future-ready consumer-tech leader. IPO Timing: “The Right Moment” Hoe shares that the rental-based home appliance and household goods segment is projected to grow at a CAGR of 9.9% from 2024 to 2029 Originally slated for listing on April 30, CUCKOO Malaysia chose to delay the move due to global market volatility. However, Hoe is confident that the time is now ripe for a successful debut. “We view this year as the right time for our IPO, supported by our strong financial fundamentals and dominant position in a rapidly growing industry,” said Hoe. He pointed to the rental-based home appliance and household goods segment — a market projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.9% from 2024 to 2029. With current market penetration estimated at just 10%-15%, Hoe sees significant untapped potential. “The delay wasn’t a setback, but a strategic decision to further strengthen our fundamentals and ensure we enter the market from a position of strength,” he noted. CUCKOO Malaysia has raised approximately RM154.74 million in gross proceeds from the IPO. The funds will catalyse strategic initiatives across multiple fronts, including product diversification and expansion, omnichannel distribution, including new cash-and-carry stores, operational improvements, regional expansion in Malaysia and Singapore, and debt reduction to enhance financial flexibility. “The IPO proceeds are not just about scaling,” said Hoe. “They’re about building a future-proof company rooted in innovation and operational excellence.” A Differentiated Model: Recurring Revenue and Dividends While many tech listings on Bursa Malaysia have struggled to gain traction, CUCKOO Malaysia believes its subscription-based rental model sets it apart. “Our model generates stable, recurring income — an attractive proposition for both retail and institutional investors,” Hoe explained. More compellingly, CUCKOO Malaysia plans to offer a dividend payout ratio of at least 20% of net profit annually, balancing short-term investor returns with long-term strategic growth. Post-listing, CUCKOO Malaysia is planning to expand beyond water and air purifiers CUCKOO Malaysia’s post-listing blueprint is built on vertical diversification and market depth. Hoe shared that the company’s plans to expand beyond water and air purifiers into a broader portfolio. “There’s a huge opportunity in cross-selling. Currently, over 70% of our customers own just one CUCKOO product — that’s a goldmine we’re ready to tap into,” said Hoe. The company has collaborative partnerships with brands like Fujiaire, Ogawa, Wonderlab, WonderKlean, and WonderDewi. Future-Proofing: Scaling with Agility Hoe acknowledged the operational risks of scaling, from reliance on limited sales channels to logistics challenges. To address these, CUCKOO Malaysia is building a robust omnichannel ecosystem, expanding its service hubs and investing in digital transformation. “Our goal is to increase delivery capability from 31.3% in 2024 to 83% by the end of 2025. It’s a bold target, but it reflects our ambition,” he said. CUCKOO Malaysia is building a robust omnichannel ecosystem, expanding its service hubs and investing in digital transformation to address the issue of limited sales channels and logistics challenges Key to this transformation is CUCKOO Malaysia’s focus on data-driven insights and digital infrastructure to ensure the company remains agile in a fast-evolving landscape. Reflecting on CUCKOO Malaysia’s IPO journey, Hoe emphasised that the listing is not just about raising funds. “This IPO is about catalysing a broader transformation — redefining consumer wellness, deepening customer trust and setting new standards for resilience in a volatile market,” he said. “For investors, CUCKOO Malaysia offers a rare combination of recurring income, dividend potential and visionary leadership. For the industry, we represent a new category of consumer-tech companies — one rooted in sustainability, wellness and innovation.” CUCKOO Malaysia will be listed on the Bursa Securities Main Market on June 24 after an earlier scheduled date of April 30. The listing exercise will be among the most anticipated for the year, with a valuation estimate of RM1.55 billion. Related

title: Stock Today: Malakoff Edges Up On 22MW WTE Boost
body:
Shares of Malakoff Corp Bhd rose slightly on Friday following news of a key concession secured by its subsidiary for a waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Melaka. As at 11.51am, the counter was trading at RM0.790, up 0.64% or 0.005 sen from the previous close, with 7.1 million shares changing hands. It opened at RM0.785 and hit a high of RM0.795. Buy and sell volumes stood at 1.74 million and 879,000 shares respectively. The movement comes a day after the company announced that Sungai Udang WTE Sdn Bhd, a joint venture 60%-owned by Malakoff, had entered into a 34-year Public Private Partnership Concession Agreement with the federal government. The agreement allows the company to design, build, operate and eventually demolish a WTE facility that will process 1,056 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily, generating 22MW of renewable energy to be sold to Tenaga Nasional Berhad. The facility is expected to begin construction in 2026, subject to financing and regulatory approvals. Related

title: Ringgit Edges Up Against Greenback Despite Global Jitters
body:
The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, even as investors remained cautious amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. At 8am, the local note stood at RM4.2490/2700 versus the greenback, appreciating from Thursday’s close of RM4.2590/2625. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd Chief Economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid attributed the gains to a slight pullback in the US Dollar Index (DXY), which stayed below the 100-point level. “This signals that traders may be rotating into other major currencies or alternative asset classes for safety,” he told local media. Nevertheless, he warned that the ringgit may stay under pressure in the near term given persistent global uncertainties. “Market sentiment is expected to remain cautious as traders closely monitor the Israel-Iran conflict and the US’ potential response,” he said. In broader trading, the ringgit was mostly lower against major currencies. It slipped against the British pound to RM5.7264/7547 from RM5.7164/7211 and eased against the euro at RM4.8910/9152 compared to RM4.8868/8908. It, however, firmed slightly versus the Japanese yen at RM2.9257/9404 from RM2.9286/9312. Regionally, the ringgit posted gains across most ASEAN currencies. It rose to RM3.3051/3219 against the Singapore dollar from RM3.3072/3102, and to RM12.9883/13.0593 versus the Thai baht from RM12.9966/13.0513. The local unit also strengthened against the Indonesian rupiah at 258.9/260.3 and the Philippine peso at 7.39/7.44. Related

title: Wall Street Wavers As Fed Sticks To Two Rate Cuts Amid Tariff Uncertainty
body:
US stocks ended Wednesday on a mixed note after the Federal Reserve signalled it still expects two interest rate cuts in 2025, although Chair Jerome Powell warned the outlook remains clouded by economic and geopolitical uncertainties. The S&P 500 edged down 1.85 points to 5,980.87, a marginal dip of less than 0.1%, after swinging between modest gains and losses throughout the session. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 44.14 points, or 0.1%, to 42,171.66, while the Nasdaq composite advanced 0.1%, adding 25.18 points to 19,546.27. Investors were digesting the Fed’s latest projections, which maintained the forecast of two rate cuts by year-end, matching the projection from three months ago. However, Powell noted, “It’s just a forecast in a very foggy time,” as uncertainty over President Donald Trump’s tariff measures and their inflationary impact complicate policymaking. In the bond market, the 10-year Treasury yield inched down to 4.38% from 4.39%, while the 2-year yield held steady at 3.94%, reflecting uncertainty over the Fed’s next move. Among notable movers, Nucor jumped 3.3% after announcing it expects profit growth across all business segments in the second quarter, supported by stronger prices at its mills. Meanwhile, economic data presented a mixed picture: initial jobless claims declined, suggesting labour market resilience, but housing starts fell short of expectations, signalling continued pressure from elevated mortgage rates. Global markets also posted mixed performances, with Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 rising 0.9%, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng lost 1.1%. Bloomberg Related

title: Stock Today: DNeX Flat At Midday Despite RM103 Million Finance System Contract Win
body:
Shares of Dagang NeXchange Bhd (DNeX) were unchanged at RM0.290 as of 2.41pm today, despite securing a major public sector contract earlier this week. The counter opened higher at RM0.300 but slipped to an intraday low of RM0.290, where it last traded. Trading volume stood at 65.6 million shares, with strong buying interest reflected in 36.1 million buy orders, compared to 19.7 million on the sell side. DNeX recently announced that its subsidiary, Innovation Associates Consulting, had clinched a RM103.76 million contract from the Ministry of Finance Malaysia to provide continued services for the Integrated Government Financial and Management System (iGFMAS). The five-year contract includes application enhancement, system support, and maintenance services—cementing DNeX’s role in supporting the digital infrastructure of Malaysia’s federal financial operations. Despite the positive development, the stock remained flat, possibly due to broader market sentiment or profit-taking after previous gains. DNeX last closed at RM0.290 with no percentage change. title: Stock Market Continues In Negative Territory As Losers Outpace Gainers 2-to-1
body:
The stock market closed on a softer note on June 19, with market breadth firmly negative as decliners outpaced gainers 660 to 298, while 460 counters remained unchanged and 1,005 were untraded. Eleven stocks were suspended. Trading activity picked up slightly, with total turnover rising to 2.81 billion shares valued at RM1.69 billion compared to 2.42 billion shares worth RM1.79 billion on June 18. Investor sentiment remained cautious, with notable losses seen across heavyweight and consumer-related counters. Heineken Malaysia Bhd led the top losers, falling 46 sen to RM26.42, followed by PPB Group Bhd, which dropped 41 sen to RM9.97 and Petronas Dagangan Bhd down 38 sen to RM20.98. Other key decliners included Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, shedding 30 sen to RM19.72, and Panasonic Manufacturing Malaysia Bhd, losing 28 sen to RM11.50. Apollo Food Holdings Bhd and Hong Leong Financial Group Bhd rounded up the top gainers for the trading session, with the counters gaining 11 sen and 10 sen each to close at RM6.50 and RM16, respectively. Overall, the local bourse mirrored a mixed regional tone amid lingering concerns over global economic headwinds and cautious corporate earnings outlooks. Related

title: Nikkei Slips From Four-Month High On Middle East Tensions
body:
Japan’s Nikkei 225 Index fell 0.8% on Thursday, pulling back from a four-month peak as geopolitical fears surrounding the Israel-Iran conflict and the potential involvement of the United States dampened investor appetite for risk assets. The broader Topix Index also declined, losing 0.6%. The market retreat halted a three-day winning streak that had lifted the Nikkei to its highest level since Feb 20. Tensions in the Middle East continued to cloud sentiment as the conflict between Israel and Iran entered its seventh day. Nomura strategist Fumika Shimizu commented, “Heightened tensions in the Middle East continue to cool investor sentiment, with the downside appearing to widen.” In terms of market breadth, decliners far outpaced advancers, with 175 stocks down on the Nikkei compared to just 48 gainers. Taiyo Yuden led the laggards, dropping 3.1%, while Sumitomo Pharma fell 3%. However, not all was negative on the board. Nippon Steel Corp stood out as the top performer, surging 4.3% after finalising its long-awaited US$14.9 billion acquisition of US Steel, a move seen as bolstering its global footprint. Investor caution intensified after US President Donald Trump offered ambiguous signals regarding possible American involvement in airstrikes against Iran’s nuclear facilities. The uncertainty prompted a flight from equities into safer assets, cutting short the Nikkei’s upward momentum. Reuters Related

title: Singapore Stocks Edge Higher Amid Global Trade Optimism And Earnings Boost
body:
The Singapore stock market posted modest gains for the week ending May 16, buoyed by easing global trade tensions and positive corporate earnings. The benchmark Straits Times Index closed at 3,891.94 on May 15, up 0.54% for the day, marking a steady climb from earlier in the week. The Singapore Exchange was closed on May 16 in observance of Vesak Day. Investor sentiment improved as US-China trade discussions showed signs of progress, alleviating concerns over escalating tariffs. This global optimism contributed to a rebound in Asian markets, including Singapore. On the corporate front, Singapore Airlines reported a 2.8% increase in revenue to S$19.5 billion for the fiscal year 2025, surpassing analyst expectations. The airline’s net income rose 3.9% to S$2.78 billion, though earnings per share slightly missed forecasts. However, not all sectors fared equally. The property sector experienced some volatility, with City Developments Ltd facing investor scrutiny amid ongoing boardroom disputes. Looking ahead, market participants will be closely monitoring upcoming economic indicators and global trade developments, which are expected to influence the STI’s trajectory in the coming weeks. title: Ringgit Rises Ahead Of Malaysia’s Q1 GDP Release
body:
The ringgit opened stronger against the US dollar on Friday, continuing its positive trajectory as markets await the release of Malaysia’s first-quarter (1Q) 2025 gross domestic product (GDP) data. At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.2705/2920 against the greenback, strengthening from Thursday’s close of 4.2795/2870. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said investors are eyeing the GDP announcement closely, with advance estimates pointing to a 4.4% expansion. “The data will be a key factor in Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) decision on whether to ease monetary policy, as well as the forecast for GDP growth this year,” he said. “As such, we expect ringgit to trade more cautiously today,” he told local media. At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies. It appreciated against the British pound to 5.6819/7105 from 5.6862/6961 and rose against the euro to 4.7800/8040 from 4.7939/8023. However, it edged lower versus the Japanese yen to 2.9338/9490 from 2.9326/9379. Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit was mixed. It climbed against the Singapore dollar to 3.2931/3102 from 3.2950/3010, and gained on the Philippine peso at 7.66/7.70 from 7.67/7.69. It also advanced on the Indonesian rupiah to 258.3/259.7 from 258.8/259.4 but slipped against the Thai baht to 12.8630/9367 from 12.8198/8488. Commenting on the broader currency landscape, Mohd Afzanizam highlighted a weaker US Dollar Index (DXY), which declined by 0.16% to 100.87 points. He also noted that the US Producer Price Index (PPI) moderated to 2.4% year-on-year in April, down from 3.4% in both February and March, signalling a cooling inflation trend. “This suggests that inflation in the US will continue to ease and create more room for the US Federal Reserve (Fed) to cut rates this year,” he said. However, he cautioned that recent remarks from Fed chair Jerome Powell may dampen expectations of imminent rate cuts. “Powell’s speech at the Thomas Laubach Research Conference in Washington hinted that the inflation trend is likely to be more erratic due to the supply shocks, which have become more frequent and potentially more persistent. “This could mean the Fed is not keen to ease its monetary policy stance in the near term, which would affect the ringgit,” he said. title: Gold Prices Slip As Selling Pressure Eases; Support Seen At US$3,150
body:
As of early May 2025, gold prices in Malaysia traded at RM13,725.68 per ounce, down RM82.77 or 0.60% for the day. Over the past 30 days, prices have fallen 5.52%, but remain up 22.08% year-on-year, reflecting sustained long-term gains despite short-term volatility. According to RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research), COMEX Gold managed to rebound from the medium-term moving average line and closed at US$3,226.60, attempting to resume an upward movement. The metal opened Thursday’s session at US$3,180.80, dipped to a low of US$3,123.30, then surged to a high of US$3,244.30 before closing with a bullish candlestick. “The latest price action shows the selling pressure has eased off while an immediate support has formed at the US$3,150 level. Riding on the renewed momentum, the commodity may attempt to test the US$3,300 resistance. However, expect strong selling pressure to emerge at the overhead resistance,” RHB Research noted. The 20-day simple moving average (SMA) is trending downwards, signalling continued downside pressure. Should selling intensify, gold prices may break below US$3,150 and retrace towards the next support at US$3,000. RHB Research advises traders to maintain short positions initiated at US$3,188.30 or on the close of May 14, with a stop-loss set at US$3,400. Key resistance levels are at US$3,300 and US$3,400, while support lies at US$3,150 and US$3,000. Related

title: FBM KLCI Opens Firmer At 1,574.94 Amid Mixed Broader Market
body:
Bursa Malaysia opened marginally higher on Friday, with the benchmark index inching up amid a mixed performance across the broader market. At 9.12 am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) added 1.92 points to 1,574.94 after moving between a high of 1,576.57 and a low of 1,574.03. The broader market performance remained mixed. The FBM 70 Index slipped 47.81 points to 16,763.37, while the FBM Emas Index rose slightly by 3.07 points to 11,777.08. The FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index (F4GBM) was up 0.06 point to 949.10, indicating marginal optimism among ESG-focused counters. However, the FBM ACE Index and FBM Shariah Index both showed weakness, with the latter falling 13.19 points to 11,705.43. Trading activity was driven by small-cap and penny stocks in early trade. Westriver emerged as the most actively traded counter, climbing 1.5 sen to 37 sen with over 190.7 million shares exchanged. This was followed by HM, which edged up 0.5 sen to 18 sen on a volume of 120.6 million shares, and Sumi, which gained 1 sen to 20 sen with 90.7 million shares traded. FIBRO saw a sharper gain, adding 4 sen to 54.5 sen on active retail interest, while SFP Tech slid 1 sen to 25.5 sen. Investors are expected to remain cautious as they await Malaysia’s first quarter GDP announcement and external cues from global markets. Analysts noted that while the FBM KLCI shows signs of resilience, volatility is likely to persist amid mixed signals from regional economies and ongoing developments in the US interest rate trajectory. title: Dialog Shares Dip 5% Amid Margin Recovery Concerns, EPS Cut for FY25
body:
Dialog Group Bhd’s shares fell 5.08% to RM1.68 as of 3.47pm on May 16, amid weaker-than-expected financial results and a downward revision of its FY25 earnings forecast by Kenanga Research. The company reported a core profit of RM291.9 million for the nine-month period ended FY25, falling short of both Kenanga’s and consensus expectations at 60% and 56% of full-year estimates respectively. The main drag was a slower-than-anticipated recovery in the Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Commissioning (EPCC) division margins, though the segment broke even in the latest quarter. Kenanga has revised its FY25 forecast earnings down by 10%, citing a less aggressive EPCC margin recovery (from -20% to -26%). However, FY26 estimates remain unchanged, with the research house expecting no repeat of prior cost overruns. Dialog declared a quarterly dividend of RM0.013, bringing the cumulative payout to RM0.037 per share. The stock saw a high of RM1.72 and low of RM1.65 during the trading day, with 15.26 million shares traded. Despite the sell-off, Kenanga has maintained its ‘Outperform’ rating and SoP-based target price of RM1.94, seeing medium-term upside potential. On a year-on-year basis, Dialog’s 9MFY25 revenue dropped 15% and core profit slipped 16%, largely due to lower contributions from the EPCC and upstream segments. Quarter-on-quarter, revenue also dipped 15%, but core profit surged, thanks to a 39% drop in operating expenses and stronger joint venture contributions. The outlook for tank terminal operations remains resilient, while the Phase 3 Pengerang expansion, including ChemOne’s proposed aromatics project, is still under discussion and not yet factored into earnings projections. title: Cheers To Gains: Heineken Tops Bursa
body:
Heineken Malaysia Bhd emerged as the top gainer on Bursa Malaysia today, with its share price rising 2.08% to RM28.40 as of 4.30pm, fuelled by growing investor confidence in its earnings resilience and strategic advantage in the tourism-driven recovery. The brewer’s stock added 58 sen, outperforming the broader market, with trading volume hitting 1.85 million shares. It opened at RM27.84, dipped to RM27.50, and peaked at RM28.68 during intraday trading. Analysts from RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) and Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) have both reaffirmed their BUY calls on Heineken, citing upside potential driven by its robust brand positioning and positive macroeconomic indicators. RHB Research has set a target price of RM31.30, while HLIB is more bullish at RM35.56—translating to total return expectations of 17% and 34.4% respectively from prior valuations. Despite a 3% year-on-year dip in revenue to RM764 million in the first quarter of FY25, Heineken’s net profit held steady at RM122 million. Analysts attribute the temporary revenue slip to the earlier Lunar New Year, which front-loaded sales into the final quarter of FY24. However, improved operational efficiency helped sustain margins. title: Bursa Slides on Broad-Based Selloff With Nestle, MPI Among Top Losers
body:
Ongoing profit-taking continued to drag the stock market, mirroring the downbeat performance of key regional markets. This resulted in the decliners thumping the gainers 613 to 380, while 481 counters ended unchanged, 922 were untraded and eight were suspended. Market activity also tapered off, with total turnover falling to 2.91 billion shares valued at RM2.16 billion compared to 3.71 billion shares worth RM2.74 billion recorded on May 15. Leading the decliners, Nestle (M) Bhd closed its trading week on a massive drop as the counter fell RM2.32 to RM81.68, followed by Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd which dropped 42 sen to RM21.28, Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd and United Plantations Bhd decreased 32 sen to RM20.38 and RM22, respectively, and rounding off the top decliners for May 16 is Sam Engineering & Equipment (M) Bhd which eased 26 sen to RM4.20. Alternatively, Heineken Malaysia Bhd ended its trading week positively as the counter added 58 sen to close RM28.40, LPI Capital Bhd grew 38 sen to RM14.76, Kluang Rubber Company (Malaya) Bhd increased 33 sen to RM5.89, Ayer Holdings Bhd surged 29 sen to RM7.99 and Negri Sembilan Oil Palms Bhd jumped 18 sen to RM4.49. title: Bursa Malaysia Edges Lower At Midday Amid Broad-Based Weakness
body:
Bursa Malaysia drifted lower at midday, weighed by persistent profit-taking across key indices despite selective buying in active small-cap stocks. At 12.35pm, the FBM KLCI slipped 1.42 points to 1,571.60, having traded between 1,570.20 and 1,580.06. Broader market sentiment was subdued, with the FBM 70 falling 134.45 points to 16,676.73 and the FBM Emas Index easing 37.47 points to 11,736.54. The Shariah Index (FBM Shariah) also posted losses, down 42.96 points to 11,675.66, while the FTSE4Good Bursa Malaysia Index (F4GBM) declined 2.30 points to 946.74. Despite the cautious undertone, trading activity was led by penny and small-cap counters. Westriver (WESTRVR) topped the most active list, gaining 1 sen to 36.5 sen on brisk volume of 261.6 million shares. SUMI and PERTAMA followed closely, each adding half a sen to 19.5 sen and 13 sen respectively, with over 200 million shares traded apiece. Other heavily traded counters included NEXG, up 0.5 sen to 36.5 sen, and EKOVEST, unchanged at 37.5 sen. Market sentiment remained cautious ahead of key economic data releases and external market cues, with investors largely sidelined amid regional consolidation. Related

title: Bursa Ends On Quiet Note, KLCI Nudges South
body:
Bursa Malaysia ended marginally lower on Thursday as the benchmark FBM KLCI edged down 1.27 points to close at 1,571.75, tracking a mixed regional performance and mild profit-taking after recent gains. The index fluctuated between 1,568.70 and 1,580.06 throughout the day, reflecting cautious investor sentiment ahead of global economic cues. Broader market indices saw steeper declines. Westriver inched up 0.5 sen to 36 sen, and Magma gained 1.5 sen to 41.5 sen. Tanco added 1 sen to close at 94.5 sen on continued retail interest. Trading sentiment was generally mixed as investors awaited signals from upcoming corporate earnings and external macro developments. Related

title: US Stocks Rise On Tariff Truce And Inflation Ease
body:
Wall Street’s main indexes are poised to open higher on Wednesday, buoyed by a strong start to the week. Soft inflation data and a US-China tariff truce have lifted sentiment, while President Donald Trump’s Gulf tour has raised hopes for further trade agreements. US stocks have been optimistic since the weekend when the US and China agreed to pause their tariff dispute, aiming to prevent a global economic slowdown. The US will temporarily reduce extra tariffs on Chinese imports to 30% from 145% for three months, while China will lower duties on US imports to 10% from 125% during the same period. Rick Gardner, chief investment officer at RGA Investments, noted that despite ongoing uncertainties, the easing of trade tensions has positively impacted markets. On Tuesday, the S&P 500 finally returned to positive territory for the year, a milestone not seen since late February, although it remains over 4% below its record peaks. Both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have regained levels last seen before Trump’s April 2 tariff announcement. A 90-day pause for countries other than China, solid earnings reports, and a limited US-UK trade agreement have contributed to the recovery. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed higher on Tuesday after US consumer prices rebounded moderately in April, with headline inflation rising 0.2%, slightly below economists’ expectations. At least three US Federal Reserve officials, including Fed Governor Christopher Waller, are scheduled to speak, with Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s remarks on Thursday being a key focus. As of 08.29 am ET, Dow E-minis were up 80 points, or 0.19%, S&P 500 E-minis were up 16 points, or 0.27%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 79.25 points, or 0.37%. Most megacap and growth stocks rose, with Nvidia leading the charge with a 3% increase. Several US technology firms announced AI deals in the Middle East, and Trump secured US$600 billion in commitments to US companies from Saudi Arabia during his Gulf trip. However, American Eagle Outfitters dropped 12.7% after withdrawing its annual forecasts due to economic uncertainty. As earnings season concludes, Walmart’s results will be closely watched later in the week. Reuters Related
